And they justify this by fabricating claims that the People of the Portico fought him and said:

“We are with Allah; whoever Allah is with, we are with him.”

By this they mean the divine decree and “the reality of the created order,” rather than the divine command and “the reality of religion.” Such arguments are invoked by those among the people who profess poverty who support unbelievers and evildoers and protect them through their hearts, resolve, and inward concentration. Despite this, they believe that they are among Allah’s friends and that they may lawfully depart from the law of Muhammad.

All this is error and falsehood. Even if its adherents practise asceticism and worship, they are to worshippers what their allies among the Tatars and others like them are to soldiers. For “A person follows the religion of his close friend,” and “A person will be with those he loves.” Thus said the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah has made the believers allies of one another and the unbelievers allies of one another.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded that those who pass out of Islam be fought, despite their extensive worship. Concerning them, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Any one of you would consider his prayer insignificant compared with theirs, his fasting compared with theirs, and his recitation compared with theirs. They recite the Quran, but it goes no farther than their throats. They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. Wherever you encounter them, kill them, for whoever kills them will have a reward with Allah on the Day of Resurrection. If I live to encounter them, I will certainly kill them as Ād were killed.”

These were the people whom the Commander of the Faithful, Alī ibn Abī Tālib, fought when they departed from the law of the Messenger of Allah

Similar to this is what some of these fabricators relate: that the People of the Portico heard what Allah said to His Messenger on the night of the Ascension, and that Allah commanded him not to tell anyone about it. and the Ismailis, the Qarmatians, the dualist Bātinīs, the Hākimīs, and others—errors contrary to the religion of Islam. What they attribute to Alī ibn Abī Tālib, Jaʿfar al-Sādiq, or other members of the Prophet’s household—such as al-Bitāqa, al-Haft, al-Jadwal, al-Jafr, Malhamat Ibn Andab, and other such writings—consists of fabricated lies, as all knowledgeable authorities agree. The family of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is connected to him through lineage and kinship, while the righteous friends of Allah, both within his family and outside it, are connected to him through loyalty and adherence to his example. Consequently, many who oppose his religion, his revealed law, and his Sunnah have taken to disguising and embellishing their falsehoods through fabrications attributed to his household and to those loyal to him who follow his example.

Many people also go to excess concerning members of either group, to the point of taking them as gods or giving what is attributed to them precedence over the Prophet’s revealed law and Sunnah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They even contradict the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the consensus of the virtuous early generations, both from his household and from those loyal to him who followed his example. This is widespread among the people of misguidance.

As for ranking the “Ahl al-Suffa (people of the sheltered platform)” above the Ten and others, this is error and misguidance. Rather, the best of this community after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, followed by Umar, as has been reported through mass transmission from the Commander of the Faithful, Alī ibn Abī Tālib, both as his own statement and as reports traced back to the Prophet. This is also established by the Quran and Sunnah and is agreed upon by the community’s early generations and the leading scholars of knowledge and the Sunnah. After them come Uthmān and Alī. The same applies to the other members of the consultative council, such as Talha, al-Zubayr, Saʿd, and Abd al-Rahmān ibn Awf. These men, together with Abū Ubayda ibn al-Jarrāh—the trustworthy one of this community—and Saʿīd ibn Zayd, are the Ten who were promised Paradise.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book:

“Those of you who spent and fought before the victory are not equal to those who did so afterwards. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. Yet Allah has promised them all the finest reward.”

Thus, Allah gave precedence to those who were foremost in striving with their wealth and their lives before the victory at al-Hudaybiyya over those who followed them afterwards. Allah Most High also says:

“Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.”

And He Most High says:

“The earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in excellence—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.”

Thus Allah, glorified is He, was pleased with the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers.

As for His words:

“And keep yourself patiently in the company of those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face.”

This applies generally to everyone who fits this description, such as those who perform the dawn and afternoon prayers in congregation. They call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face, whether they belong to “Ahl al-Suffa” or not. Allah commanded His Prophet to remain patiently with His righteous servants who seek His Face, and not to let his eyes turn away from them in pursuit of the adornment of worldly life. This verse is in al-Kahf, a Meccan surah.

The same applies to the verse in Sūrat al-Anʿām:

“Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face. You bear no responsibility for their reckoning, nor do they bear any responsibility for yours. Were you to drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers.”

It has been reported that these two verses were revealed concerning believers who were oppressed, when the arrogant demanded that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, send them away from his company. Allah forbade him to drive away anyone seeking Allah’s Face, even if he was oppressed, and then commanded him to remain patiently with them. This was before the migration to Medina and before the Suffa (shaded platform) existed. Nevertheless, the verse applies to everyone fitting this description, whether among Ahl al-Suffa or others.

The purpose is that he should remain with the pious believers, who are Allah’s friends, even if they are poor and weak. No one gains higher standing with Allah through his authority and wealth, nor through his lowly status and poverty. Rather, one gains higher standing with Him through faith and righteous deeds. Allah therefore forbade His Prophet to obey those possessing authority and wealth who wanted the weak or poor to be sent away. He commanded him not to drive away those among them who sought His Face, but to remain patiently with them in the congregational gatherings in which he was commanded to join them, such as the dawn and afternoon prayers. He was not to obey the dictates of those who were heedless of Allah’s remembrance and followed their own desires.

As for the purported hadith:

“No group ever gathers without a friend of Allah among them.”

It is a fabrication, found in none of the compendia of Islam. How could it be true, when a group may consist of disbelievers or sinful people who die in that state?

Section

The friends of Allah are “those who believe and are mindful of Him,” as Allah Most High has stated in His Book. They fall into two categories: those who follow a middle course—the people of the right—and the foremost, who are brought near to Allah.

A friend of Allah is the opposite of an enemy of Allah. Allah Most High says:

“Surely Allah’s friends shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve—those who believe and are mindful of Him.”

He also says:

“Your only allies are Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe”—up to His words—“Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies, then surely it is Allah’s party that will prevail.”

And He says:

“Do not take My enemies and yours as allies.”

And He says:

“On the Day when Allah’s enemies are gathered towards the Fire, they will be held in ranks.”

And He says:

“Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, even though they are your enemies?”

Al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘Whoever shows enmity towards a friend of Mine has openly challenged Me to war. My servant draws near to Me through nothing comparable to fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he strikes, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give to him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I have never hesitated over anything I am going to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.’”

translated_text:
The word walī (friend) is derived from walā’ (allegiance), which denotes closeness, just as ‘aduww (enemy) is derived from ‘adw, which denotes distance. Thus, a friend of Allah is someone who allies himself with Him by conforming to what He loves and is pleased with, and draws near to Him through the acts of obedience He has commanded.

In this authentic hadith, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned both categories: those who follow a middle course—the people of the right—who draw near to Allah through obligatory acts; and the foremost, who are brought near to Him, who draw near to Him through voluntary acts in addition to obligatory ones. Allah mentioned these two categories in the surahs Fātir, al-Wāqi‘a, al-Insān, and al-Mutaffifīn. He stated that the drink with which those brought near quench their thirst, drinking it pure, is mixed for the people of the right.

A friend of Allah without qualification is one who dies in that state. But if a person possesses faith and mindfulness of Allah, yet Allah knows that he will turn away from them, is he a friend of Allah while he has faith and mindfulness? Or should it be said that he was never a friend of Allah, because Allah knows his ultimate fate? Scholars hold two views on this.

Likewise, concerning faith followed by disbelief, they ask: is it valid faith that subsequently becomes void, like deeds that are nullified after being fully performed? Or is it invalid faith, like the fast of someone who breaks it before sunset, or the prayer of someone who breaks his state of ritual purity before the concluding salutation? Jurists, theologians, and Sufis likewise hold two views on this.

translated_text:
This disagreement exists among the adherents of the Sunnah and hadith who follow Imam Ahmad and others. It also exists among the followers of Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, and others.

Most followers of Abū Hanīfa, however, do not make a sound final outcome a condition, whereas many followers of Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, and Ahmad do. This is also the position of many theologians among the people of hadith, such as al-Ash‘arī, and among the Shia. Upon this disagreement they base the following questions: Can a friend of Allah become His enemy, and vice versa? Has someone whom Allah loves and is pleased with ever been hated by Him and incurred His wrath, and vice versa? Has someone whom Allah hates and with whom He is wrathful ever been loved by Him and enjoyed His pleasure? These questions are subject to the two views.

The “correct resolution” is to reconcile the two views. Allah’s eternal, beginningless knowledge, and His love, pleasure, hatred, wrath, friendship, and enmity consequent upon it, do not change. Whoever Allah knows will meet death with faith and mindfulness of Him has been the object of Allah’s love, friendship, and pleasure from eternity and forevermore. Likewise, whoever Allah knows will meet death in disbelief has been the object of Allah’s hatred, enmity, and wrath from eternity and forevermore. Nevertheless, Allah Most High hates whatever disbelief and wickedness the former person may have displayed before his death.

It may be said that He hates and detests him on that account, just as He forbids him to do those things. He, glorified and exalted is He, commands the faith and mindfulness of Him that the latter person practised, and He loves and is pleased with what He commands. It may be said that He takes him as a friend at that time on that account.

The evidence for this is the imams’ agreement that whoever was a believer and then apostatized

translated_text:
is not deemed to have had invalid faith initially, as though he had invalidated a prayer, fast, or Hajj before completing it. Rather, one says what Allah Most High has said:

“Whoever rejects faith, his deeds have become worthless.”

He also said:

“If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely become worthless.”

And He said:

“If they had associated others with Allah, all that they used to do would have become worthless.”

If his faith had been invalid in itself, it would necessarily follow that his previous marriages must be judged invalid, the animals he had slaughtered unlawful to eat, his previous receipt of inheritance invalid, and all his acts of worship void. Even if he had performed Hajj on someone else’s behalf, that Hajj would be invalid. If he had led people in prayer for a time and then apostatized, they would have to repeat the prayers they had offered behind him. If he had given testimony or issued a judicial ruling and then apostatized, his testimony and ruling would necessarily be invalidated—and likewise in similar cases.

Similarly, when a disbeliever repents of his disbelief, if he had been loved by Allah and a friend of His while still a disbeliever, it would necessarily follow that the rulings attaching to that disbelief must be deemed inapplicable. All of this contradicts what is established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and scholarly consensus.

The discussion of this “question” parallels the discussion of provision and appointed lifespans. It also rests on the “principle concerning the attributes of action,” which is a major principle.

On this basis, the answer to the questioner becomes clear. For those who hold that a friend of Allah can only be someone who meets Him at death with faith and mindfulness of Him, ascertaining this is more difficult for the person himself and for others. For those who hold that a person who possesses faith and mindfulness of Allah may be His friend even if his ultimate outcome is unknown, ascertaining this is easier.

Even so, this can be known by the friend of Allah himself and by others, though such knowledge is rare, and they may not assert it categorically. As for someone whose friendship with Allah and place among the people of Paradise are established by a scriptural text—such as the Ten and others—the generality of Ahl al-Sunnah affirm for him what the text affirms.

As for someone whose good name is widespread throughout the Muslim community, such that the community unanimously praises him, should the same be affirmed for him? Ahl al-Sunnah differ on this, but the more likely correct view is that it should. This concerns the general rule. As for “certain exceptional individuals,” they may know the ultimate fate of particular people through what Allah has disclosed to them. This, however, is not something everyone is obliged to believe. Many who are thought to have received such disclosure are merely relying on conjecture that is of no avail against the truth.

Those who experience spiritual unveilings and communications are sometimes right and sometimes wrong, just like those who engage in reasoning and inference in matters open to scholarly judgment. They must therefore all hold fast to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and weigh their spiritual experiences, visions, opinions, and rational conclusions against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, rather than relying on these experiences and conclusions alone.

For the foremost of the inspired men in this community, who receive spiritual communications, was Umar ibn al-Khattāb. Yet situations arose in which he was corrected by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or by the Messenger’s friend, who followed him and learned from him, and who was more perfect than the inspired man whose heart spoke to him from his Lord. For this reason, everyone is obliged to follow the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace

This is among the claims of renegades who imagine that some people may stand in relation to the Messenger as al-Khidr did to Moses. Whoever says this is a disbeliever.

Allah Most High has said:

“We never sent any messenger or prophet before you without Satan casting something into his recitation when he recited. But Allah abolishes what Satan casts; then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

Allah has thus guaranteed the messenger and the prophet that He will abolish whatever Satan casts into his recitation, but He has not guaranteed this to the inspired man. Hence the alternative reading recited by Ibn Abbās and others:

“We never sent any messenger, prophet, or inspired man before you without Satan casting something into his recitation when he recited.”

It is possible—and Allah knows best—that this wording was not part of the recited revelation, since He did not guarantee that whatever Satan casts into the inspired man’s recitation would be abolished. Such abolition of what Satan casts is assured only for prophets and messengers, for they are protected against anything Satan casts becoming established in what they convey from Allah Most High. Such protection is not assured for anyone else, even if he is among Allah’s pious friends. Section

As for the “poor” whom Allah mentions in His Book, they fall into two categories: those entitled to charity and those entitled to fayʾ. Regarding those entitled to charity, Allah mentions them in His Book when He says:

“If you give charity openly, that is good; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, that is better for you.”

And He says:

“Alms are only for the poor and the needy.”

When either the term “poor” or the term “needy” appears alone in the Quran—as in His saying, “Its expiation is to feed ten needy people”—the two terms mean the same thing. When they appear together, however, they denote two distinct categories. Both refer to people in need: those who cannot obtain enough to meet their needs, whether by asking others or through work they are capable of doing. Any Muslim in this situation is entitled to receive obligatory charity, charitable endowments, donations pledged by vow, and charitable bequests. Jurists differ over certain subsidiary issues in this matter, as is well known among scholars.

Their opposites are the “wealthy,” for whom receiving charity is forbidden. These, in turn, are

of two kinds: those obliged to pay zakat—although, according to the majority of scholars, zakat may be due from someone who is also permitted to receive it—and those not obliged to pay it.

People in either category may have a surplus beyond their obligatory expenses. These are the ones of whom Allah says:

“They ask you what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever is surplus.’”

They may instead have no surplus. Those whose provision is just sufficient for their subsistence are wealthy insofar as they have no need of others, but poor insofar as they have nothing extra to give in charity.

The poor enter Paradise half a day before the wealthy only because they have no surplus wealth for whose disbursement and expenditure they must account. Anyone without a surplus belongs to this group, even if not eligible to receive zakat. Yet those who possess surplus wealth, if they use it well, may attain a higher rank after entering Paradise than many of the poor who entered before them, just as the wealthy among the prophets and the steadfastly truthful, among the foremost and others, rank above the poor who are below them.

This is why the poor said:

“The wealthy have carried off the rewards.”

And when the wealthy matched them in bodily acts of worship and surpassed them through acts of worship involving wealth, it was said:

“That is the bounty of Allah, which He grants to whom He wills.”

This, then, is what “poor” means in the usage of the Quran and Sunnah.

translated_text:
The poor, like the wealthy, may be among the foremost, among those who follow a middle course, or among those who wrong themselves. Both groups include the steadfastly truthful believer and the hypocritical heretic.

In the terminology of later generations, however, “faqīr” denotes someone journeying towards Allah Most High, as does “Sūfī” in their usage. Some regard the designation “Sūfī” as superior to “faqīr,” because, in their view, it describes someone who fulfills both the inward and outward requirements. Others regard “faqīr” as superior, because, in their view, it describes someone who has severed attachments and whose outward activities are confined to obligatory duties. These are disputes over wording and terminology.

The correct understanding is that the praiseworthy meaning intended by these two terms is already encompassed by such designations as the steadfastly truthful, the friend of Allah, and the righteous, along with similar names found in the Quran and Sunnah. Insofar as someone falls within these prophetic designations, the rulings conveyed by the divine message apply to him.

As for distinctive features which an adherent considers virtues although they are not, or on whose basis he forms bonds of allegiance with others, and similar matters upon which higher standing in religious and worldly affairs is made to depend, these carry no weight in Islamic law. If, however, they are treated as merely permissible pursuits, like crafts, there is no harm in that, provided one does not believe that these permissible things are religiously recommended.

As for whatever accompanies this that is reprehensible in Allah’s religion, including various forms of religious innovation and wickedness, it must be forbidden as Islamic law prescribes.

translated_text:
He was also asked about people who say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to the door of the “people of the Suffa” and asked permission to enter. They asked, “Who are you?” He replied, “I am Muhammad.” They said, “We have no place here for someone who says ‘I.’” He went back, then asked permission a second time, saying, “I am Muhammad, a poor man.” They then allowed him to enter.

Is it permissible to say this, or is it disbelief?

He answered:

This account is among the gravest lies against the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and against the “people of the Suffa.” The “people of the Suffa” had no premises where permission was required to enter. The Suffa was simply a sheltered platform on the northern side of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, where believers who had no family would take shelter. No fixed group lived there; rather, some would leave and others would arrive. The “people of the Suffa” were not the best of the Companions; rather, they were simply among the Companions.

None of the Companions would have treated the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the disrespect described. Anyone who does so is a disbeliever, and anyone who believes this account concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is a disbeliever. He must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is to be put to death. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were they? They also claim that when Allah, glorified and exalted be He, took His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the heavenly ascent, He revealed to him a hundred thousand secrets and commanded him not to disclose them to any human being.

When he descended to earth, he found the people of the Suffa discussing them. He said, “My Lord, I have not disclosed this secret to anyone!” Allah then revealed to him: “They were witnesses between Me and you.” Is any of this authentic?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. All these hadiths are fabricated lies; let their fabricator take his seat in the Fire. All Muslim scholars—those with expert knowledge and others alike—agree that they are lies and inventions, none of which has any basis. Indeed, whoever believes all these hadiths to be authentic is a disbeliever who must be called upon to repent. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death. None of these hadiths has any basis whatsoever. They are not found in any book, nor has anyone who knows Allah and His Messenger ever transmitted them.

As for the first hadith, the statement:

“I am from Allah, and the believers are from me,”

this wording is not known to have been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. However, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAlī:

“You are from me, and I am from you.”

Likewise, Allah, glorified be He, said:

“You are of one another.”

That is, you are of one kind, united in purpose and guidance, like two souls whose attributes correspond. These are the mustered hosts concerning which

translated_text:
the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Souls are mustered hosts: those that recognize one another come together, and those that do not recognize one another are at odds.”

As for the notion that creation is part of the Creator, exalted is He, this is blatant disbelief professed by Allah’s enemies—the Christians, extremists among the Rāfidah, and ignorant Sufis. Whoever believes it is a disbeliever.

Indeed, believers who know Allah and love Him attain stations of nearness and degrees of certainty that words can scarcely encompass, and that none truly knows except those who have reached and experienced them. Yet the Lord remains the Lord, and the servant remains the servant. Nothing of His creation is within His essence, nor is anything of His essence within His creation.

None of those who know Allah believes that the Lord, exalted is He, dwells within him or any other created being, or becomes united with him. If anything of this sort is heard attributed to some of the leading shaykhs, much of it is false, fabricated by the lying antinomian advocates of union with Allah, whom Satan has led astray and joined to the Christian community. What is authentically reported from the shaykhs has sound meanings. Some such utterances come from them when they are overwhelmed by a spiritual state that makes them, for that moment, like an intoxicated person who cannot discern what he is saying. Then, when their reason and discernment return, they repudiate those words and declare anyone who professes them a disbeliever. As for words uttered during the absence of

Rather, no accountability attaches to someone who is asleep, insane, unconscious, or intoxicated through no unlawful cause—for example, someone who is given wine without knowing what it is, has it poured down his throat until he becomes intoxicated, or is fed banj (an intoxicating plant) without knowing what it is. The same applies here.

Many believers may witness tremendous things of Allah’s majesty, greatness, and beauty that come upon tender hearts, causing fainting and unconsciousness. Some may cause death, and some may impair reason. Although this does not befall those among them who have attained perfection, just as it does not befall those below them, it occurs when what comes upon their hearts is powerful and the receiving heart is weak. Whoever is taken in by what they say or do in that state is astray and leads others astray.

“Sound spiritual states” are instead exemplified by what al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who related that his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, said:

“Whoever shows enmity to a close servant of Mine has openly declared war on Me. My servant draws near to Me through nothing like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he strikes, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give to him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I have never hesitated over anything I am going to do as I hesitate over

taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.”

Notice how He says later in the hadith:

“Through Me he hears, and through Me he sees; and if he asks Me, and if he seeks My protection.”

Thus He distinguishes between the Lord and the servant. Do you not hear the words of the Exalted?

“They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.’ But the Messiah said, ‘O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.’ Whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise to him, and his refuge will be the Fire. The wrongdoers will have no helpers.”

He also says:

“There is no god but One God. If they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely afflict those among them who disbelieve.”

Then, further on, He says:

“The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers had passed away before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both ate food.”

He also says:

“O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion, and say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was only Allah’s messenger, His word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him.”

Then, further on, He says:

“Those who disdain to worship Him and are arrogant—He will gather them all to Himself.”

Likewise, Muslim narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah the Exalted says, ‘O son of Adam, I was ill, but you did not visit Me.’ He replies, ‘My Lord, how could I visit You when You are the Lord of all worlds?’ He says, ‘Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was ill? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.’”

translated_text:
“I was ill,” then explains this later in the hadith: “My servant so-and-so was ill. Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.” Thus He distinguishes between the Lord and the servant.

The will of a servant who knows Allah is united with Allah’s will, such that he desires only what Allah commands and approves, loves only what Allah loves, and hates only what Allah hates. He pays no heed to reproach or blame, as Allah, glorified be He, says:

“Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and fearing no blame from any critic.”

Much could be said about the spiritual stations of those who know Allah. The purpose here is simply for the believer to recognize the difference between these heretics—who have imitated the Christians, followed the path of those who profess “divine indwelling and union,” fabricated lies against Allah and His Messenger, and rejected the truth spoken by Allah and His Messenger—and those who know Allah and love Him: His allies, who will have no fear, nor will they grieve.

The two groups may be confused with one another, just as many misguided people confused Musaylimah the Liar, the pretender to prophethood, with Muhammad ibn Abdullāh, the true Messenger of Allah, until they believed the liar and disbelieved the truthful one. Yet Allah has provided signs, indications, and proofs of the truth. Whoever Allah grants no light has no light.

and Abū Bakr,” it is a fabricated lie. Certainly, Abū Bakr al-Siddīq—may Allah be pleased with him—was the closest of all people to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had the strongest claim to his companionship, and understood best what he intended concerning the matters about which people questioned him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would speak in Arabic that the Companions—may Allah be pleased with them—understood, while al-Siddīq would gain an additional understanding that agreed with theirs and went beyond it without contradicting it.

An example is the report in the two Sahīh collections from Abū Saʿīd:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed the people and said, ‘Allah gave a servant a choice between this world and the Hereafter, and that servant chose what is with Allah.’ Abū Bakr wept and said, ‘Rather, we would ransom you with our lives and wealth!’ Some people were astonished and said, ‘How remarkable that this old man should weep because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a servant whom Allah gave a choice between this world and the Hereafter!’”

Abū Saʿīd said, “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the one given the choice, and Abū Bakr understood him better than any of us.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a servant without specifying who he was. This was plain Arabic speech containing no riddle. Because of his profound knowledge of the Prophet’s intentions, al-Siddīq understood that the Prophet himself was the servant given the choice. Knowing that the unspecified servant was this particular person went beyond what the wording itself indicated, but agreed with it and did not contradict it. This is why Abū Saʿīd said, “Abū Bakr understood him better than any of us.”

those who withheld zakat, ʿUmar said to him, “How can you fight the people when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Once they do so, their lives and property are protected from me, except as rightfully required, and their reckoning rests with Allah, Mighty and Majestic’?”

Abū Bakr replied, “Zakat is among those rightful requirements. By Allah, I will certainly fight anyone who distinguishes between prayer and zakat, for zakat is a right due on wealth. It is also reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, and give zakat. Once they do so, their lives and property are protected from me, except as rightfully required by Islam.”

This explicit text agrees with Abū Bakr’s understanding. Likewise, what he said to ʿUmar concerning the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya matched what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had said to him. There are many similar examples.

As for the notion that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke in words that ʿUmar and others like him could not understand, and that sounded to them like the speech of a Zanjī—whoever believes this is ignorant and astray. May Allah inflict upon him what he deserves.

After embracing Islam, many who were not among the “people of the Suffa”—such as Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them—had greater knowledge of Allah and firmer certainty than most of the people of the Suffa.

As for the claim that they stayed behind rather than accompany him in jihad, this is the claim of an ignorant, misguided person. On the contrary, they were among the foremost in fighting and jihad, as Allah describes them in the Quran:

“For the poor emigrants who were driven from their homes and possessions, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful.”

He also describes them as follows:

“For the poor who are confined in Allah’s cause and unable to travel through the land. Those who do not know their circumstances think them wealthy because they refrain from begging. You recognize them by their appearance; they do not beg people persistently.”

Seventy of them were killed in a single day, at Biʾr Maʿūna. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was deeply distressed over them and supplicated in prayer for a month against those who had killed them. He also said of them:

“Through them calamities are warded off and the frontiers are defended. They will be the first people to arrive at the Cistern. Their hair is dishevelled and their clothes soiled; they do not marry women accustomed to luxury, nor are the doors of kings opened to them.”

translated_text:
As for their number, Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī compiled their history: they numbered some six or seven hundred, or thereabouts. They were not all present at the same time. Rather, on the northern side of the mosque there was a sheltered platform—the Suffa—where poor emigrants took refuge. Whoever married, travelled, or went out on a military expedition would leave it. At any one time, there might be seventy there, or fewer or more. Among them were Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqās, one of the Ten, Abū Hurayra, Khubayb, Salmān, and others.

As for the claim that they knew what Allah revealed to His Prophet on the night of the Ascension, it is a lie, and whoever makes it is accursed. How could that be, when the Ascension took place in Mecca before the emigration, whereas the people of the Suffa were only in Medina after the emigration and the construction of the Messenger’s mosque—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in Medina, the Pure?

All this is clear to anyone who knows Allah and His Messenger and is a Muslim devoted to pure monotheism, or who knows the life of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the lives of his Companions alongside him. Only people whose faith is deficient, whose knowledge is scant, and whose souls have grown arrogant fall into such ignorance, until they become like Pharaoh and end up in a worse condition than the Christians.

May Allah accept our repentance and theirs, and that of all our Muslim brothers, and guide us and them to His straight path—the path of those He has blessed, not those who have incurred His wrath, nor those who have gone astray. And Allah Most High knows best.

translated_text:
He was asked:

About the practice conventionally known as “futuwwa” (chivalry) … and so forth.

He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

As for the “futuwwa” he mentioned, in which a man clothes another in trousers and gives him water and salt to drink, this has no basis. None of the early Muslims practised it, neither 'Alī nor anyone else. The chain of transmission they cite for “futuwwa,” tracing it back to the Commander of the Faithful, 'Alī ibn Abī Tālib, through Caliph al-Nāsir and others, is obscure. Most of its transmitters are unknown and unidentifiable, and receive no mention among the scholars.

It has been related that this practice originated when he placed a pair of trousers by 'Alī’s grave, and by morning they were tied shut. Such things also occur in connection with others besides 'Alī, just as similar occurrences thought to be miracles take place in churches and elsewhere. For example, someone suffering from seizures enters a church and recovers through a votive offering made to it, and other such things. If this is not a fabrication, then it is the work of devils, just as similar things are done before idols. I know of numerous incidents of this kind.

translated_text:
The point here is that the trousers associated with futuwwa have no basis in anything transmitted from 'Alī or any other early Muslim. Whatever conditions some of them stipulate, if they concern something commanded by Allah and His Messenger, it should be done because Allah and His Messenger commanded it. Whatever He has forbidden—such as partisan support for one person against another, or assisting in sin and transgression—remains forbidden, even if they make it a condition.

The word fatā means “young man” in Arabic, as the lexicographers explain. Examples include the words of Allah Most High:

“Two young men entered the prison with him.”

“They were young men who believed in their Lord.”

“And when Moses said to his young attendant.”

The verbal forms fatā and yaftā describe being young; a fatā is someone whose youth is evident. Among animals, the aftā are the young, as opposed to the aged. The word fatā may also refer to a slave irrespective of age, as in the words of Allah Most High:

“From among your believing slave women.”

Since a young man is more amenable than an old man, his disposition contains a liberality and generosity not found among the elderly. People therefore came to use the word fatā for someone liberal and generous. One says, “He is a fatā of manifest futuwwa”; also qasada yaftā and yufātā. The plurals are fityān and fitya.

The use of fatā to mean someone endowed with noble character occurs in the words of many spiritual teachers. It may be supposed that the Quranic wording conveys this meaning. Whoever calls people to the noble qualities of character to which Allah and His Messenger have called them is doing good, whether or not he calls this chivalry. Whoever introduces into Allah’s religion something that does not belong to it will have it rejected. Usually, however, they include forbidden practices in chivalry. Is the “brotherhood” that shaykhs establish among the Sufi poor at gatherings for devotional listening and elsewhere permissible at such gatherings and similar occasions? Did the Messenger of Allah—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—establish brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers, or between each Emigrant and a Helper? Did the Messenger of Allah—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—take ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib—may Allah honour his countenance—as his brother or not? Explain this to us with reasons and clear evidence, and provide a thorough, satisfying answer—may you be rewarded. May Allah Most High reward you.

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. As for the aforementioned practice of clothing someone in the garb of “chivalry,” whether trousers or something else, and giving a drink of salt and water, this is invalid and has no basis. Neither the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—nor any of his Companions, neither ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib nor anyone else, nor those who followed them in righteousness, did this.

The chain of transmission they cite, through the caliph al-Nāsir to ʿAbd al-Jabbār to Thumāma, cannot serve as evidence and includes unknown individuals. It is not permissible for a Muslim to attribute to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—through such an obscure chain of transmission

whose transmitters are unknown, anything not known to have come from him. What, then, if he is credited with something known to be a lie and a fabrication against him? Those familiar with his Sunnah and life unanimously agree that this is a lie fabricated against him and against ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib—may Allah be pleased with him. Their claim that this garment descended in a chest is among the most obvious lies, by the agreement of those familiar with his Sunnah.

The “clothing that covers one’s nakedness” means anything that covers the private parts, whatever kind of permissible clothing it may be. Allah Most High revealed this verse because the polytheists used to circumambulate the House naked, saying, “We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we have disobeyed Allah.” So Allah Most High revealed this verse, and He revealed His words:

“Take your adornment at every place of prayer.”

The falsehood here is even more obvious than in the account concerning the wearing of the patched cloak: that the Prophet—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—went into ecstasy until his mantle fell from his outer garment; that he distributed the pieces of cloth among his Companions; that Gabriel came to him and said, “Your Lord asks for His share of the collar of poverty”; and that he hung it from the Throne. This too is a lie, by the agreement of those knowledgeable in the matter.

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and his Companions never gathered to listen to handclapping, frame drums or flutes, or to dance. No garment fell from him on such an occasion, nor did he distribute it among his Companions. Everything narrated to this effect is a fabricated lie, by the agreement of those familiar with his Sunnah.

 مَا كَانَ مِنْهَا مِمَّا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَرَسُولُهُ كَصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَأَدَاءِ الْفَرَائِضِ وَاجْتِنَابِ الْمَحَارِم وَنَصْرِ الْمَظْلُومِ. وَصِلَةِ الْأَرْحَامِ وَالْوَفَاءِ بِالْعَهْدِ.
 أَوْ كَانَتْ مُسْتَحَبَّةً:
 كَالْعَفْوِ عَنْ الظَّالِمِ وَاحْتِمَالِ الْأَذَى وَبَذْلِ الْمَعْرُوفِ الَّذِي يُحِبُّهُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَأَنْ يَجْتَمِعُوا عَلَى السُّنَّةِ وَيُفَارِقَ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ إذَا كَانَ عَلَى بِدْعَةٍ. وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ.
 فَهَذِهِ يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا كُلُّ مُسْلِمٍ سَوَاءٌ شَرَطَهَا شُيُوخُ الْفُتُوَّةِ أَوْ لَمْ يَشْرُطُوهَا وَمَا كَانَ مِنْهَا مِمَّا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَرَسُولُهُ:
 مِثْلُ التَّحَالُفِ الَّذِي يَكُونُ بَيْنَ أَهْلِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ أَنَّ كُلًّا مِنْهُمَا يُصَادِقُ صَدِيقَ الْآخَرِ فِي الْحَقِّ وَالْبَاطِلِ وَيُعَادِي عَدُوَّهُ فِي الْحَقِّ وَالْبَاطِلِ وَيَنْصُرُهُ عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْ يُعَادِيه سَوَاءٌ كَانَ الْحَقُّ مَعَهُ أَوْ كَانَ مَعَ خَصْمِهِ فَهَذِهِ شُرُوطٌ تُحَلِّلُ الْحَرَامَ وَتُحَرِّمُ الْحَلَالَ وَهِيَ شُرُوطٌ لَيْسَتْ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ.
 وَفِي السُّنَنِ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{الْمُسْلِمُونَ عِنْدَ شُرُوطِهِمْ: إلَّا شَرْطًا أَحَلَّ حَرَامًا أَوْ حَرَّمَ حَلَالًا}
 وَكُلُّ مَا كَانَ مِنْ الشُّرُوطِ الَّتِي بَيْنَ الْقَبَائِلِ وَالْمُلُوكِ وَالشُّيُوخِ وَالْأَحْلَافِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّهَا عَلَى هَذَا الْحُكْمِ بِاتِّفَاقِ عُلَمَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَا كَانَ مِنْ الْأَمْرِ الْمَشْرُوطِ الَّذِي قَدْ أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَرَسُولُهُ
translated_text:
Section

Some of the conditions stipulated by the masters of futuwwa (chivalry) concern what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, such as speaking truthfully, fulfilling trusts, performing obligatory duties, avoiding forbidden acts, supporting the oppressed, maintaining ties of kinship and keeping covenants. Others concern recommended acts, such as pardoning a wrongdoer, bearing harm patiently, doing good that Allah and His Messenger love, uniting upon the Sunnah, and parting company with one another if the other follows a religious innovation, and similar matters. Every Muslim believes in these, whether or not the masters of futuwwa stipulate them.

Other conditions concern what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, such as pacts of the kind made by the people of the pre-Islamic age of ignorance: each party befriends the other’s friend in both right and wrong, treats the other’s enemy as his own enemy in both right and wrong, and supports him against anyone who opposes him, whether he or his adversary is in the right. Such conditions make the unlawful lawful and the lawful unlawful. They are conditions that are not in the Book of Allah.

It is reported from the Prophet in the Sunan collections that he said:

“Muslims are bound by their conditions, except a condition that makes the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful.”

All conditions agreed upon among tribes, kings, masters, allies and others are subject to this ruling, by the agreement of Muslim scholars. If the stipulated matter is something that Allah and His Messenger have commanded,

translated_text:
then it is to be enjoined as Allah and His Messenger have commanded. If it is something that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, it is to be prohibited as Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it. People may not enter into covenants, contracts, alliances or stipulations that contravene what Allah and His Messenger have commanded. Rather, each of them must fulfil the contracts and covenants that Allah has enjoined upon mankind, as Allah Most High says:

“Fulfil My covenant, and I will fulfil your covenant.”

The same applies to commitments a person undertakes alone, such as a vow; contracts concluded by two parties, such as sales, leases, gifts and the like; and arrangements that may involve either one party or two, such as endowments and bequests. In all these arrangements, whenever a person stipulates something that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, that stipulation is invalid.

In the Sahīh, it is reported from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him.”

Contracts that contravene what Allah and His Messenger have commanded belong to the religion of the pre-Islamic age of ignorance. They are a branch of the religion of the polytheists and those among the People of the Book who concluded agreements requiring what Allah and His Messenger had forbidden and forbidding what Allah and His Messenger had commanded. This is a grave matter that every Muslim must avoid.

translated_text:
Section

As for the word fatā, its linguistic meaning is “young man,” as in the words of Allah Most High:

“Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord.”

And His words:

“They said, ‘We heard a young man called Abraham mention them.’”

And likewise:

“And when Moses said to his young attendant.”

However, since gentleness is characteristic of the young, many spiritual masters have come to use the term futuwwa (chivalry) to mean noble character. Thus, one of them said: “Our way is to practise chivalry, not to seek victory.” Another said:

[“Futuwwa means drawing near to those who keep you at a distance, honouring those who hurt you, and doing good to those who mistreat you—with generosity, not suppressed anger, and with affection, not malice.”] (*)

Another said: “Futuwwa means abandoning what you desire because of what you fear.”

Similar sayings describe futuwwa in terms of praiseworthy and beloved qualities, whether or not these are called futuwwa. These qualities merit praise in the Quran and Sunnah only because they fall within the terms that Allah and His Messenger have praised, such as doing good, mercy, pardon, overlooking faults, forbearance, restraining anger, righteousness, charity, zakāh and goodness, and other commendable terms encompassing these meanings.

Whenever Allah associates a term with praise and reward in the Quran and Sunnah, those who possess the quality it denotes are praiseworthy. Whenever He associates a term with blame and punishment in the Quran and Sunnah, those who possess the quality it denotes are blameworthy, as with lying and betrayal

As for the term “zaʿīm,” it is synonymous with kafīl, qabīl and damīn, meaning a guarantor. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever brings it shall have a camel-load, and I guarantee it.”

Anyone who undertakes responsibility for the affairs of a group is called its zaʿīm. If what he undertakes is good, he is praised for it; if it is evil, he is blamed for it.

As for the “head of a group,” this means the leader of people who band together to form a group. If they unite upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, without adding or omitting anything, they are believers, with the rights and obligations that this entails. But if they have added to this or omitted from it—for example, by siding with those who join their group, whether they are right or wrong, and turning away from those who do not join it, whether they are right or wrong—this is part of the division condemned by Allah Most High and His Messenger. Allah and His Messenger have commanded unity and harmony and forbidden division and discord. They have commanded cooperation in righteousness and piety and forbidden cooperation in sin and transgression.

It is reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“The believers, in their mutual love, mercy and compassion, are like a single body: when one part suffers, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness.”

It is also reported in the two Sahīh collections that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“One believer is to another like a building whose parts support one another.”

And he interlaced

his fingers.

It is reported in a Sahīh collection that he said:

“A Muslim is the brother of another Muslim: he neither abandons him to harm nor fails to support him.”

It is also reported in a Sahīh collection that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or is oppressed.” He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, I can help him when he is oppressed, but how can I help him when he is an oppressor?” He replied, “Prevent him from committing oppression; that is how you help him.”

It is reported in a Sahīh collection that he said:

“A Muslim owes another Muslim five duties: to greet him when he meets him, visit him when he is ill, invoke Allah’s mercy upon him when he sneezes, accept his invitation, and accompany his funeral procession when he dies.”

It is also reported in a Sahīh collection that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“By Him in Whose hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother the good that he loves for himself.”

These hadiths and others like them convey what Allah and His Messenger have commanded concerning the rights that believers owe one another.

It is reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Do not sever ties with one another, turn your backs on one another, hate one another, or envy one another. Be brothers, O servants of Allah.”

It is also reported in the two Sahīh collections that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Allah is pleased with three things for you: that you worship Him without associating anything with Him; that you all hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not become divided; and that you offer sincere counsel to those whom Allah has placed in authority over you.”

It is reported in the Sunan collections that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Shall I tell you of something higher in rank than prayer, fasting, charity, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong?”

They replied, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”

As for the term “daskara” (gathering place), it is not a term established in Islamic law to which praise or blame attaches. Rather, in common usage it denotes places of gathering. Thus, the account of Heraclius mentions that he assembled the Byzantines in a daskara, and people gathered to drink wine are said to be in a daskara. The term itself therefore entails neither praise nor blame, though it tends more towards blame, since people most commonly use it for gatherings involving indecency, wine, and singing.

Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong are obligatory upon every Muslim, but they are collective obligations. If enough people—whether those in authority or others—undertake these duties to discharge the obligation, what is most incumbent upon the rest is to do what they can in this regard.

“Allah created the angels from light, created Iblīs from a flame of fire, and created Adam from what has been described to you.”

The superiority of some created beings over others is not determined solely by what they were created from. A believer may be born to a disbeliever, and a disbeliever to a believer, as Noah’s son was born to him, and Abraham to Āzar.

Allah created Adam from clay. Once He had fashioned him, breathed into him of His spirit, caused the angels to prostrate before him, and favoured him above them by teaching him the names of all things, by creating him with His two hands, and in other ways, Adam and his righteous descendants are superior to the angels, even though the former were created from clay and the latter from light. This is a “major question,” discussed at length elsewhere. The superiority of Adam’s descendants rests upon reasons whose explanation would be lengthy here.

Their superiority will only become apparent when they enter the everlasting abode:

“And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, ‘Peace be upon you for your patient endurance. How excellent is the final home!’”

The human being is created from a drop of sperm, then from a lump of flesh, then from a clinging clot. He then passes from childhood to adulthood, and from one abode to another. His superiority does not become apparent in his initial stages, but only when he reaches his perfected state—unlike the angel, whose beginning and end are alike. This is where those who held the angels to be superior to the prophets erred: they considered the prophets’ condition while they were still passing through these stages, before attaining the ultimate perfection promised to them in the Hereafter.

translated_text:
Our Prophet’s superiority over the angels became apparent on the night of the Ascension, when he reached a level where the scratching of the pens could be heard and rose above the stations of the angels. Through righteous human beings—the prophets and Allah’s devoted servants—Allah Most High has manifested aspects of His immense power and wondrous wisdom the like of which He has not manifested through the angels, for He brought together in them what is dispersed among created beings.

He created the human body from the earth and the human spirit from the highest assembly. Hence it is said: “The human being is the microcosm, a counterpart of the macrocosm.” Muhammad is the master of the children of Adam, the best of creation and the most honoured by Allah. This is why some have said that Allah created the world for his sake, or that, were it not for him, He would not have created any Throne or Footstool, heaven or earth, sun or moon.

But this is not a hadith from the Prophet (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace), whether authentic or weak. No scholar of hadith has transmitted it from the Prophet (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace), nor is it even known to have come from the Companions. Rather, it is a statement whose author is unknown. It can, however, be interpreted in a sound sense, along the lines of His words:

“He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.”

And His words:

“And He has subjected ships to you, sailing through the sea by His command, and has subjected rivers to you. He has subjected the sun and the moon to you, both pursuing their courses, and has subjected the night and the day to you. He has given you of all that you have asked Him. If you were to count Allah’s blessings, you could never enumerate them.”

There are other such verses in which He explains that He created these things for the children of Adam. It is well known that Allah has other great and wise purposes in creating them,

and purposes greater still. Yet He explains to the children of Adam the benefits these things hold for them and the blessings He has lavished upon them.

Thus, saying, “He did this for that purpose,” does not imply that there is no other wise purpose behind it. Likewise, saying, “Were it not for this, that would not have been created,” does not imply that there are no other great and wise purposes behind it. Rather, if Muhammad is the best of the righteous descendants of Adam, and his creation is a desired end and an intended purpose of consummate wisdom greater than that of others, then it follows that creation attained its completion and the pinnacle of perfection through Muhammad (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace).

Allah created the heavens, the earth and everything between them in six days. Creation was completed on Friday, when Adam was created. He was the last to be created, being created on Friday after the afternoon prayer, at the end of Friday. The master of Adam’s descendants is Muhammad (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace); Adam and all those below him are under his banner. He (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Indeed, I was recorded with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets while Adam was still lying in his clay.”

That is, my prophethood was recorded and made known when Adam was created, before the spirit was breathed into him, just as Allah records a servant’s provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed when the fetus is created, before the spirit is breathed into it.

Thus, if the human being is the culmination of created beings and the last of them

and encompasses all that they contain, and the finest human being is the finest of all created beings without exception, and Muhammad is the pupil of this eye, the pivot of this mill, and the constituent parts of this whole, then this would seem to be the ultimate end among created things. What objection, then, can there be to saying that they were all created for his sake, and that, were it not for him, they would not have been created? If these and similar words are interpreted in accordance with what the Quran and Sunnah indicate, they are acceptable. But if they involve excess like that of the Christians, by allowing created beings a share in any aspect of lordship, then they are rejected and unacceptable. It is authentically reported that he (may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace) said:

“Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised Jesus son of Mary. I am only a servant, so say: ‘The servant of Allah and His Messenger.’”

Allah Most High has said:

“O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion, and say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only the Messenger of Allah, His word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, ‘Three.’ Desist—it is better for you. Allah is only one God.”

Allah has reserved for Himself a right in which no created being shares. Worship is due to Him alone; supplication is to be addressed to Him alone; reliance is to be placed upon Him alone; longing is to be directed to Him alone; and fear is to be of Him alone. There is no refuge or escape from Him except with Him. None but He brings good, and none but He removes evil. There is neither power nor strength except through Him.

“Intercession is of no avail with Him except for those to whom He grants permission.”

“Who is it that

can intercede with Him except by His permission?”

“There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant.”

“He has counted them and numbered them precisely.”

“And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah and is mindful of Him—it is they who will triumph.”

Thus, He enjoins obedience to Allah and the Messenger, while reserving reverent fear and mindfulness for Allah alone. Likewise, He says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah alone we turn in hope.’”

Giving is thus attributed to Allah and the Messenger, whereas reliance is upon Allah alone, and hope is directed to Allah alone.

Section

As for “bonds of brotherhood,” the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) established such bonds between the Emigrants and the Helpers when he arrived in Medina. He paired Salmān al-Fārisī with Abū al-Dardā’, and ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn ‘Awf with Sa‘d ibn al-Rabī‘. They used to inherit from one another by virtue of those bonds until Allah Most High revealed:

“But blood relatives have a greater claim upon one another in the Book of Allah.”

Thereafter, they inherited from one another on the basis of kinship.

Concerning this, Allah Most High revealed:

“And those with whom you have sworn a pact—give them their share.”

This is an alliance by covenant. Scholars differed over whether inheritance through such a bond, in the absence of kinship or ties of manumission, remains in force or has been abrogated. There are two views:

Hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother the good he loves for himself,” and other such rights arising from faith that one believer owes another—then these rights are obligatory by virtue of faith itself. Committing oneself to them is like committing oneself to prayer, zakah, fasting, and Hajj; making a covenant to uphold them is like making a covenant to fulfil what Allah and His Messenger have made obligatory. Every believer owes these rights to every other believer, even if they have not entered into a pact of brotherhood.

If, however, the intention is to establish a particular legal effect, as existed between the Emigrants and the Helpers, then the scholars hold two positions, depending on whether that arrangement has been abrogated. Those who hold that it has been abrogated—such as Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad according to the better-known report from him—say that this is not religiously prescribed. Those who hold that it has not been abrogated—such as Abū Hanīfah and Ahmad according to the other report—say that it is religiously prescribed.

As for the “conditions” to which many people commit themselves in “samāʿ” (listening sessions) and elsewhere, such as saying, “On condition that we share in good deeds, and whichever of us is saved on the Day of Resurrection, his companion will also be saved,” and similar statements, these are all invalid conditions. For on that Day the earth belongs to Allah. It is:

“The Day when no soul will have any power to help another.”

And, as the Most High says:

“You have certainly come to Us individually, just as We created you the first time, leaving behind all that We had bestowed upon you. We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed to be Allah’s partners in your affairs. The bonds between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has deserted you.”

Likewise, they stipulate conditions concerning worldly matters but do not fulfil them.

 فَقَالُوا: عَدِيُّ بْنُ مُسَافِرِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مُوسَى بْنِ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ أَحْمَد بْنِ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ الْأُمَوِيِّ. وَهَذَا كَذِبٌ قَطْعًا فَإِنَّهُ يَمْتَنِعُ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ خَمْسَةُ أَنْفُسٍ. وَأَمَّا 
" الْخِرْقَةُ "
 فَقَالُوا: دَخَلَ عَلَى الشَّيْخِ الْعَارِفِ عُقَيْلٍ المنبجي وَأَلْبَسَهُ الْخِرْقَةَ بِيَدِهِ وَالشَّيْخُ عُقَيْلٌ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ مسلمة المردجي وَالشَّيْخُ مسلمة لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخَرَّازِ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—also said:

Section

Shaykh ʿAdī ibn Musāfir ibn Sakhr was a righteous man and had righteous followers. Among his associates, however, were some whose extreme excesses led them into grievous disbelief. I have seen a booklet brought by his followers containing his genealogy and the chain of transmission of his spiritual path, and I found both inconsistent.

As for his genealogy, they said: “ʿAdī ibn Musāfir ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Mūsā ibn Marwān ibn Ahmad ibn Marwān ibn al-Hakam ibn Marwān al-Umawī.” This is unquestionably false, for it is impossible that only five people should separate him from Marwān ibn al-Hakam.

As for the cloak of initiation, they said: “He visited the spiritually knowledgeable shaykh ʿUqayl al-Manbijī, who personally invested him with the cloak. Shaykh ʿUqayl received the cloak from Shaykh Maslama al-Mardajī, and Shaykh Maslama received it from Shaykh Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz.”

original_text:
قُلْت:
 هَذَا كَذِبٌ وَاضِحٌ فَإِنَّ مسلمة لَمْ يُدْرِكْ أَبَا سَعِيدٍ بَلْ بَيْنَهُمَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مِائَةٍ سَنَةٍ بَلْ قَرِيبًا مِنْ مِائَتَيْ سَنَةٍ.
 ثُمَّ قَالُوا:
 وَالشَّيْخُ أَبُو سَعِيدٍ الْخَرَّازُ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ الْعَنْسِيَّ والعنسي لَبِسَهَا مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَلِيلٍ الرَّمْلِيِّ وَالشَّيْخُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَلِيلٍ لَبِسَهَا مِنْ يَدِ وَالِدِهِ الشَّيْخِ عَلِيلٍ الرَّمْلِيِّ وَالشَّيْخُ عَلِيلٌ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ عَمَّارٍ السَّعْدِيِّ وَالشَّيْخُ عَمَّارٌ السَّعْدِيُّ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ الشَّيْخِ يُوسُفَ الْغَسَّانِيِّ وَالشَّيْخُ يُوسُفُ الْغَسَّانِيُّ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ وَالِدِهِ الشَّيْخِ يَعْقُوبَ الْغَسَّانِيِّ وَالشَّيْخُ يَعْقُوبُ الْغَسَّانِيُّ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ يَوْمَ خَطَبَ النَّاسَ بِالْجَابِيَةِ وَعُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَبِسَ الْخِرْقَةَ مِنْ يَدِ جبرائيل وجبرائيل مِنْ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى.
 قُلْت:
 لُبْسُ عُمَرَ لِلْخِرْقَةِ وَإِلْبَاسُهُ وَلُبْسُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِلْخِرْقَةِ وَإِلْبَاسُهُ يَعْرِفُ كُلُّ مَنْ لَهُ أَدْنَى مَعْرِفَةٍ أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ. وَأَمَّا الْإِسْنَادُ الْمَذْكُورُ مَا بَيْنَ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ إلَى عُمَرَ فَمَجْهُولٌ وَمَا أَعْرِفُ لِهَؤُلَاءِ ذِكْرًا لَا فِي كُتُبِ الزُّهْدِ وَالرَّقَائِقِ وَلَا فِي كُتُبِ الْحَدِيثِ وَالْعِلْمِ وَمِنْ الْمُمْكِنِ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَعْضُ هَؤُلَاءِ كَانُوا شُيُوخًا وَقَدْ رَكَّبَ هَذَا الْإِسْنَادَ عَلَيْهِمْ مَنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ أَزْمَانَهُمْ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِحَقِيقَةِ أَمْرِهِمْ.
translated_text:
I say:

This is an obvious lie, for Maslama did not live in Abū Saʿīd’s time. Indeed, more than a hundred years separated them—nearly two hundred, in fact.

They then said:

“Shaykh Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz received the cloak from Shaykh Abū Muhammad al-ʿAnsī, and al-ʿAnsī received it from Shaykh ʿAlī ibn ʿAlīl al-Ramlī. Shaykh ʿAlī ibn ʿAlīl received it from his father, Shaykh ʿAlīl al-Ramlī, and Shaykh ʿAlīl received the cloak from Shaykh ʿAmmār al-Saʿdī. Shaykh ʿAmmār al-Saʿdī received the cloak from Shaykh Yūsuf al-Ghassānī, and Shaykh Yūsuf al-Ghassānī received it from his father, Shaykh Yaʿqūb al-Ghassānī. Shaykh Yaʿqūb al-Ghassānī received the cloak from the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, on the day he addressed the people at al-Jābiya. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb received the cloak from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, received the cloak from Gabriel, and Gabriel received it from Allah Most High.”

I say:

Anyone with even the slightest knowledge knows that the claims that ʿUmar wore the cloak and invested others with it, and that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wore it and invested others with it, are false. As for the chain mentioned between Abū Saʿīd and ʿUmar, it is unknown. I know of no mention of these men in books on asceticism and spiritual exhortation, nor in books of hadith and learning. It is possible that some of them were shaykhs, and that someone who did not know when they lived fabricated this chain and attributed it to them. Allah knows best the truth about them.

original_text:
ثُمَّ ذَكَرُوا بَعْدَ هَذَا 
" عَقِيدَتَهُ "
 وَقَالُوا: هَذِهِ عَقِيدَةُ السُّنَّةِ مِنْ إمْلَاءِ الشَّيْخِ عَدِيٍّ. وَ " الْعَقِيدَةُ مِنْ (كِتَابِ التَّبْصِرَةِ لِلشَّيْخِ أَبِي الْفَرَجِ المقدسي. بِأَلْفَاظِهِ نَقْلَ الْمِسْطَرَةِ لَكِنْ حَذَفُوا مِنْهَا تَسْمِيَةَ الْمُخَالِفِينَ وَأَقْوَالَهُمْ وَذَكَرُوا مَا ذَكَرَهُ مِنْ الْأَدِلَّةِ وَزَادُوا فِيهَا مِنْ ذِكْرِ يَزِيدَ وَغَيْرِهِ أَشْيَاءَ لَمْ يَقُلْهَا الشَّيْخُ أَبُو الْفَرَجِ وَفِيهَا أَحَادِيثُ مَوْضُوعَةٌ وَقَالَ فِي آخِرِهَا فَهَذَا اعْتِقَادُنَا وَمَا نَقَلْنَاهُ عَنْ مَشَايِخِنَا نَقَلَهُ جبرائيل عَنْ اللَّهِ وَنَقَلَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ جبرائيل وَنَقَلَهُ الصَّحَابَةُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَسُمِّيَ مَنْ سَمَّاهُ اللكائي فِي أَوَّلِ كِتَابِ (شَرْحِ أُصُولِ السُّنَّةِ كَمَا ذَكَرُوا أَنَّ هَذَا أَمْلَاهُ الشَّيْخُ عَدِيٌّ مِنْ حِفْظِهِ. وَأَمَرَ بِكِتَابَتِهِ وَرَوَوْا ذَلِكَ بِالسَّمَاعِ مِنْ الشَّيْخِ حَسَنِ بْنِ عَدِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي الْبَرَكَاتِ بِسَمَاعِهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ عَدِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي الْبَرَكَاتِ بْنِ صَخْرِ بْنِ مُسَافِرٍ وَهُوَ عَدِيٌّ.
translated_text:
They then set out “his creed,” saying: “This is the creed of the Sunnah, dictated by Shaykh ʿAdī.” This “creed” is copied word for word from Kitāb al-Tabsira by Shaykh Abū al-Faraj al-Maqdisī. However, they omitted the names of those who held opposing views and their statements, while retaining the evidence he cited. They also added statements concerning Yazīd and others that Shaykh Abū al-Faraj never made. It also contains fabricated hadiths.

At its conclusion he says:

“This, then, is our creed. What we have transmitted from our shaykhs was transmitted by Gabriel from Allah, by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from Gabriel, and by the Companions from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

The same people whom al-Lālakā’ī named at the beginning of his book Sharh Usūl al-Sunnah are named here. They also claimed that Shaykh ʿAdī dictated this from memory and ordered it to be written down. They transmitted it as something heard directly from Shaykh Hasan ibn ʿAdī ibn Abī al-Barakāt, who had heard it from his father, ʿAdī ibn Abī al-Barakāt ibn Sakhr ibn Musāfir, who is ʿAdī.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
هَلْ تَخَلَّلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ بِالْعَبَاءَةِ؟ وَتَخَلَّلَتْ الْمَلَائِكَةُ لِأَجْلِهِ بِالْعَبَاءَةِ أَمْ لَا؟ ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَمْ يَتَخَلَّلْ أَبُو بَكْرٍ بِالْعَبَاءَةِ وَلَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ تَخَلَّلُوا بِالْعَبَاءَةِ وَذَلِكَ كَذِبٌ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

“Did Abū Bakr fasten a cloak around himself, and did the angels do likewise for his sake, or not?”

He replied:

“Praise be to Allah. Abū Bakr did not fasten a cloak around himself, nor did the angels do so. That is a lie. And Allah knows best.”

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ مَعْنَى قَوْلِ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 
" حُبُّ الدُّنْيَا رَأْسُ كُلِّ خَطِيئَةٍ "
 فَهَلْ هِيَ مِنْ جِهَةِ الْمَعَاصِي؟ أَوْ مِنْ جِهَةِ جَمْعِ الْمَالِ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
لَيْسَ هَذَا مَحْفُوظًا عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَلَكِنْ هُوَ مَعْرُوفٌ عَنْ جُنْدُبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ البجلي مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ وَيُذْكَرُ عَنْ الْمَسِيحِ ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَأَكْثَرُ مَا يَغْلُو فِي هَذَا اللَّفْظِ الْمُتَفَلْسِفَةُ وَمَنْ حَذَا حَذْوَهُمْ مِنْ الصُّوفِيَّةِ عَلَى أَصْلِهِمْ فِي تَعَلُّقِ النَّفْسِ إلَى أُمُورٍ لَيْسَ هَذَا مَوْضِعَ بَسْطِهَا.
 وَأَمَّا حُكْمُ الْإِسْلَامِ فِي ذَلِكَ:

{إيَّاكُمْ وَالشُّحَّ فَإِنَّ الشُّحَّ أَهْلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ أَمَرَهُمْ بِالْبُخْلِ فَبَخِلُوا وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِالظُّلْمِ فَظَلَمُوا وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِالْقَطِيعَةِ فَقَطَعُوا}
 وَعَنْ كَعْبٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: {مَا ذِئْبَانِ جَائِعَانِ أُرْسِلَا فِي غَنَمٍ
translated_text:
He was also asked:

“What is meant by the saying, ‘Love of this world is the root of every sin’? Does it refer to sins or to amassing wealth?”

He replied:

This is not reliably transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. However, it is known as a saying of Jundub ibn ‘Abd Allāh al-Bajalī, one of the Companions, and is also attributed to the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Those who exaggerate most concerning this saying are the philosophizers and those Sufis who follow their lead, drawing on their doctrine concerning the soul’s attachment to matters that this is not the place to discuss at length.

As for the Islamic ruling on this matter, the love for which a person is punished is that which entails acts of disobedience, leading to injustice, lying, and indecency. There is no doubt that greed for wealth and leadership brings this about, as stated in the two Sahīh collections, where he said:

“Beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those before you. It commanded them to be stingy, and they were stingy; it commanded them to commit injustice, and they committed injustice; and it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them.”

Ka‘b narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Two hungry wolves let loose among a flock of sheep

are no more destructive to it than a man’s eagerness for wealth and status is to his religion.” Al-Tirmidhī said: “This is a sound hadith.”

Thus, a man’s eagerness for wealth and status corrupts his religion. As for mere love residing in the heart, if a person does what Allah has commanded, refrains from what He has forbidden, fears standing before his Lord, and restrains himself from desire, Allah does not punish him for such love when it is not accompanied by action. Nor is he punished for accumulating wealth if he fulfils the obligations attached to it and does not acquire it through unlawful means. Nevertheless, giving away surplus wealth and contenting oneself with what suffices is better and safer: it leaves the heart freer, focuses one’s concerns, and is more beneficial in this world and the Hereafter.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever begins the day with this world as his greatest concern, Allah will throw his affairs into disarray, place his poverty before his eyes, and nothing of this world will come to him except what has been decreed for him. But whoever begins the day with the Hereafter as his greatest concern, Allah will place richness in his heart, set his affairs in order, and this world will come to him despite itself.”

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَمَّا يُذْكَرُ مِنْ قَوْلِهِمْ:
 اتَّخِذُوا مَعَ الْفَقِيرِ أَيَادِي فَإِنَّ لَهُمْ دَوْلَةً وَأَيَّ دَوْلَةٍ وَقَوْلُ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ -: إنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَكُنْت بَيْنَهُمَا كَالزِّنْجِيِّ مَا مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ؟
 وَقَوْلُ بَعْضِ النَّاسِ لِبَعْضِ:

فَأَجَابَ:
