translated_text:
enmity is hatred and distance.

It has also been said that an ally is called a walī because he performs acts of obedience in succession. The first explanation, however, is more correct. A walī is someone near; thus one says, “This yalī that,” meaning that it is near it. This is also the sense of the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Give the prescribed shares of inheritance to those entitled to them, and whatever remains is for the nearest male relative.”

That is, the man most closely related to the deceased. He emphasized this by specifying “male,” to make clear that this ruling applies exclusively to males, rather than equally to males and females. Similarly, he said concerning zakat:

“Then a male camel in its third year.”

Since an ally of Allah is someone who concurs with Him and follows Him concerning what He loves and is pleased with, what He hates and is displeased with, and what He commands and forbids, whoever shows enmity to His ally shows enmity to Him. As Allah Most High says:

“Do not take My enemies and yours as allies, offering them affection.”

Whoever shows enmity to Allah’s allies has thus shown enmity to Him, and whoever shows enmity to Him has waged war against Him. For this reason, He said:

“Whoever shows enmity to an ally of Mine has openly waged war against Me.”

The best of Allah’s allies are His prophets; the best of His prophets are those who are messengers; and the best of the messengers are those of firm resolve: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah Most High says:

“He has ordained for you the same religion He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: uphold the religion and do not become divided in it.”

Allah Most High also says:

“And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of

Mary—and We took from them a solemn covenant—so that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared a painful punishment for the disbelievers.”

The best of those of firm resolve is Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: the Seal of the Prophets, the leader of the God-fearing, the foremost of Adam’s descendants, the leader of the prophets when they gather, and their spokesman when they arrive as a delegation. His is the Praiseworthy Station, which the first and last will wish to share. He is the bearer of the Banner of Praise, the possessor of the Pool to which people will come, the intercessor for creation on the Day of Resurrection, and the one granted al-Wasīlah and al-Fadīlah. Allah sent him with the best of His Books, prescribed for him the best of His religious laws, and made his community the best community ever raised for mankind. He brought together for him and his community virtues and merits that He had distributed among those before them. They are the last community to be created and the first to be resurrected, as he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“We are the last, but we shall be the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, although they were given the Scripture before us and we were given it after them. This was their day over which they differed—meaning Friday—and Allah guided us to it. The people follow us in this: tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow for the Christians.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“I will be the first for whom the earth splits open.”

And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I will come to the gate of Paradise and ask for it to be opened. The keeper will say, ‘Who are you?’ I will reply, ‘I am Muhammad.’ He will say, ‘I was commanded concerning you not to open it for anyone before you.’”

The virtues of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and of his community are many. From the time Allah sent him, He made him the criterion distinguishing His allies from His enemies. No one can be an ally of Allah unless he believes in the Prophet and what he brought, and follows him inwardly and outwardly. Whoever claims to love Allah and to be His ally without following the Prophet is not among Allah’s allies. Rather, whoever opposes him is among Allah’s enemies and Satan’s allies. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.’”

Al-Hasan al-Basrī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “Some people claimed to love Allah, so Allah revealed this verse as a test for them.” Allah has made clear in this verse that He loves whoever follows the Messenger. Whoever claims to love Allah but does not follow the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is not among Allah’s allies—even though many people consider themselves or others to be Allah’s allies when they are not. The Jews and Christians claim to be Allah’s allies and His beloved ones. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings among those He has created.’”

And the verse continues. Allah Most High also says:

“They say, ‘None will enter Paradise unless he is a Jew or a Christian.’ Those are their wishful hopes,”

up to His words:

“nor will they grieve.”

The Arab polytheists used to claim that they were Allah’s own people because they lived in Mecca and dwelt beside the House. On that account, they arrogantly considered themselves superior to others, as Allah Most High says:

“My verses were recited to you, but you would turn back on your heels, arrogant on account of it, speaking abusively in your nightly gatherings.”

Allah Most High also says:

“And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you,”

up to His words:

“while they bar people from the Sacred Mosque

though they are not its guardians. Its guardians are only the God-fearing.” Thus, He, glorified be He, has made clear that the polytheists are neither His allies nor the guardians of His House. His allies are only the God-fearing.

It is established in the two Sahīh collections that ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀs, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say openly, not in secret:

“The family of so-and-so are not my allies”—meaning a group of his relatives—“my allies are only Allah and the righteous believers.”

This accords with His words, Most High:

“Allah is his Protector, as are Gabriel and the righteous believers.”

And the verse continues. “The righteous believers” means those believers who are righteous: the God-fearing believers who are Allah’s allies. They include Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and all the others who took the Pledge of Divine Pleasure beneath the tree. They numbered one thousand four hundred, and all of them will be in Paradise, as is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one who pledged allegiance beneath the tree will enter the Fire.”

Another hadith conveys a similar meaning:

“My allies are the God-fearing, whoever they may be and wherever they may be.”

Just as some disbelievers claim to be allies of Allah when they are not His allies but His enemies, so too there are hypocrites who outwardly profess Islam. They outwardly affirm the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that he was sent to all mankind—indeed, to both mankind and jinn—yet inwardly believe

“Ahl al-Suffa” were not a fixed group of people who remained permanently at the portico. Rather, their numbers sometimes decreased and sometimes increased; a man might stay there for a time and then move elsewhere. Those who lodged there were like other Muslims, with no special distinction in knowledge or piety. Indeed, among them were some who apostatized from Islam and whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, put to death, such as the men of ʿUrayna. They found Medina disagreeable—that is, unhealthy—so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arranged for them to have milch camels—that is, camels giving milk—and instructed them to drink their urine and milk. When they recovered, they killed the herdsman and drove off the camels. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent men in pursuit of them, and they were brought back. He ordered their hands and feet to be cut off, their eyes were seared, and he left them on the lava field, where they asked for water but were given none. Their account is related in both Sahīh collections through Anas, and it mentions that they stayed at the portico.

Thus, people like these lodged there, but so did some of the finest Muslims, including Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqās, who was the best of those who stayed at the portico and later moved away. Abū Hurayra and others also stayed there. Abū ʿAbd al-Rahmān al-Sulamī compiled a history of those who stayed at the portico.

As for the “Helpers,” they were not among Ahl al-Suffa. Nor were the leading Emigrants, such as Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Talha, al-Zubayr, and ʿAbd al-Rahmān

ibn Abī Tālib was closer to the truth than Mu'āwiya and his companions. How, then, could the abdāl be in the inferior of the two armies rather than the superior one?

Likewise, some people relate concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“A reciter recited to him:
‘The serpent of passion has stung my heart;
It has no physician, no healer with incantations,
Except the beloved who has enthralled me:
With him lie my healing incantation and antidote.’

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went into ecstasy until his mantle fell from his shoulder.”

This is a lie by the agreement of the scholars of hadith. Even more false is what some of them relate:

“He tore his garment, and Gabriel took a piece of it and hung it upon the Throne.”

Those with knowledge of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recognize this and similar reports as among the most blatant lies attributed to him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Likewise, they relate that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abū Bakr would converse, while I sat between them like a black African.”

This is a fabricated lie by the agreement of the scholars of hadith.

The point here is that among those who outwardly acknowledge that his message is universal are some who inwardly believe things that contradict this. Such a person is therefore a hypocrite, yet he claims of himself and others like him

that they are friends of Allah, despite inwardly disbelieving in what the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought, whether out of obstinacy or ignorance. Likewise, many Christians and Jews believe that they are friends of Allah and that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger, but say, “He was sent only to those other than the People of the Book, and we are not obliged to follow him, because He sent messengers to us before him.” All these people are disbelievers, despite regarding their own group as friends of Allah. The friends of Allah are only those whom Allah Most High described as such when He said:

“Indeed, the friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve.”

“Those who believe and fear Him.”

Faith necessarily entails believing in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and believing in every messenger Allah sent and every book Allah revealed. As Allah Most High said:

“Say, ‘We believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what Moses and Jesus were given, and what the prophets were given by their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.’”

“So if they believe in what you believe, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension. Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”

Allah Most High also said:

“The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers: ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers.’”

And so on to the end of the surah.

He said at the beginning of the surah:

“Alif, Lām, Mīm.”

“This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guide for those who fear Allah.”

“who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them.”

“And who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and are certain of the Hereafter.”

“Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.”

Faith necessarily entails believing that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the Seal of the Prophets, that there is no prophet after him, and that Allah sent him to all jinn and humankind. Whoever does not believe in what he brought is not a believer, let alone one of Allah’s friends who fear Him. Whoever believes in some of what he brought but disbelieves in some is a disbeliever, not a believer, as Allah Most High said:

“Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and wish to take a path in between—”

“Those are truly the disbelievers. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.”

“But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—He will give them their rewards. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Believing in him includes believing that he is the intermediary between Allah and His creation in conveying His commands and prohibitions, His promises and warnings, and what He permits and forbids. What is lawful is what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful; what is unlawful is what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden; and religion is what Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have prescribed. Whoever believes that any of Allah’s friends has a path to Allah without following Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is a disbeliever and one of Satan’s friends.

translated_text:
As for Allah Most High creating His creatures, providing for them, answering their supplications, guiding their hearts, granting them victory over their enemies, and otherwise bringing them benefit and warding off harm, all this belongs to Allah alone. He does it through whatever means He wills; the messengers have no intermediary role in such matters.

Moreover, however far a man may advance in “asceticism, worship, and knowledge,” if he does not believe in everything Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought, he is neither a believer nor a friend of Allah Most High. Such is the case with the rabbis and monks among the scholars and worshippers of the Jews and Christians. The same applies to those associated with learning and worship among the polytheists—the Arabs, Turks, Indians, and others. Any sage among the Indians or Turks who possesses knowledge, or practises asceticism and worship within his religion, but does not believe in everything Muhammad brought, is a disbeliever and an enemy of Allah, even if some people consider him a friend of Allah—just as the Persian sages were disbelieving Magians.

Likewise, the sages of “Greece,” such as Aristotle and others like him, were polytheists who worshipped idols and heavenly bodies. Aristotle lived three hundred years before the Messiah, peace be upon him, and was a minister to Alexander of Macedon, son of Philip. This is the Alexander from whom Roman and Greek chronologies reckon their dates, as do the Jews and Christians. He is not Dhū al-Qarnayn, whom Allah mentioned in His Book, although some people suppose that Aristotle was a minister to Dhū al-Qarnayn. Seeing that one was named Alexander and that the other is also sometimes called Alexander, they assumed that the two were the same, as Ibn Sīnā and a group who share his view suppose.

But this is not so; rather, this polytheist Alexander, whose minister was Aristotle, lived later than the other. He neither built the barrier nor reached the lands of Gog and Magog. It is from this Alexander, whose ministers included Aristotle, that the well-known Roman chronology is reckoned.

Among the various polytheists—the Arabs, Indians, Turks, Greeks, and others—there are those who devote themselves earnestly to learning, asceticism, and worship. Yet they neither follow the messengers nor believe in what they brought; they neither accept their reports as true nor obey their commands. Such people are neither believers nor friends of Allah. Devils associate with them and descend upon them, enabling them to disclose certain hidden matters to people and perform extraordinary feats of the same kind as sorcery. They belong to the same category as soothsayers and sorcerers upon whom devils descend.

Allah Most High says:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?”

“They descend upon every sinful liar.”

“They pass on what is heard, and most of them are liars.”

All these people who lay claim to disclosures of hidden matters and extraordinary feats, if they do not follow the messengers, will inevitably lie, and their devils will lie to them. Their deeds will inevitably include sin and wickedness, such as some form of polytheism, injustice, indecency, excess, or innovations in worship. This is why devils descend upon them and associate with them, so that they become friends of Satan rather than friends of the Most Merciful.

Allah Most High says:

“And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil

who becomes his companion.”

The remembrance of the Most Merciful is the reminder with which He sent His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, such as the Quran. Whoever does not believe in the Quran, affirm the truth of its reports, and regard its commands as binding has turned away from it. Allah therefore appoints a devil for him, who becomes his companion. Allah Most High says:

“And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down.”

And He Most High says:

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind when I used to see?’”

“He will say, ‘Just as Our signs came to you and you neglected them, so today you will be neglected.’”

This shows that His remembrance refers to the verses He has revealed. Thus, even if a man were constantly to remember Allah, Glorified and Exalted, night and day, practice the utmost asceticism, and strive diligently in worshipping Him, yet did not follow the reminder He has revealed—the Quran—he would be among the friends of Satan, even if he flew through the air or walked on water. For Satan carries him through the air. This has been discussed at length elsewhere.

Section

Some people possess faith while also having a trait of hypocrisy. As related in the two Sahīh collections, ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Four traits—whoever possesses them is a complete hypocrite, and whoever possesses one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it:

When he speaks, he lies;

when he makes a promise, he breaks it; when he is entrusted with something, he betrays that trust; and when he makes a covenant, he acts treacherously.”

Also in the two Sahīh collections, Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Faith has sixty-odd or seventy-odd branches. The highest is the declaration that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and the lowest is removing something harmful from the road. Modesty is a branch of faith.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that whoever possesses one of these traits has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it. It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said to Abū Dharr—who was among the finest believers:

“You are a man who still has some pre-Islamic ignorance in him.”

He asked, “O Messenger of Allah, even at my advanced age?”

He replied, “Yes.”

It is also established in the Sahīh that he said:

“Four practices in my community belong to pre-Islamic ignorance: boasting of ancestral distinction, disparaging people’s lineage, wailing over the dead, and seeking rain through the stars.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted with something, he betrays that trust.”

In Sahīh Muslim, the wording includes:

“Even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim.”

Al-Bukhārī related that Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: “I met thirty of the Companions of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, all of whom feared hypocrisy for themselves.”

Allah Most High says:

“What befell you on the day the two armies met was by Allah’s permission, so that He might make evident the believers,”

“and make evident those who were hypocrites. They were told, ‘Come, fight in Allah’s cause, or help defend.’ They said, ‘Had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you.’ They were closer that day to disbelief

than to faith.”

Allah thus described these people as closer to disbelief than to faith. It is therefore clear that they combine faith and disbelief, with disbelief predominating, while others combine the two with faith predominating.

Since the “friends of Allah” are the believers who are mindful of Him, a servant’s friendship with Allah Most High is proportionate to his faith and piety. Whoever is more perfect in faith and piety is more perfect in friendship with Allah.

People therefore differ in their degrees of friendship with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, according to their differing degrees of faith and piety. Likewise, they differ in their degrees of enmity towards Allah according to their differing degrees of disbelief and hypocrisy. Allah Most High says:

“Whenever a surah is revealed, some of them ask, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.”

“But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds impurity to their impurity, and they die as disbelievers.”

He Most High also says:

“Postponing the sacred months is only an increase in disbelief.”

He Most High also says:

“As for those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them piety.”

Concerning the hypocrites, He Most High says:

“In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease.”

He, Glorified and Most High, has thus made clear that a single person may have a share of friendship with Allah in proportion to his faith, and may also have a share of enmity towards Allah in proportion to his disbelief and hypocrisy. He Most High says:

“And so that those who believe may increase in faith.”

He Most High also says:

“So that they may increase in faith beyond the faith they already have.”

Section

The friends of Allah fall into “two ranks”: the foremost, who are brought near to Him, and the people of the right, who follow a moderate course. Allah mentions them in several places in His Mighty Book: at the beginning and end of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah, and in Sūrat al-Insān, Sūrat al-Mutaffifīn, and Sūrat Fātir.

He, Glorified and Most High, mentions the greater resurrection at the beginning of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah and the lesser resurrection at its end. At its beginning, He says:

“When the Event occurs,
there can be no denying its occurrence,
bringing some low and raising others.
When the earth is shaken violently,
and the mountains are crushed to powder,
becoming scattered dust,
and you are divided into three groups:
the people of the right—what people are the people of the right!
And the people of the left—what people are the people of the left!
And the foremost will be the foremost.
Those are the ones brought near to Allah,
in Gardens of Bliss:
a multitude from the earlier generations,
and a few from the later generations.”

This is the division of humanity when the greater resurrection takes place, at which Allah gathers the first and the last, as He, Glorified be He, has described in numerous places in His Book.

Then, at the end of the surah, He Most High says:

“Then why not”—meaning, “Why do you not”—“when the soul reaches the throat,
while you are looking on,
and We are nearer to him than you, though you do not see—
then why not, if you are not subject to judgment,
bring it back, if you are truthful?”

“Then, if he is among those brought near to Allah,
there will be rest, bounty, and a Garden of Bliss.
And if he is among the people of the right,
then a greeting of peace to you from the people of the right.
But if he is among the misguided deniers,
then a welcome of scalding water
and burning in Hell.
Indeed, this is the absolute truth.
So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.”

He Most High says in Sūrat al-Insān:

“Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he chooses to be grateful or ungrateful.
Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a blazing Fire.
Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor,
a spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it flow abundantly.
They fulfil their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.
They give food, despite their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive,
saying, ‘We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We desire neither reward nor thanks from you.
Indeed, we fear from our Lord a grim and terrible Day.’
So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and grant them radiance and joy,
and reward them for their patience with a Garden and garments of silk.”

And the subsequent verses.

Likewise, He mentions them in Sūrat al-Mutaffifīn, saying:

“No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn.”

Then He goes on to say:

“No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyyīn.
And what will make you know what ‘Illiyyīn is?
It is an inscribed record,
witnessed by those brought near to Allah.
Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss,
seated on couches, gazing around.
You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.
They will be given a sealed, pure wine to drink,
whose seal is musk—so for this let those who aspire compete.
Its mixture will be from Tasnīm,
a spring from which those brought near to Allah drink.”

It is reported from Ibn ‘Abbās—may Allah be pleased with them both—and others among the early generations that they said: “It is mixed

for the people of the right, while those brought near to Allah drink it pure.” This is indeed as they said. For the Most High says, “drink of it” (yashrabu bihā), not “drink from it” (yashrabu minhā), because He has given the word “drink” the additional sense of having one’s thirst quenched by it. A person may drink without having his thirst quenched. Thus, saying “they drink from it” does not indicate that their thirst is quenched, whereas “they drink of it” means that their thirst is quenched by it. Those brought near to Allah have their thirst quenched by it and therefore have no need of anything inferior to it alongside it. For this reason, they drink it pure, unlike the people of the right, for whom it is mixed with something else. This accords with what the Most High says in Sūrat al-Insān:

“Whose mixture is camphor—a spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it flow abundantly.”

The servants of Allah are those brought near to Him who are mentioned in that surah. This is because recompense corresponds to deeds, whether good or evil. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals a Muslim’s faults, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah continues to help His servant so long as the servant helps his brother. Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge, Allah will thereby make easy for him a path to Paradise. Whenever people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, tranquillity descends upon them, mercy envelops them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. Whoever is held back by his deeds will not be advanced by his lineage.”

Muslim narrated this in his Sahīh. And he said:

may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Show mercy to those on earth, and the One in heaven will show mercy to you.”

Al-Tirmidhī said, “An authentic hadith.” Another authentic hadith recorded in the Sunan collections states:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I am al-Rahmān (the Most Merciful). I created the bond of kinship (al-rahim) and derived its name from My name. Whoever maintains it, I shall maintain ties with him; whoever severs it, I shall cut him off.’”

He also said:

“Whoever maintains it, Allah will maintain ties with him; whoever severs it, Allah will sever ties with him.”

There are many similar examples.

The close friends of Allah Most High are of two kinds: those brought near to Him and the people of the right, as explained earlier. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, described the deeds of both groups in the hadith concerning Allah’s close friends:

“Allah Most High says: ‘Whoever shows enmity to a close friend of Mine has openly declared war against Me. Nothing by which My servant draws near to Me equals his fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks.’”

The righteous—the people of the right—are those who draw near to Him through obligatory duties. They do what Allah has made obligatory upon them and refrain from what He has forbidden them. They do not oblige themselves to perform recommended acts or to forgo what is superfluous among permissible things. As for the foremost, those brought near to Him, they draw near to Him through voluntary acts after fulfilling the obligatory duties, and thus they perform

obligatory duties and recommended acts, and refrain from forbidden and disliked acts. When they drew near to Him through all the acts dear to them that they were capable of performing, the Lord loved them with a complete love, as He, Most High, says:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him.”

This means love in its fullest sense, just as He, Most High, says:

“Guide us to the straight path—the path of those You have blessed, not those who have incurred Your wrath, nor those who have gone astray.”

That is, He bestowed upon them the full and complete blessing mentioned in His words:

“Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are!”

For those brought near to Him, even permissible activities became acts of obedience through which they drew near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. All their deeds thus became acts of worship devoted to Allah. They therefore drank an unmixed draught, just as their deeds had been purely for Him. Those who followed a middle course, however, performed some deeds for themselves, for which they are neither punished nor rewarded. They therefore did not drink an unmixed draught; rather, some of the drink of those brought near was mixed into theirs, in proportion to the mixture they had made in this world.

A parallel to this is the division of the prophets, peace be upon them, into servants who are messengers and prophets who are kings. Allah, Glorified is He, gave Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the choice between being a servant and messenger or a prophet and king. He chose to be a servant and messenger. Examples of prophets who were kings include David, Solomon, and others like them, blessings and peace be upon them both. Allah Most High says in the account of Solomon, who said:

“My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as no one after me will have. Indeed, You are the Bestower.”

“So We subjected the wind to him, blowing

gently at his command wherever he directed it. And the devils—every builder and diver—and others bound together in shackles. This is Our gift: give or withhold as you please, without being called to account.”

That is: give to whomever you wish and withhold from whomever you wish; you will not be called to account. A prophet who is a king performs what Allah has enjoined upon him, refrains from what Allah has forbidden him, and exercises his authority and disposes of wealth as he wishes and chooses, without incurring sin. A servant who is a messenger, however, gives to no one except by his Lord’s command. He does not give or withhold merely as he wishes. Rather, it is reported that he said:

“By Allah, I neither give to anyone nor withhold from anyone. I am only a distributor; I allocate as I have been commanded.”

This is why Allah ascribes the funds governed by Islamic law to Himself and the Messenger, as in His words, Most High:

“Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.”

And His words, Most High:

“Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and the Messenger.”

And His words, Most High:

“Know that whatever spoils you acquire, one-fifth belongs to Allah and the Messenger.”

For this reason, the best-supported scholarly view is that these funds should be spent on purposes beloved to Allah and His Messenger, according to the ruler’s considered judgment. This is the position of Mālik and others among the early generations, and it is also reported as one position held by Ahmad. Another view is that the fifth should be divided into five shares, as held by al-Shāfiʿī and, according to his well-known position, Ahmad. Yet another view is that it should be divided into three shares, as held by Abū Hanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him.

And “the point here” is that a servant who is a messenger is superior to a prophet who is a king, just as Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—blessings and peace be upon them—are superior to Joseph, David, and Solomon—peace be upon them. Likewise, those who are foremost and brought near to Allah are superior to the righteous companions of the right who are not among those foremost and brought near. Whoever fulfils what Allah has made obligatory upon him and does whatever he likes among permissible things belongs to the latter group. Whoever does only what Allah loves and is pleased with, intending to use what has been made permissible to him to help him fulfil Allah’s commands, belongs to the former group.

Section

Allah Most High mentions “His friends”—those who follow a moderate course and those who are foremost—in Surah Fātir, saying:

“Then We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book. Among them are those who wrong themselves, those who follow a moderate course, and those who are foremost in good deeds by Allah’s permission. That is the great bounty.”

“Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.”

“And they will say, ‘Praise be to Allah, who has removed all sorrow from us. Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.’”

“‘He who, out of His bounty, has settled us in the everlasting abode, where neither toil nor weariness touches us.’”

 إنَّ أَهْلَ الْكَبَائِرِ مُخَلَّدُونَ فِي النَّارِ وَتَأَوَّلَ الْآيَةَ عَلَى أَنَّ السَّابِقِينَ هُمْ الَّذِينَ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَأَنَّ الْمُقْتَصِدَ أَوْ الظَّالِمَ لِنَفْسِهِ لَا يَدْخُلُهَا كَمَا تَأَوَّلَهُ مِنْ الْمُعْتَزِلَةِ فَهُوَ مُقَابَلٌ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْمُرْجِئَةِ الَّذِينَ لَا يَقْطَعُونَ بِدُخُولِ أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكَبَائِرِ النَّارَ وَيَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكَبَائِرِ قَدْ يَدْخُلُ جَمِيعُهُمْ الْجَنَّةَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عَذَابٍ وَكِلَاهُمَا مُخَالِفٌ لِلسُّنَّةِ الْمُتَوَاتِرَةِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَلِإِجْمَاعِ سَلَفِ الْأُمَّةِ وَأَئِمَّتِهَا. وَقَدْ دَلَّ عَلَى فَسَادِ قَوْلِ 
" الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ "
 قَوْلُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى فِي آيَتَيْنِ مِنْ كِتَابِهِ وَهُوَ قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{إنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ}
 فَأَخْبَرَ تَعَالَى أَنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الشِّرْكَ وَأَخْبَرَ أَنَّهُ يَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُرَادَ بِذَلِكَ التَّائِبُ كَمَا يَقُولُهُ مَنْ يَقُولُهُ مِنْ

“Those who follow a moderate course” fulfil their obligations and avoid what is forbidden, while “those who are foremost in good deeds” fulfil their obligations and perform voluntary acts of worship, as described in those verses.

His words, “Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter,” are among the evidence Ahl al-Sunnah cite to establish that none of those who affirm Allah’s oneness will remain in Hell forever. As for many perpetrators of major sins entering Hell, this is established through mass-transmitted reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, mass-transmitted reports establish their eventual departure from Hell, the intercession of our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for perpetrators of major sins, and the deliverance from Hell of those who leave it through the intercession of our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the intercession of others.

Whoever says that perpetrators of major sins will remain in Hell forever, and interprets the verse to mean that only those who are foremost will enter those gardens, whereas those who follow a moderate course or wrong themselves will not—as some of the Mu'tazilah have interpreted it—is met with the opposing interpretation of the Murji’ah. They do not affirm with certainty that any perpetrator of major sins will enter Hell, and claim that all perpetrators of major sins might enter Paradise without punishment. Both positions contradict the mass-transmitted Sunnah of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the consensus of the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars.

The falsity of the positions of “both groups” is demonstrated by Allah Most High’s statement, which occurs in two verses of His Book:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.”

The Most High thus declares that He does not forgive associating partners with Him, and that He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. This cannot be understood as referring to those who repent, as claimed by some among

the Mu'tazilah, for Allah forgives associating partners with Him when a person repents, and He likewise forgives lesser sins for those who repent. Such forgiveness is therefore not made contingent on His will.

Thus, when speaking of forgiveness for those who repent, the Most High said:

“Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.’”

Here He made forgiveness universal and unqualified, for Allah forgives His servant any sin of which he repents. Whoever repents of associating partners with Allah, Allah forgives him; whoever repents of major sins, Allah forgives him. Whatever sin His servant repents of, Allah forgives him. Thus, in the verse concerning repentance, He made forgiveness universal and unqualified, whereas in the other verse He made a distinction and imposed a condition: He singled out associating partners with Him as something He does not forgive, and made forgiveness of anything else contingent on His will. Denial of the Creator is included in associating partners with Him.

This demonstrates the falsity of the view of anyone who categorically affirms forgiveness for every sinner—or considers it possible that no sin will be punished. By mentioning the association of partners with Him, He also draws attention to what is even graver, such as denial of the Creator. For if that view were correct, He would not have stated that He forgives some but not others. If everyone who wronged himself were forgiven without repentance or good deeds that erase sins, He would not have made that forgiveness contingent on His will.

The Most High’s words,

“but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills,”

are evidence that He forgives some but not others. Thus, both outright denial and a blanket suspension of judgment are invalid.

translated_text:
Section

Since the “friends of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,” are the pious believers, and people differ in their faith and piety, their friendship with Allah varies accordingly. Likewise, since they differ in disbelief and hypocrisy, their enmity towards Allah varies accordingly.

The foundation of faith and piety is belief in Allah’s messengers. This is encompassed in belief in the Seal of the Messengers, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for belief in him entails belief in all of Allah’s Books and messengers. The foundation of disbelief and hypocrisy is rejection of the messengers and what they brought. This is the disbelief for which a person deserves punishment in the Hereafter, for Allah Most High has stated in His Book that He does not punish anyone until the message has reached them.

Allah Most High said:

“And We would never punish until We had sent a messenger.”

And He Most High said:

“Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms.”

“And We sent messengers whose stories We have related to you before, and messengers whose stories We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.”

“messengers bringing good news and warnings, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers.”

Allah Most High said concerning the people of the Fire:

“Whenever a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did no warner come to you?’”

“They will say, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said: Allah has revealed nothing; you are only in great error.’”

He thus states that whenever a group is cast into the Fire, they acknowledge that a warner came to them and that they rejected him. This shows that every group cast into it consists of those who rejected the warner. Allah Most High also said, addressing Iblīs:

“I will surely fill Hell with you and all those among them who follow you.”

He thus states that He will fill it with Iblīs and his followers. Once it is filled with them, no one else will enter it. It is therefore clear that none will enter the Fire except those who followed Satan. This indicates that no one without sin will enter it, for such a person has neither followed Satan nor committed sin. What preceded also indicates that none will enter it except those against whom proof has been established through the messengers.

Section

Some people believe in the messengers in general terms. As for detailed belief, much of what the messengers brought may have reached a person, while some of it has not. He believes in whatever has reached him from the messengers, while remaining unaware of what has not reached him; had it reached him, he would have believed in it. Nevertheless, he believes in general terms in everything the messengers brought. If such a person acts upon what he knows Allah has commanded him to do, along with

his faith and piety, he is one of the friends of Allah Most High. His share of friendship with Allah is commensurate with his faith and piety. As for matters concerning which proof has not been established against him, Allah Most High has not required him to know them or believe in them in detail, so He will not punish him for failing to do so. Nevertheless, he misses out on the fullness of friendship with Allah in proportion to what he has missed of those matters. Thus, someone who knows what the messengers brought, believes in it in detail, and acts upon it is more complete in faith and friendship with Allah than someone who neither knows it in detail nor acts upon it. Yet both are friends of Allah Most High.

Paradise has ranks that differ immensely, and Allah’s believing, pious friends occupy those ranks according to their faith and piety.

He, Blessed and Most High, said:

“Whoever desires this fleeting life, We hasten therein whatever We will for whomever We choose. Then We have appointed Hell for him, which he will enter, condemned and banished.”

“But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as he should, while being a believer—it is they whose striving will be appreciated.”

“To each We extend the gifts of your Lord—to these and to those. The gifts of your Lord are not withheld.”

“See how We have favoured some over others. But the Hereafter is greater in ranks and greater in distinction.”

Allah, Glorified and Most High, thus explains that He extends His gifts both to those who desire this world and to those who desire the Hereafter, and that His gifts are withheld from neither the righteous nor the wicked. Then He, Most High, said:

“See how We have favoured some over others. But the Hereafter is greater in ranks and greater in distinction.”

Allah, Glorified be He, thus explains that the differences in rank among the people of the Hereafter are greater than those among people in this world, and that its ranks are greater than the ranks of this world. He has also made clear

the differences in rank among His prophets, peace be upon them, just as among the rest of His believing servants. He, Most High, said:

“Those messengers—We favoured some over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some in rank. We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit.”

He, Most High, also said:

“We certainly favoured some prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms.”

In Sahīh Muslim, Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, relates that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah’s help, and do not lose resolve. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such and such, this and that would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah has decreed, and He does whatever He wills,’ for ‘if only’ opens the way for Satan’s work.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Abū Hurayrah and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀs, may Allah be pleased with them both, relate that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a judge exercises his judgment and reaches the correct decision, he receives two rewards; when he exercises his judgment but errs, he receives one reward.”

Allah Most High has said:

“Those among you who spent and fought before the conquest are not equal to the others. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. Yet Allah has promised them all the finest reward.”

He, Most High, also said:

“Those believers who remain behind, other than those with disabilities, are not equal to those who strive in Allah’s cause with their wealth and their lives. Allah has favoured those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who remain behind by a rank. To each Allah has promised the finest reward, but Allah has favoured those who strive over those who remain behind with a tremendous reward—ranks from Him, forgiveness, and mercy. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

He, Most High, also said:

“Do you consider providing water for pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to the deeds of one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in Allah’s cause? They are not equal in Allah’s sight. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

“Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in Allah’s cause with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with Allah. It is they who will triumph.

“Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him, His pleasure, and gardens in which they will enjoy lasting bliss,

“remaining there forever. Indeed, with Allah is a tremendous reward.”

He, Most High, also said:

“Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing in prayer, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for his Lord’s mercy, like one who is not? Say, ‘Are those who know equal to those who do not know?’ Only people of understanding take heed.”

He, Most High, also said:

“Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge in rank. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.”

Section

Since a servant can only be a friend of Allah if he is a believer who fears Him, as He, Most High, says:

“Indeed, the friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve—those who believe and are mindful of Him,”

and as stated in the well-known hadith in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, already cited, in which Allah, Blessed and Most High, says:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him,”

and since he cannot be a believer who fears Allah until he draws near to Him through the obligatory acts of worship, thereby becoming one of the righteous

—those of the right hand—and thereafter continues to draw near through voluntary acts of worship until he becomes one of the foremost, those brought near to Allah, it is evident that no disbeliever or hypocrite can be a friend of Allah. The same applies to those whose faith and worship are not valid, even supposing that they bear no sin, such as the children of disbelievers and those whom the call to Islam has not reached—even if it is held that they will not be punished until a messenger is sent to them. They cannot be among Allah’s friends unless they are believers who fear Him. Whoever does not draw near to Allah, whether by doing good deeds or refraining from evil deeds, is not among His friends. The same applies to the insane and to children, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“The pen of accountability has been lifted from three: the insane person until he regains his sanity, the child until he reaches puberty, and the sleeper until he awakens.”

This hadith was narrated by the compilers of the Sunan collections on the authority of ‘Alī and ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both. The scholars versed in hadith have unanimously accepted it. However, according to the majority of scholars, the acts of worship of a child who has reached the age of discernment are valid, and he is rewarded for them.

As for the insane person from whom the pen of accountability has been lifted, none of his acts of worship is valid, by scholarly consensus. Neither his faith nor his disbelief is valid, nor are his prayer or any other acts of worship. Indeed, rational people generally consider him unfit even for worldly pursuits such as commerce and crafts. He is not fit to work as a cloth merchant, perfumer, blacksmith, or carpenter, and his contracts are invalid by scholarly consensus. This differs from a child who has reached the age of discernment: in some matters, his statements have legal effect according to scriptural texts and scholarly consensus, while in others their effect is disputed.

If an insane person’s faith, fear of Allah, and drawing near to Him through obligatory and voluntary acts of worship are not valid, and he therefore cannot be a friend of Allah, then no one may believe that he is a friend of Allah. This is especially so when the evidence offered is either some disclosure of hidden matters heard from him, or some exercise of extraordinary power—for example, seeing him point at someone who then dies or falls into a fit. For it is known that disbelievers and hypocrites—among the polytheists and the People of the Book—have disclosures of hidden matters and extraordinary powers originating from devils, as do soothsayers, sorcerers, and devotees among the polytheists and the People of the Book.

No one may therefore infer from such things alone that a person is a friend of Allah, even if nothing is known about him that contradicts friendship with Allah. How, then, could this be permissible when something is known about him that does contradict it? For example, he may be known not to believe that following the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is obligatory both inwardly and outwardly; rather, he believes that he follows the outward religious law, but not the inward reality. Or he may believe that Allah’s friends have a path to Allah other than the path of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Or he may say, “The prophets have made the path narrow,” or, “They are exemplars for ordinary people, not the elect,” and similar things said by some who claim friendship with Allah. Such people harbour disbelief that is incompatible with faith, let alone friendship with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whoever cites the extraordinary feats performed by any of them as evidence of their friendship with Allah is more astray than the Jews and Christians.

translated_text:
The same applies to an insane person, for his insanity precludes the validity of the faith and acts of worship that are prerequisites for friendship with Allah. As for someone who is sometimes insane and sometimes lucid, if, during his lucid periods, he believes in Allah and His Messenger, fulfils his obligations, and avoids what is forbidden, then his insanity does not prevent Allah from rewarding him for the faith and fear of Allah he displayed while lucid. His share of friendship with Allah will be commensurate with that.

Likewise, if someone becomes insane after having had faith and feared Allah, Allah will reward and recompense him for his previous faith and fear of Him. He will not nullify that because of the insanity with which the person has been afflicted through no sin of his own. During his insanity, he is not held accountable.

Accordingly, if someone presents himself as a friend of Allah while neither fulfilling his obligations nor avoiding what is forbidden—and may even do things contrary to these requirements—no one may say, “This is a friend of Allah.” If such a person is not insane, but is merely bewildered without being insane, or if he loses his reason through insanity at times and regains it at others, yet does not fulfil his obligations and instead believes that he is not obliged to follow the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, then he is a disbeliever. If, however, he is insane both inwardly and outwardly and is no longer held accountable, then, although he is not punished as disbelievers are punished, he is not entitled to the honour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to which people of faith and fear of Allah are entitled. In neither case may anyone believe him to be a friend of Allah. But if he had a lucid period during which he believed in Allah and feared Him, his share of friendship with Allah would be commensurate with that.

But if he harbours disbelief or hypocrisy while lucid, or was a disbeliever or hypocrite before becoming insane, then he bears disbelief or hypocrisy for which he is liable to punishment. His insanity does not absolve him of the disbelief or hypocrisy he displays while lucid.

Section

Allah’s friends have no distinctive outward features in matters that are permissible. They are not distinguished by wearing one kind of clothing rather than another when both are permissible, nor by shaving, trimming, or braiding their hair when that is permissible. As the saying goes:

“How many a truthful believer wears a coat,
And how many a heretic wears a cloak!”

Rather, they are found among all groups within the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, provided they are not among those given to manifest religious innovations or wickedness. They are found among people devoted to the Quran and people of knowledge, among those who wage jihad and wield the sword, and among merchants, craftsmen, and farmers. Allah mentions the various groups within the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in His words, Most High:

“Your Lord knows that you stand in prayer for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, as do some of those with you. Allah determines the night and the day. He knows that you cannot keep precise account of it, so He has turned to you in mercy. Recite, then, whatever you can of the Quran. He knows that some of you will be ill, others travelling through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and others fighting in Allah’s cause. So recite whatever you can of it.”

The early generations called people of religious devotion and learning “the reciters,” a designation that included both scholars and ascetics. Later, the terms “Sufis” and “the poor” came into use. The term “Sufi” derives from wearing wool (sūf); this is the correct explanation. It has also been said to derive from safwat al-fuqahā’ (the elite of the jurists); from Sūfa ibn Udd ibn Tānja, an Arab tribe known for religious devotion; from the people of the Suffa (the shaded portico); from safā (purity); from safwa (the elite); or from the foremost rank before Allah Most High. These explanations are weak, for if that were its derivation, the term would have been suffī, safā’ī, safawī, or saffī, rather than sūfī.

The designation “the poor” also came to refer to those following the spiritual path. This is a later usage. People have disputed which designation is superior: “Sufi” or “poor.” They also dispute which is better: a grateful rich person or a patient poor person.

This latter question was the subject of an early disagreement between al-Junayd and Abū al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Atā’, and two positions on it have been reported from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The correct position on all of this is expressed in the words of Allah, Blessed and Most High:

“O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.”

I replied, “Yes.”

He said, “Restrain this tongue of yours,” and took hold of his tongue.

Muādh said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say?”

He replied, “For shame, O Muādh! What casts people into the Fire on their noses but the harvest of their tongues?”

This is explained by his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as authentically reported in the two Sahīhs:

“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”

Speaking good is better than remaining silent about it, while refraining from evil speech is better than uttering it. As for perpetual silence, it is a prohibited religious innovation. Likewise, abstaining from eating bread and meat and from drinking water is also among the blameworthy religious innovations. As authentically reported in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Ibn Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man standing in the sun and asked, “What is this?”

They replied, “It is Abū Isrā’īl. He has vowed to stand in the sun, not to seek shade or speak, and to fast.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Tell him to sit down, seek shade, speak, and complete his fast.”

This means following a different way in the belief that it is better than his. Whoever does so has disassociated himself from Allah and His Messenger. Allah Most High says:

“Who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?”

Rather, every Muslim must believe that the best speech is Allah’s speech and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is authentically reported that he would proclaim this in his sermon every Friday.

Section

It is not a condition of being an ally of Allah that one be infallible, never making a mistake or falling into error. Rather, some knowledge of the Sharia may remain unknown to him, and certain religious matters may become confused for him, to the point that he regards some things as commanded by Allah and others as forbidden

by Allah. He may also suppose that certain extraordinary occurrences are among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah Most High’s allies, when in fact they are from Satan, who has disguised them for him because of his deficient spiritual rank. He does not recognize that they are from Satan, although he may not thereby cease to be an ally of Allah Most High.

For Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has pardoned this community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do. Allah Most High says:

“The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. All have believed in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers: ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers.’ And they say, ‘We hear and obey. We seek Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.’”

“Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned, and it will bear the evil it has earned. ‘Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.’”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs that Allah, glorified is He, answered this supplication and said, “I have done so.” In Sahīh Muslim, Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated:

“When this verse was revealed—‘Whether you disclose what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He then forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah has power over all things’—their hearts were gripped by a distress more severe than anything they had ever felt before. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Say: We hear, we obey, and we submit.’ Then Allah instilled faith in their hearts, and Allah Most High revealed: ‘Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity’

up to His words, ‘or make a mistake.’ Allah said, ‘I have done so.’ ‘Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us.’ He said, ‘I have done so.’ ‘Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.’ He said, ‘I have done so.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“There is no blame upon you for what you do by mistake, but only for what your hearts deliberately intend.”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs, in narrations from Abū Hurayra and ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a judge exercises independent judgment and is correct, he has two rewards; if he errs, he has one reward.”

Thus, he did not deem someone sinful for erring in the exercise of independent judgment. Rather, he granted him a reward for his effort and declared his error forgiven. However, someone whose independent judgment is correct receives two rewards and is therefore superior to him.

Since an ally of Allah may make mistakes, people are not obliged to believe everything an ally of Allah says; otherwise, he would be a prophet. Indeed, an ally of Allah may not rely on what is cast into his heart, or on experiences he regards as inspiration, communication, or an address from the True One, unless it accords with the revealed law. Rather, he must assess all of this against what Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought. If it agrees with that, he accepts it; if it contradicts it, he does not accept it. If he does not know whether it agrees or contradicts, he must suspend judgment.

In this matter, people fall into “three categories”: two extremes and a middle course. Some, once they believe that a person is an ally of Allah, agree with him in everything they think has been communicated

to his heart from his Lord, and unquestioningly accept everything he does. Others, when they see him say or do something that does not accord with the revealed law, exclude him entirely from Allah’s allies, even if he has erred while exercising independent judgment. The best course lies between these extremes: he should neither be regarded as infallible nor held sinful when he errs in exercising independent judgment. He is not to be followed in everything he says, nor judged a disbeliever or an evildoer when he has exercised independent judgment. People are obliged to follow what Allah sent His Messenger with. However, if he disagrees with some jurists while agreeing with others, no one has the right to compel him to adopt the opposing opinion and say, “This man has contradicted the revealed law.”

It is authentically established in the two Sahīhs that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Among the nations before you were men who received inspiration. If there is anyone like them in my community, ‘Umar is one of them.”

Al-Tirmidhī and others narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Had I not been sent among you, ‘Umar would have been sent among you.”

In another hadith:

“Allah has placed the truth upon ‘Umar’s tongue and in his heart.”

It also states:

“Had there been a prophet after me, it would have been ‘Umar.”

‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say, “We did not consider it unlikely that al-sakīna spoke through ‘Umar’s tongue.” This is authentically established from him through the narration of al-Sha‘bī.

Ibn ‘Umar said:

“Whenever ‘Umar said of something, ‘I believe it to be such-and-such,’ it turned out as he said.”

Qays ibn Tāriq said, “We used to say that an angel spoke through ‘Umar’s tongue.”

And ‘Umar used to say:

Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, replied, “Did he not say, ‘Except where a rightful claim applies’? Zakat is one such rightful claim. By Allah, if they withheld from me even a young she-goat that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, I would fight them for withholding it.”

‘Umar said, “By Allah, as soon as I saw that Allah had opened Abū Bakr’s heart to fighting, I knew that it was right.”

There are similar examples demonstrating Abū Bakr’s superiority over ‘Umar, even though ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, was a muhaddath (one granted inspiration). The rank of the siddīq (one of consummate truthfulness) is above that of the muhaddath, because the siddīq receives from the infallible Messenger everything the Messenger says and does, whereas the muhaddath receives certain things from his own heart. His heart, however, is not infallible, so he must test what he receives against what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought.

For this reason, ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, would consult the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, debate with them, and defer to them in certain matters. They would dispute some matters with him, and he would present evidence against them while they presented evidence against him from the Quran and Sunnah. He allowed them to disagree with him and did not tell them, “I am a muhaddath, inspired and spoken to, so you must accept what I say and not oppose me.”

Thus, if anyone claims—or his companions claim on his behalf—that he is an ally of Allah who is spoken to, and that his followers must therefore accept everything he says, never oppose him, and accept his spiritual state without assessing it against the Quran and Sunnah, then both he and they are mistaken. Such a person is among the most misguided of people. For ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, is superior to him, and he is

the Commander of the Faithful, yet the Muslims would dispute what he said, while both he and they adhered to the Quran and Sunnah. The early generations of this community and its leading scholars agreed that anyone’s statements may be accepted or rejected, except those of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

This is one of the distinctions between the prophets and others. The prophets, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them, must be believed in everything they convey from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and obeyed in what they command. This is unlike Allah’s allies: it is not obligatory to obey everything they command or believe everything they report. Rather, their commands and reports must be assessed against the Quran and Sunnah. Whatever agrees with the Quran and Sunnah must be accepted, and whatever contradicts them must be rejected—even if the person who said it is one of Allah’s allies and has exercised independent judgment, is excused for what he said, and is rewarded for his effort. Nevertheless, if he contradicts the Quran and Sunnah, he is mistaken. His error is forgiven if he has feared Allah to the best of his ability, for Allah Most High says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

This explains His words, Most High:

“O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared.”

Ibn Mas‘ūd and others said, “Fearing Him as He should be feared means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not met with ingratitude.” That is, according to your ability, for Allah Most High does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. As He, Most High, says:

“Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the good it has earned, and bear the evil it has earned.”

And He, Most High, says:

“But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity—will be the inhabitants of Paradise, abiding there forever.”

And He, Most High, says: “And give full measure

and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity.”

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has mentioned belief in what the prophets brought in several places, as in His words, Most High:

“Say, ‘We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.’”

And He, Most High, says:

“Alif Lām Mīm.”

“This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those who fear Allah,”

“Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them,”

“And who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and are certain of the Hereafter.”

“They are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is they who are successful.”

And He, Most High, says:

“Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. Rather, righteousness is in one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets; who gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, stranded travellers, those who ask, and to free slaves; who establishes prayer and gives the prescribed alms; and in those who fulfil their pledges when they make them, and who are patient in poverty, hardship, and battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and those are the ones who fear Allah.”

What I have mentioned—that Allah’s allies must adhere firmly to the Quran and Sunnah, and that none of them is infallible such that he or anyone else may follow whatever occurs in his heart without assessing it against the Quran and Sunnah—is something upon which the allies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, have agreed. Anyone who disagrees with this is not among those allies of Allah, glorified is He, whom Allah has commanded

They believe that someone is an ally of Allah and suppose that everything an ally of Allah says must be accepted, that they must defer to everything he says and submit to everything he does, even if it contradicts the Quran and Sunnah. so whoever follows him is among Allah’s righteous allies, His successful soldiers, and His righteous servants; whoever does not follow him is among Allah’s enemies—the losers and evildoers. “On the Day when the wrongdoer bites his hands, saying, ‘If only I had taken a path with the Messenger!

Anyone who goes against any part of what the Messenger brought, following someone whom he believes to be a friend of Allah, bases his position on the assumption that this person is a friend of Allah and that a friend of Allah must never be contradicted in anything. Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Let none of you consult anything but the Quran about himself. If he loves the Quran, he loves Allah; and if he hates the Quran, he hates Allah and His Messenger.”

ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“If our hearts were pure, they would never have their fill of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Ibn Masʿūd also said:

“Remembrance of Allah causes faith to grow in the heart as water causes plants to grow, and singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart as water causes plants to grow.”

The authentic hadith recorded in al-Bukhārī and elsewhere has already been cited. In it, Allah says:

Just as one must distinguish a true prophet from a lying claimant to prophethood—distinguishing Muhammad, the truthful and trustworthy Messenger of the Lord of all worlds, Moses, the Messiah, and others from Musaylima the Liar, al-Aswad al-Ansī, Tulayha al-Asadī, al-Hārith al-Dimashqī, Bābāh al-Rūmī, and other liars—so too must one distinguish Allah’s pious allies from Satan’s misguided allies.

Section

“Reality”—the reality of religion, the religion of the Lord of all worlds—is what the prophets and messengers agreed upon, even though each had a law and a way. Shirʿa means sharīʿa (religious law). Allah Most High says:

“To each of you We have prescribed a law and a way.”

The Most High also says:

“Then We set you upon a law in matters of religion, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. They can be of no help to you against Allah. Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the ally of the righteous.”

Minhāj means a path. The Most High says:

“If they had remained steadfast on the path, We would have given them abundant water to drink, to test them thereby. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will subject him to an arduous punishment.”

Thus, the prescribed law is like a watering place at a river, while the way is the path one follows. The intended goal is the reality of religion: worshipping Allah alone, without partner. This is the reality of the religion of Islam: that the servant submits to Allah, Lord of all worlds, and submits to no other. Whoever submits both to Him and to another associates partners with Him, and Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him. Whoever does not submit to Allah, but arrogantly refuses to worship Him, is among those of whom Allah says:

“Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation.”

Islam is the religion of all the prophets and messengers, from the earliest to the last. The words of the Most High,

“Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him,”

apply to every time and place.

Noah, Abraham, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus, and the disciples all followed Islam: worshipping Allah alone, without partner. Allah Most High relates that Noah said:

“O my people, if my presence and my reminding you of Allah’s signs have become a burden to you, then I have put my trust in Allah. So resolve upon your course of action,”

up to His words:

“And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.”

The Most High also says:

“Who would turn away from the faith of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? We certainly chose him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.”

“When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of all worlds.’”

“Abraham enjoined this upon his sons, as did Jacob: ‘O my sons, Allah has chosen this religion for you, so do not die except as Muslims.’”

The Most High also says:

“Moses said, ‘O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then in Him

put your trust, if you are Muslims.’”

The sorcerers said:

“Our Lord, pour out patience upon us and cause us to die as Muslims.”

Joseph, peace be upon him, said:

“Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”

Bilqīs said:

“I submit, along with Solomon, to Allah, Lord of all worlds.”

The Most High says:

“By it the prophets who submitted to Allah judged for the Jews, as did the godly scholars and learned men.”

The disciples said:

“We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we are Muslims.”

Thus, the religion of the prophets is one, even though their prescribed laws differed. As reported in the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“We prophets share one religion.”

The Most High says:

“He has ordained for you the same religion that He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: uphold the religion and do not become divided over it. What you call the polytheists to is difficult for them to accept.”

The Most High also says:

“O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I know well what you do.”

“Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.”

“But they divided their religion among themselves into sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has.”
