Section

The early generations of this community, its leading scholars, and all the friends of Allah Most High have agreed that the prophets are superior to those friends of Allah who are not prophets. Allah has placed His servants who have attained felicity and received His favor in four ranks. The Most High says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has favored: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions they are!”

A hadith states:

“The sun has neither risen nor set upon anyone, apart from the prophets and messengers, who is superior to Abū Bakr.”

The best of all communities is the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Most High says:

“You are the best community ever raised up for mankind.”

The Most High also says:

“Then We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in a hadith recorded in al-Musnad:

“You complete the number of seventy communities; you are the best of them and the most honored by Allah.”

The best generation of Muhammad’s community, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the first generation. It is authentically established through several routes of transmission that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best generation is the generation in which I was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.”

This is established through several routes of transmission in the two Sahīh collections. They also record that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not revile my Companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, were any of you to spend gold equal to Mount Uhud, it would not equal a double handful given by one of them, nor even half of that.”

The earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers are superior to the rest of the Companions. The Most High says:

“Those of you who spent and fought before the victory are not equal to those who did so afterward. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward. Yet Allah has promised the finest reward to all.”

The Most High also says:

“The earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.”

The earliest forerunners are those who spent and fought before the victory. The victory here means the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, for it marked the beginning of the conquest of Mecca. On that occasion, Allah Most High revealed:

“Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive you your past and future sins.”

They said, “O Messenger of Allah, is this a victory?” He replied, “Yes.”

The best of the earliest forerunners are “the four caliphs,” and the best of them is Abū Bakr, followed by Umar. This is the position known from the Companions, those who followed them in righteousness, the leading scholars of this community, and its overwhelming majority. Ahl al-Sunnah al-Nabawiyyah fī Naqd Kalām Ahl al-Shī‘ah wa-l-Qadariyyah”.

In short, the Sunni and Shia groups agree that the best member of this community after its Prophet is one of the caliphs. No one who comes after the Companions can be superior to the Companions. The best of Allah Most High’s close friends are those who have the greatest knowledge of what the Messenger—may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace—brought and follow him most faithfully. Such were the Companions, whose knowledge of his religion and adherence to it were the most complete in this community. Abū Bakr al-Siddīq possessed the most complete knowledge of what he brought and put it into practice most fully. He is therefore the best of Allah’s close friends, since Muhammad’s community—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is the best of all communities, its best members are Muhammad’s Companions, and the best of them is Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

Some people have mistakenly supposed that the “Seal of Allah’s Close Friends” is the best of them, drawing an analogy with the Seal of the Prophets. None of the early spiritual masters spoke of the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends except Muhammad ibn Alī al-Hakīm al-Tirmidhī, who wrote a work in which he made errors in several places. Later, a number of people emerged, each claiming to be the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends. Some of them claim that the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends surpasses the Seal of the Prophets in knowledge of Allah, and that the prophets acquire their knowledge of Allah through him. Such is the claim of Ibn Arabī, the author of al-Futūhāt al-Makkiyyah and al-Fusūs. He thus contradicted both revealed law and reason, as well as all the prophets and close friends of Allah Most High. It is as one would say to someone who declared, “The roof fell upon them from beneath them”: “Neither reason nor Quran!”

translated_text:
For the prophets have precedence in time over Allah’s close friends in this community, and the prophets—may the finest blessings and peace be upon them—are superior to Allah’s close friends. How, then, could all the prophets and Allah’s close friends acquire their knowledge of Allah only from someone who comes after them and claims to be the Seal of Allah’s Close Friends? The last of Allah’s close friends is not the best of them, even though the last of the prophets is the best of them. Muhammad’s superiority—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is established by scriptural texts indicating this, such as his saying:

“I am the master of the children of Adam, and I say this without boasting.”

And his saying:

“I will come to the gate of Paradise and ask for it to be opened. The keeper will say, ‘Who are you?’ I will say, ‘Muhammad.’ He will say, ‘I have been commanded not to open it to anyone before you.’”

On “the Night of the Ascension,” Allah raised his rank above all the prophets. He was thus the foremost of those described in the words of the Most High:

“Those messengers—We favored some of them over others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in rank.”

There are other proofs besides these. Each of the prophets receives revelation from Allah. Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in particular had no need of anyone else in his prophethood. His revealed law therefore needed neither a predecessor nor a successor. This contrasts with the Messiah, who referred his followers to the Torah for most of the law and came to complete it. For this reason, Christians needed the prophetic revelations preceding the Messiah, such as the Torah, the Psalms, and the full twenty-four prophetic revelations.

The communities before us needed people granted inspiration, unlike the community of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Through him, Allah gave them all they needed, so that, with him, they needed neither a prophet nor anyone granted inspiration. Rather, there were gathered in him virtues and forms of knowledge

and righteous deeds that He had distributed among the other prophets. Thus, the excellence with which Allah favored him came from Allah, through what He revealed and sent to him, not through a human intermediary.

This is unlike “Allah’s close friends.” Anyone whom the message of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—has reached can be a close friend of Allah only by following Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Whatever guidance and true religion he attains comes through Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, anyone reached by the message of a messenger sent to him can be a close friend of Allah only by following that messenger.

Whoever claims that, among Allah’s close friends whom the message of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—has reached, there are some who have a path to Allah on which they have no need of Muhammad is an unbeliever and a heretic. If he says:

“I need Muhammad for outward knowledge, but not inward knowledge, or for knowledge of the revealed law, but not knowledge of reality,”

then he is worse than those Jews and Christians who said:

“Muhammad is a messenger to the unlettered, but not to the People of the Book.”

For those people believed in part and disbelieved in part, and were unbelievers on that account. Likewise, someone who says that Muhammad was sent with outward knowledge but not inward knowledge believes in part of what he brought and disbelieves in part. He is therefore an unbeliever, and his unbelief is greater than theirs. For inward knowledge—the knowledge of the faith, understanding, and states of the heart—is knowledge of the inward realities of faith. This is nobler than knowledge merely of the outward acts of Islam.

translated_text:
Thus, if someone claims that Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—knew only these outward matters, but not the realities of faith, and that he himself does not derive these realities from the Quran and the Sunnah, he is claiming that the portion of the Messenger’s teachings in which he believes is inferior to the other portion. This is worse than someone who says, “I believe in part and disbelieve in part,” without claiming that the part he believes in is the lesser of the two.

These heretics claim that “closeness to Allah” is superior to “prophethood.” They mislead people by saying, “His closeness to Allah is superior to his prophethood,” and reciting:

“The station of prophethood lies between the two:
Just above the messenger, below the close friend.”

They say, “We share with him in his closeness to Allah, which is greater than his messengership.” This is among their gravest errors. No one has equalled Muhammad in his closeness to Allah—not Abraham or Moses, let alone these heretics.

Every messenger is a prophet and a close friend of Allah. Thus, a messenger is both a prophet and a close friend of Allah: his messengership encompasses his prophethood, and his prophethood encompasses his closeness to Allah. If they suppose that Allah merely informs him without his being a close friend of Allah, this is an impossible supposition. For when Allah informs him, he cannot be anything other than a close friend of Allah. His prophethood cannot be separated from his closeness to Allah; and even if it were supposed to be separate, no one would equal the Messenger in his closeness to Allah.

These people may claim—as does Ibn ‘Arabī, the author of “al-Fusūs”—that they draw from the same source as the angel through whom revelation is conveyed to the Messenger. This is because they adopted “the creed of the philosophers” and then presented it in the guise of “spiritual unveiling.”

These philosophers maintain that the celestial spheres are eternal, without beginning, and have a cause which they seek to resemble, as Aristotle and his followers say; or that they have a cause which necessitates their existence by its very essence, as their later followers, such as Ibn Sīnā and others, say. They do not affirm that these spheres belong to a Lord who created the heavens, the earth, and everything between them in six days, nor that He created things by His will and power. They also deny that He knows particulars: either they deny His knowledge altogether, as Aristotle does, or they say that, concerning changing things, He knows only their universals, as Ibn Sīnā does. In reality, this position amounts to denying His knowledge of those things.

For everything that exists in external reality is an individual particular. Each individual celestial sphere is a particular, as are all concrete entities, their attributes, and their actions. Whoever knows only universals knows none of the things that actually exist. Universals exist as universals only in the mind, not in concrete reality.

These people are discussed at length elsewhere, in “Radd ta‘ārud al-‘aql wa-l-naql” (Refuting the Conflict between Reason and Revelation) and other works. Their unbelief is greater than that of the Jews and Christians, and even that of the Arab polytheists. All these groups affirm that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and that He brought created beings into existence by His will and power. Aristotle and other philosophers like him

and the Greeks worshipped the celestial bodies and idols. They had no knowledge of the angels and prophets, and Aristotle’s books contain no mention of any of these. Their learning was chiefly concerned with natural phenomena. As for divine matters, each of them was seldom right and frequently wrong. Even after abrogation and alteration, the Jews and Christians know far more about divine matters than they do. Their later followers, however, such as Ibn Sīnā, sought to patch together their predecessors’ teachings and what the Messengers had brought. They borrowed elements from the principles of the Jahmiyyah and the Muʿtazilah and constructed a doctrine to which philosophers belonging to religious communities may profess allegiance. It contains errors and contradictions, some of which we have pointed out elsewhere.

When these thinkers saw that the mission of Messengers such as Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—had dazzled the world, acknowledged that the law with which Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was sent was the greatest law ever to reach the world, and found that the prophets had spoken of angels and jinn, they sought to reconcile all this with the teachings of their Greek predecessors. Yet those predecessors were the furthest of all people from knowing Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day.

Those predecessors affirmed ten intellects, which they called “immaterial entities” and “separate entities.” This notion was originally derived from the soul’s separation from the body. They called these entities “separate” because they are separate from matter and free of it. They also affirmed the celestial spheres, assigning a soul to each sphere. Most of them regarded these souls as accidents, while some regarded them as substances. Upon examination, these “immaterial entities” which they affirmed amount to things

that exist in the mind, not in external reality, just as Plato’s followers posited “abstract Platonic Forms.” They posited matter abstracted from form, and abstract duration and void. Their most accomplished thinkers acknowledged that these exist only in the mind, not in external reality.

When their later followers, such as Ibn Sīnā, sought to establish prophethood on their corrupt principles, they claimed that prophethood has three distinctive characteristics, and that whoever possesses them is a prophet.

The first is that he possesses an intellectual faculty, which they call the “sacred faculty,” through which he acquires knowledge without instruction.

The second is that he possesses an imaginative faculty that presents to him in images what he apprehends intellectually within himself. Thus, he sees forms within himself or hears sounds within himself, just as a sleeper sees and hears, although these have no external existence. They claimed that those forms are Allah’s angels and those sounds are the speech of Allah Most High.

The third is that he possesses an active faculty through which he influences the matter of the world. They reduced the miracles of the prophets, the extraordinary gifts bestowed upon Allah’s righteous servants, and the extraordinary feats of sorcerers to powers of the soul. Thus, they acknowledged those that accorded with their principles, such as turning a staff into a serpent, but not the splitting of the moon and the like, for they deny that such things occurred.

translated_text:
We have discussed these people at length in several places. We have explained that their claims are utterly unsound; that ordinary individuals and followers of the prophets attain things greater than what they have designated as distinctive characteristics; and that the angels described by the messengers are living, speaking beings, the greatest of Allah’s creatures. They are numerous, as Allah Most High says:

“And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him.”

They are not ten in number, nor are they accidents. These people, moreover, claim that the first emanation is the “First Intellect,” from which everything beneath it emanated, and that the “Tenth Active Intellect” is the lord of everything below the lunar sphere. The falsity of all this is known by necessity from the religion of the messengers: no angel is the originator of everything other than Allah.

These people claim that this is the intellect mentioned in a report which states:

“When Allah first created the intellect, He said to it, ‘Come forward,’ and it came forward. Then He said to it, ‘Go back,’ and it went back. Then He said, ‘By My might, I have created nothing more honoured in My sight than you. Through you I take, and through you I give. Yours is the reward, and upon you is the punishment.’”

They also call it “the Pen,” citing the hadith beginning, “When Allah first created the Pen,” narrated by al-Tirmidhī.

The report they mention concerning the intellect is a lie, fabricated according to the hadith experts, as stated by Abū Hātim al-Bustī, al-Dāraqutnī, Ibn al-Jawzī and others. It does not appear in any of the authoritative hadith collections. Yet even so,

its wording, if authentic, would constitute evidence against them. For it reads: “When Allah Most High first created the intellect, He said to it”—or, according to another version, “When Allah created the intellect, He said to it.” The report thus means that He addressed it at the very beginning of its creation, not that it was the first of all created things. The word awwal (“first”) is in the accusative as an adverb of time, corresponding to lammā (“when”) in the other wording.

The report continues: “I have created nothing more honoured in My sight than you.” This implies that He had created other things before it. He then said: “Through you I take, and through you I give. Yours is the reward, and upon you is the punishment.” Thus, He mentioned four kinds of accidents, whereas they maintain that all the substances of the upper and lower worlds emanated from that intellect. How far apart these two accounts are!

Their error arises because the word “intellect” in Muslim usage does not mean what it means in the usage of these Greeks. In Muslim usage, ʿaql (“reasoning”) is the verbal noun of ʿaqala, yaʿqilu (“to reason”), as in the Quran:

“And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’”

“Indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.”

“Have they not travelled through the land, so that they may have hearts with which to reason, or ears with which to hear?”

“Intellect” also denotes the innate faculty Allah Most High has placed in human beings by which they reason. For those people, however, the intellect is a self-subsisting substance, like a being endowed with intellect. This does not accord with the language of the messengers and the Quran.

As Abū Hāmid relates, their “realm of creation” is the realm of bodies, while he calls the intellect and souls the “realm of command.” The intellect may also be called the realm of jabarūt (supreme power), souls the realm of malakūt (dominion), and bodies

These people mislead Muslims in many ways. For example, they describe the “celestial sphere” as “originated,” meaning merely that it is caused, even though they consider it eternal. Yet whatever is originated must have been preceded by nonexistence. Neither in Arabic nor in any other language is something eternal and without beginning called originated. Allah has declared that He is the Creator of everything. Everything created is originated, and everything originated comes into existence after not having existed.

However, the speculative theologians among the Jahmiyyah and Muʿtazilah debated them inadequately: they neither properly understood what the messengers had conveyed nor rigorously established the conclusions of reason. Thus, they neither championed Islam nor defeated its enemies. They shared some of those people’s false premises while disputing some of their sound rational conclusions. Their shortcomings in knowledge derived from revelation and reason therefore helped strengthen the others’ misguidance, as has been explained at length elsewhere.

These philosophers sometimes identify “Gabriel” with the image that takes shape within the soul of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while imagination is subordinate to the intellect. Then came heretics who shared the views of these heretical philosophers and claimed to be “friends of Allah,” that Allah’s friends are superior to His prophets, and that they receive directly from Allah without an intermediary. Among them was Ibn ʿArabī, author of al-Futūhāt and al-Fusūs, who said:

that he draws from the same source as the angel who conveys revelation to the Messenger. By “source” he means the intellect, and by “angel” he means imagination. Imagination is subordinate to the intellect. He claims to receive from that which is the origin of imagination, whereas the Messenger receives from imagination. Thus, in his own estimation, he ranks above the Prophet.

Even if a prophet’s distinctive quality were what they describe, he would not belong to the same category, let alone rank above him. How much less so when what they describe is attainable by individual believers, whereas prophethood lies beyond that! Although Ibn ʿArabī and his like claim to be Sufis, they are Sufis among the heretical philosophers, not Sufis among the people of knowledge, let alone masters of those who adhere to the Book and Sunnah, such as al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyād, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī, Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, al-Junayd ibn Muhammad, Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī, and their like—may Allah be pleased with them all.

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has described the angels in His Book in terms that contradict these people’s claims. For example, the Exalted says:

“They say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken offspring.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants.”

“They do not precede Him in speech, and they act at His command.”

“He knows what is before them and what is behind them. They intercede only for those He approves, and they stand in reverent fear of Him.”

“Whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ We will repay him with Hell. Thus do We repay the wrongdoers.”

The Exalted also says:

“How many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing except after Allah has given permission to whom He wills and approves.”

And the Exalted says: “Say, ‘Call upon

those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. They possess not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.’”

“Intercession is of no benefit with Him except for one to whom He gives permission.”

The Exalted also says:

“To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and on earth. Those who are with Him are neither too proud to worship Him nor do they grow weary.”

“They glorify Him night and day, without ceasing.”

He has related that the angels came to Abraham, peace be upon him, in human form, and that the angel appeared to Mary as a man, perfectly formed. Gabriel, peace be upon him, would come to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the form of Dihyah al-Kalbī and in the form of a Bedouin, and people would see them in these forms.

Allah Most High has described Gabriel, peace be upon him, as possessing strength, holding an honoured position with the Lord of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy. He has stated that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw him on the clear horizon. He also described him as:

“Mighty in power,
possessed of strength. He stood poised
on the highest horizon.
Then he drew near and came down,
until he was two bow-lengths away or nearer.
Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed.
The heart did not deny what it saw.
Will you then dispute with him about what he sees?
And he certainly saw him on another descent,
by the lote tree of the utmost boundary,
near which is the Garden of Refuge,
when the lote tree was covered by whatever covered it.
His sight neither strayed nor exceeded its bounds.
He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.”

translated_text:
It is established in the two Sahīh collections, on the authority of ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created only twice.” This means the first occasion on the highest horizon and the other descent by the lote tree of the utmost boundary.

Elsewhere, Allah describes Gabriel, peace be upon him, as the Trustworthy Spirit and the Holy Spirit, among other attributes which make clear that he is among the greatest of Allah Most High’s living, intelligent creatures, and that he is a substance subsisting in his own right—not an image in the Prophet’s mind, as claimed by these heretical philosophers and those who claim to be friends of Allah and more knowledgeable than the prophets.

Ultimately, their position amounts to denying the “foundations of faith”: belief in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day. In reality, their position is a denial of the Creator, for they have identified the existence of creation with the existence of the Creator, saying, “Existence is one.” They have failed to distinguish between numerical unity and unity of kind. Existing things share in what is denoted by existence, just as human beings share in what is denoted by humanity, and animals in what is denoted by animal. Yet this shared universal exists as a shared universal only in the mind. In actual reality, the animal nature subsisting in this human being is not the animal nature subsisting in a horse, and the existence of the heavens is not the very same existence as that of a human being. Thus, the existence of the Creator—majestic is His glory—is not like the existence of His creatures.

translated_text:
In essence, their position is that of Pharaoh, who denied the Creator. He did not deny the reality we witness, but claimed that it exists of itself and has no maker. These people agreed with him on this, but claimed that it is Allah. They were therefore more astray than he was, even though the falsity of his position was more obvious than theirs. Accordingly, they maintained that idol worshippers worshipped none but Allah, saying:

“Since Pharaoh held the position of command and wielded the sword, even if he was unjust by the standards of religious law, he accordingly said, ‘I am your lord most high’—meaning: although all are lords in some respect, I am higher than you by virtue of the outward authority I have been given over you.”

They said:

“When the sorcerers recognized that Pharaoh had spoken truthfully, they acknowledged this and said, ‘So decree whatever you will decree; you can only decree concerning this worldly life.’ They said: Thus Pharaoh’s declaration, ‘I am your lord most high,’ was true, and Pharaoh was the Real Himself.”

They then denied the reality of the Last Day, claiming that the people of Hell enjoy bliss just as the people of Paradise do. Thus, they disbelieved in Allah, the Last Day, His angels, His Books, and His messengers, while claiming to be the very elite of the innermost circle of Allah’s friends. They also claimed to be superior to the prophets, and that the prophets derive their knowledge of Allah only from their light.

This is not the place to expound upon these people’s heresy. However, since the discussion concerns “the friends of Allah” and the distinction between “the friends of the Most Merciful and the friends of Satan,” and since these people are among the most emphatic in claiming friendship with Allah while being among Satan’s closest allies, we have drawn attention to this. For this reason, most of their discourse concerns states

of a satanic nature. They speak as the author of al-Futūhāt does in his chapter on “The Land of Reality,” which they call the land of imagination.

It thus becomes clear that the reality he discusses is imagination and a realm in which Satan operates, for Satan makes people imagine things to be other than they really are. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever turns a blind eye to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil who becomes his companion.”

“They certainly turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided.”

“Until, when he comes to Us, he says, ‘Would that there were between me and you the distance between east and west! What an evil companion!’”

“Today, since you did wrong, it will not benefit you that you share in the punishment.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whomever He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed strayed far astray.”

Up to His words:

“He makes them promises and fills them with false hopes, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Satan will say when the matter has been decided, ‘Allah made you a true promise. I too made you promises, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot rescue you, nor can you rescue me. I disavow your having previously associated me with Allah. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and said, ‘No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector.’ But when the two forces came within sight of one another, he turned on his heels and said, ‘I have nothing to do with you. I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.’”

It has been related from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in an authentic hadith

that “he saw Gabriel marshaling the angels.”

When the devils see Allah’s angels, with whom He supports His servants, they flee from them. Allah supports His believing servants with His angels. Allah Most High says:

“When your Lord revealed to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who believe.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“O you who believe, remember Allah’s favor upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see.”

Allah Most High also says:

“When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with armies you did not see.”

Allah Most High also says:

“When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?’”

“Yes indeed! If you remain steadfast and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels bearing marks of distinction.”

These people, however, are visited by spirits that speak to them and appear before them. They are jinn and devils, yet these people imagine them to be angels—like the spirits that speak to those who worship the heavenly bodies and idols.

Among the first of these people to appear in Islam was al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd, whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, foretold in the authentic hadith recorded by Muslim in his Sahīh. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There will be among Thaqīf a liar and a destroyer.”

The liar was al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd, and the destroyer was al-Hajjāj ibn Yūsuf.

Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās were told, “Al-Mukhtār claims that something descends to him.” They both replied, “He has spoken the truth. Allah Most High says:

‘Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?’

‘They descend upon every sinful liar.’”

al-Mukhtār claimed to receive revelation, he replied, “Allah Most High says:

‘Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you.’”

The spirit from which the author of al-Futūhāt claims to have received that book is one of these satanic spirits. Thus, he describes various forms of seclusion involving particular foods and other specified things. Such practices open the way for those who undertake them to communicate with the jinn and devils. They imagine this to be among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s righteous servants, whereas it is nothing but satanic states. I know a number of these people. Some would be carried through the air to distant places and brought back. Others would receive stolen property, which the devils stole and brought to them. Others would be shown where stolen property was, in return for a fee they received from people or a gift people gave them when they directed them to their stolen possessions, and similar things.

Since these people’s states were satanic, they opposed the messengers—may Allah Most High bless them and grant them peace—as can be seen in the writings of the author of al-Futūhāt al-Makkiyya and al-Fusūs, and similar works. He praises disbelievers such as the peoples of Noah and Hūd, Pharaoh, and others, while disparaging prophets such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Aaron. He censures Muslim shaykhs whom Muslims hold in esteem, such as al-Junayd ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Abd Allāh al-Tustarī, while praising those whom Muslims condemn, such as al-Hallāj and others like him, as he recounts in his imaginary, satanic visions. and he replied: “Affirming Allah’s oneness means distinguishing what has a beginning from what is eternal.” He thus explained that affirming Allah’s oneness means distinguishing the Eternal from what has been brought into being, and the Creator from creation. The author of al-Fusūs rejected this, saying in his imaginary, satanic conversation with him: “O Junayd, can anyone distinguish what has been brought into being from the Eternal unless he is other than both?”

He therefore declared al-Junayd mistaken for saying, “Distinguishing what has a beginning from what is eternal,” because his own position is that the existence of what has been brought into being is identical with the existence of the Eternal. As he says in his Fusūs:

“Among His Most Beautiful Names is ‘the Most High.’ Above whom, when none exists but He? And beyond what, when there is nothing but He? His exaltedness is therefore in relation to Himself, and He is the very reality of all existing things. Thus, those called originated things are exalted by virtue of His essence and are none other than He.”

He goes on to say:

“He is the very reality of what is hidden and the very reality of what is manifest. There is none who sees Him but He, and none who speaks of Him but He. He is the one called Abū Sa‘īd al-Kharrāz and by other names that have come into being.”

This heretic should be told: Someone who distinguishes between two things in knowledge and speech need not be a third entity, other than both. Every person distinguishes between himself and others without being a third entity. The servant knows that he is a servant and distinguishes between himself and his Creator. The Creator—exalted is His majesty—distinguishes between Himself and His creatures and knows that He is their Lord and that they are His servants, as the Quran declares in numerous places. He replied, “The entire Quran is polytheism; only our teachings affirm Allah’s oneness.”

He was asked, “If existence is one, why is a wife lawful and a sister forbidden?”

He replied, “To us, all is lawful. But these veiled people said, ‘It is forbidden,’ so we said, ‘It is forbidden to you.’”

Besides its enormous unbelief, this is plainly self-contradictory. If existence is one, who is veiled, and who imposes the veil?

Thus, one of their shaykhs said to his disciple, “Whoever tells you that anything other than Allah exists in the universe has lied.”

His disciple replied, “Then who is it that lies?”

They told another person, “These are loci of manifestation.”

He asked them, “Are the loci of manifestation other than that which is manifest, or are they identical? If they are other, you have affirmed a relation; if they are identical, there is no distinction.”

Elsewhere, we have discussed at length the exposure of these people’s secrets and explained the true nature of each one’s position. We explained that the author of al-Fusūs holds that the nonexistent is a thing and that the existence of the Real governs it. He thus distinguishes between existence and subsistence.

The Mu‘tazilites who said that the nonexistent is a thing subsisting outside the mind, despite their misguidance, are better than he is. They said that the Lord created, for these things subsisting in nonexistence, an existence distinct from His own. These people may not deliberately lie. Rather, they imagine things that exist within their own minds and suppose that they exist externally. They also see things that do exist externally, but suppose them to be miraculous gifts granted to the righteous, when they are actually deceptions wrought by devils.

These advocates of oneness may place the saints above the prophets and maintain that prophethood has not ceased, as is reported of Ibn Sab‘īn and others. They posit “three” levels, saying: “The servant first witnesses obedience and disobedience, then obedience without disobedience, then neither obedience nor disobedience.”

The “first witnessing” is the correct one: distinguishing between acts of obedience and acts of disobedience. By the “second witnessing,” however, they mean witnessing divine decree. Thus, one of them says: “I disbelieve in a Lord who is disobeyed.” This person claims that disobedience means opposing the divine will—that is, what Allah wills to occur. All created beings are subject to the rule of this will. Their poet says:

“I have become subject to whatever You choose for me;
thus all my deeds are acts of obedience.”

It is well known that this contradicts what Allah sent His messengers with and revealed in His Books. For the disobedience that makes a person deserving of blame and punishment consists in opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger. As the Exalted says:

“These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain there forever. That is the great triumph.”

“And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, to remain there forever, and he will have a humiliating punishment.”

We shall explain the difference between the universal will and the religious will, and between the universal command and the religious command. This “question” had confused a group of Sufis, so al-Junayd—may Allah have mercy on him—clarified it for them. Whoever followed al-Junayd in this was on the right course, while whoever opposed him went astray. They had been discussing how all things occur through Allah’s will and power, and the witnessing of this oneness, which they call the “first unification.” Al-Junayd explained to them that one must also witness the “second distinction”: while witnessing that all things share in being subject to Allah’s will, power, and creation, one must distinguish between what He commands, loves, and is pleased with, and what He forbids, dislikes, and is displeased with. One must also distinguish between His allies and His enemies. As the Exalted says:

“Shall We then treat those who submit to Allah like the criminals?”

“What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”

And the Exalted says:

“Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?”

And the Exalted says: “Or

do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and death? How evil is their judgment!”

And the Exalted says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to those who do evil. How little you take heed!”

Thus, the position of the early generations of this community and its leading scholars was that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. Whatever He wills occurs, and whatever He does not will does not occur. There is no Lord besides Him. Nevertheless, He commands obedience and forbids disobedience. He does not love corruption, does not approve of disbelief for His servants, and does not command indecency. Although it occurs by His will, He neither loves nor approves of it; rather, He hates it, censures those who commit it, and punishes them.

As for the “third rank”—in which one witnesses neither obedience nor disobedience—a person at this rank regards existence as one. They consider this the ultimate realization and friendship with Allah. In reality, however, it is the utmost deviation concerning Allah’s names and signs, and the utmost enmity towards Allah. For whoever adopts this perspective takes Jews, Christians, and all other disbelievers as allies, whereas the Exalted has said:

“Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them.”

He does not disavow polytheism and idols, and thus departs from the religion of Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says:

“You have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disown you and whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.’”

And Allah’s intimate friend said—upon him

translated_text:
Thus He stated that the heavens and the earth—and, elsewhere, “whatever is between them”—are created and glorify Him. He, glory be to Him, also declared that He knows everything. As for His words, “He is with you,” the word “with” does not, in Arabic, imply that one of two things is intermingled with the other. For example, the Most High says:

“Fear Allah and be with the truthful.”

And the Most High says:

“Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers.”

And the Most High says:

“And those who believed afterwards, emigrated, and strove alongside you—they are of you.”

The word “with” occurs in the Quran in both a general and a specific sense. The general sense appears in this verse and in the verse of Sūrat al-Mujādilah:

“Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? No three converse in secret without Him being their fourth, nor five without Him being their sixth, nor fewer than that nor more without Him being with them wherever they may be. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah has knowledge of all things.”

He began the passage with knowledge and ended it with knowledge. Hence Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Dahhāk, Sufyān al-Thawrī, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: He is with them through His knowledge.

As for His being with particular people in a specific sense, this appears in the words of the Most High:

“Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good.”

And in His words to Moses:

“Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.”

And the Most High says:

“When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us.’”

This refers to the Prophet

—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Thus, He is with Moses and Aaron, but not Pharaoh; with Muhammad and his companion, but not Abū Jahl and His other enemies; and with those who fear Him and those who do good, but not the unjust aggressors. If “being with” meant that He Himself is everywhere, the specific and general statements would contradict one another. Rather, it means that He is with these people through His help and support, but not with those others.

As for the words of the Most High:

“It is He who is God in heaven and God on earth,”

they mean that He is the God of those in the heavens and those on earth, as Allah Most High says:

“To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

Likewise, His words:

“And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth,”

mean that He is the One worshipped in the heavens and on earth, as explained by the leading scholars, including Imam Ahmad and others.

The early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars unanimously agreed that the Lord Most High is distinct from His creation. He is described as He described Himself and as His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—described Him, without distorting or denying His attributes, specifying how they are, or likening them to those of creation. He is described with attributes of perfection, not attributes of deficiency, and it is known that nothing is like Him in His attributes of perfection. As Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘He is Allah, the One;
Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
He neither begets nor is born,
and there is none comparable to Him.’”

Ibn ‘Abbās said: “Al-Samad is the All-Knowing, whose knowledge is perfect; the Magnificent, whose magnificence is perfect; the All-Powerful, whose power is perfect; the All-Wise, whose wisdom is perfect; the Master, whose mastery is perfect.

translated_text:
And Ibn Mas‘ūd and others said: “He is the One who has no hollow interior.” Al-Ahad (the One) is He who has no equal. His name al-Samad affirms that He possesses the attributes of perfection and is free of all deficiencies, while His name al-Ahad affirms that nothing is like Him. We have discussed this at length in our commentary on this surah and our explanation of how it equals one-third of the Quran.

Section

Many people confuse the realities pertaining to divine command, religion, and faith with those pertaining to creation, divine decree, and the cosmic order. For creation and command belong to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, as He Most High says:

“Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He brings the night as a covering over the day, pursuing it swiftly. The sun, the moon, and the stars are subject to His command. Surely, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.”

He, glorified is He, is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything. There is no creator besides Him and no lord other than Him. Whatever He wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. Every movement and every state of rest in existence occurs through His decree, ordainment, will, power, and creation.

He, glorified is He, has commanded obedience to Himself and His messengers and forbidden disobedience to Himself and His messengers. He has commanded that He alone be worshipped and that worship be devoted sincerely to Him, and He has forbidden associating partners with Allah. Thus, the greatest of good deeds is

worshipping Allah alone, and the greatest evil is associating partners with Him.

Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills.”

He Most High also says:

“Among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Ibn Mas‘ūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?’ He said, ‘To set up a rival to Allah when He is the One who created you.’ I asked, ‘Then which?’ He said, ‘To kill your child for fear that he will share your food.’ I asked, ‘Then which?’ He said, ‘To commit adultery with your neighbour’s wife.’ Allah then revealed in confirmation of this:

‘And those who do not invoke another god besides Allah, nor kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden to be killed, except by right, nor commit adultery. Whoever does so will face a penalty. The punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will remain in it forever, humiliated—except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’”

He, glorified is He, has commanded justice, excellence in doing good, and giving to relatives, and has forbidden indecency, wrongdoing, and oppression. He has declared that He loves those who fear Him, those who do good, those who act justly, those who repeatedly repent, those who purify themselves, and those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a firmly joined structure.

He detests what He has forbidden, as He says in Surah Subhān:

“The evil of all these things is detested by your Lord.”

He has forbidden associating partners with Him and mistreating parents, and has commanded that relatives be given their due rights

and has forbidden squandering and stinginess, keeping one’s hand shackled to one’s neck, and stretching it out without restraint. He has forbidden killing a soul without right, adultery, and approaching an orphan’s property except in the best manner, until He says:

“The evil of all these things is detested by your Lord.”

He, glorified is He, does not love corruption, nor does He approve of disbelief for His servants.

The servant is commanded to turn continually to Allah Most High in repentance. Allah Most High says:

“Turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, so that you may succeed.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“O people, turn to your Lord in repentance. By Him in whose hand is my soul, I seek Allah’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.”

In Sahīh Muslim, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“A cloud comes over my heart, and I seek Allah’s forgiveness a hundred times a day.”

In the Sunan collections, Ibn ‘Umar said:

“In a single gathering, we would count the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying a hundred times—or he said, more than a hundred times—‘My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.’”

Allah, glorified is He, has commanded His servants to conclude their righteous deeds by seeking forgiveness. Thus, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had pronounced the salutation ending the prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say:

“O Allah, You are Peace, and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honour.”

as is established in an authentic hadith from him. Allah Most High has said:

“And those who seek forgiveness before dawn.”

Thus, He commanded them to stand in prayer at night and seek forgiveness before dawn. Likewise, He concluded Sūrat al-Muzzammil, the surah concerning night prayer, with His words:

“And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Likewise, He said concerning the Hajj:

“When you depart from ‘Arafāt, remember Allah at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, although before that you were among those astray.”

“Then depart from where the people depart, and seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Indeed, towards the end, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, undertook the expedition to Tabūk—his last military expedition—Allah, glorified and exalted is He, revealed:

“Allah has certainly turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had almost swerved. Then He turned to them in mercy. Indeed, He is Most Kind and Most Merciful to them.”

“And to the three who were left behind, until the earth, despite its vastness, became confining to them, and their own souls became a burden to them, and they knew that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.”

It was the last of the Quran to be revealed. It has also been said that the last surah revealed was His saying:

“When Allah’s help and victory come,
and you see people entering Allah’s religion in multitudes,
then glorify your Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever the Accepter of Repentance.”

Thus, Allah Most High commanded him to conclude his deeds by glorifying Him and seeking forgiveness. In the two Sahīh collections, ‘Ā’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would

say when bowing and prostrating:

“Glory and praise be to You, O Allah, our Lord. O Allah, forgive me”—thus putting the Quran into practice.

It is also reported in the two Sahīh collections that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say:

“O Allah, forgive my sins, my ignorance, my excesses in my affairs, and whatever You know better than I do. O Allah, forgive what I have done in jest and in earnest, inadvertently and deliberately—and I am guilty of all of these. O Allah, forgive what I have done before and what I have yet to do, what I have concealed and what I have made public. There is no god but You.”

In the two Sahīh collections, Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to recite in my prayer.” He replied:

“Say: ‘O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and none forgives sins but You. So grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. Indeed, You are the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.’”

In the Sunan collections, Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to recite in the morning and evening.” He replied:

“Say: ‘O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I testify that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul, from the evil of Satan and his incitement to associate partners with You, and from committing evil against myself or bringing it upon another Muslim.’ Say this in the morning, in the evening, and when you go to bed.”

No one, then, should imagine that they have no need to repent to Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins. Rather, everyone constantly needs this.

Allah, Blessed and Most High, said:

“But it was undertaken by

man. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.”

“So that Allah may punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, and turn in mercy to the believers, men and women. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Man is unjust and ignorant, and the highest attainment of believing men and women is repentance. Allah Most High has told us in His Book of the repentance of His righteous servants and His forgiveness of them.

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one will enter Paradise by his deeds.” They asked, “Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “Not even me, unless Allah envelops me in mercy and bounty from Him.”

This does not contradict His words:

“Eat and drink with pleasure for what you did in days gone by.”

For the Messenger negated the sense of exchange and equivalence conveyed by the preposition bi (“by”), whereas the Quran affirmed its causal sense.

As for the saying, “When Allah loves a servant, sins do not harm him,” it means that when Allah loves a servant, He inspires him to repent and seek forgiveness, so that he does not persist in sin. Whoever thinks that sins do not harm someone who persists in them is misguided, opposing the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations and the imams. Rather, whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. His praiseworthy servants are none other than those mentioned in His words, Most High:

“And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing.”

“Those who spend in prosperity and adversity, restrain their anger, and pardon others—and Allah loves those who do good.”

“And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves,

remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and do not knowingly persist in what they have done.”

Whoever thinks that “divine decree” is an excuse for sinners is like the polytheists of whom Allah Most High said:

“Those who associate partners with Allah will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

Allah Most High said in reply to them:

“Likewise, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.’”

“Say, ‘To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.’”

If “divine decree” were an excuse for anyone, Allah would not have punished those who rejected the messengers, such as the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the overturned cities, and the people of Pharaoh. Nor would He have commanded that the prescribed punishments be carried out upon transgressors. No one invokes divine decree as an excuse unless he is following his desires without guidance from Allah.

Whoever regards divine decree as an excuse that absolves sinners of blame and punishment must neither blame nor punish anyone who wrongs him. Rather, he must regard whatever brings pleasure and whatever brings pain as equal, making no distinction between someone who treats him well and someone who treats him badly. Human nature, reason, and divine law all rule this out.

Allah Most High has said:

“Should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat the God-fearing like the wicked?”

Some have said that Adam prevailed over Moses in argument only because he was his father, because he had repented, because the sin occurred under one revealed law while the blame was expressed under another, or because this applies in this world but not in the Hereafter. All of this is false.

Rather, the meaning of the hadith is that Moses, peace be upon him, blamed his father only for the calamity that had befallen them because he ate from the tree. He said to him, “Why did you cause us and yourself to be expelled from Paradise?” He did not blame him merely for having committed a sin and then repented of it. Moses knew that someone who repents of a sin is not to be blamed, and he too had repented. Had Adam believed that divine decree absolved him of blame, he would not have said:

“Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.”

The believer is commanded to be patient and submit when calamities strike, and to seek forgiveness and repent when he sins. Allah Most High said:

“So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin.”

Thus, He commanded him to endure calamities patiently and seek forgiveness for his faults.

And He Most High said:

“No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.”

Ibn Masʿūd said: “This is a man whom calamity strikes, who knows that it is from Allah, and so is content and submits.”

“Patience” is obligatory by scholarly consensus. Higher than this is contentment with Allah’s decree. Some have held that “contentment” is obligatory, while others have held that it is recommended, which is the correct view. Higher still is to thank Allah for the calamity, recognizing His favor in making it a means of expiating one’s sins, raising one’s rank, turning back to Him, humbly beseeching Him, and sincerely placing one’s trust and hope in Him rather than in created beings.

As for people of transgression and misguidance, you find them invoking divine decree as an excuse when they sin and follow their desires, yet attributing good deeds to themselves when Allah blesses them with them. As some scholars have said: “When you obey, you are a Qadarī; when you sin, a Jabrī. Whatever doctrine suits your desires, you adopt.”

When people of guidance and sound judgment perform a good deed, they recognize Allah’s favor upon them in it: He is the One who blessed them, made them Muslims, enabled them to establish prayer, and inspired them with piety. They recognize that there is neither might nor power except through Him. Through this recognition of divine decree, they are freed from self-admiration, reproachful reminders of their favors, and hurtful conduct. When they commit a sin, they seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him for it.

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Shaddād ibn Aws reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best supplication for forgiveness is for the servant to say: ‘O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me

for none forgives sins but You.’ Whoever says this in the morning with firm conviction in it, then dies that night, will enter Paradise.”

In an authentic hadith, Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, narrated from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, that He said:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins and do not mind doing so. So seek My forgiveness, and I will forgive you.

“O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed. So ask Me for food, and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I clothe. So ask Me for clothing, and I will clothe you. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide. So seek My guidance, and I will guide you.

“O My servants, you will never be able to harm Me, nor will you ever be able to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, were all as pious at heart as the most pious person among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, were all as wicked at heart as the most wicked person among you, that would diminish My dominion in no way.

“O My servants, if the first and last of you, humans and jinn alike, gathered on a single plain and asked of Me, and I gave each person what he asked for, that would diminish what I possess no more than a single dip of a needle diminishes the sea.

“O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then recompense you for in full. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame no one but himself.”

Thus He, glorified be He, commands the servant to praise Allah for whatever good he finds, and to blame no one but himself if he finds evil.

Many people speak in the language of “reality” without distinguishing between the reality of creation and divine decree, which concerns His creation and will, and the reality of religion and divine command, which concerns His pleasure and love. Nor do they distinguish between someone who adheres to religious reality in accordance with what Allah commanded through His messengers, and someone who follows his own spiritual experience and inward perception without assessing them against the Quran and Sunnah.

Likewise, many people use the term “Sharia” without distinguishing between the law revealed by Allah Most High—the Quran and Sunnah with which Allah sent His Messenger—and the law embodied in a judge’s ruling. No created being is permitted to depart from the revealed law, and none departs from it except a disbeliever. A judge, however, sometimes rules correctly and sometimes errs.

This is when he is knowledgeable and just. Otherwise, it is reported in the Sunan collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There are three kinds of judges: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knows the truth and judges accordingly is in Paradise. A man who judges people’s cases in ignorance is in the Fire. And a man who knows the truth but rules contrary to it is in the Fire.”

The finest of all knowledgeable and just judges is the foremost of Adam’s descendants, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is authentically reported from him in the two Sahīh collections that he said:

“You bring your disputes before me, and some of you may present their arguments more eloquently than others. I judge only on the basis of what I hear. So whoever

Thus, the foremost of creation explained that if he gives a judgment based on what he has heard, while the actual facts are otherwise, the person in whose favour he rules may not take what he has been awarded: he is only assigning him a piece of the Fire. The scholars agree on this concerning cases of outright ownership. If a judge rules on the basis of what he considers legally valid proof, such as witness testimony or an admission, while the actual facts differ from what appears outwardly, the person in whose favour he rules may not take what he has been awarded, by scholarly agreement. If he rules on contracts and annulments on a similar basis, most scholars hold that the same applies. This is the position of Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Abū Hanīfa, may Allah be pleased with him, distinguished between the two categories.

Thus, when the terms “religious law” and “Sharia” mean the Quran and Sunnah, neither any of Allah’s allies nor anyone else may depart from them. Whoever thinks that any of Allah’s allies has a path to Allah other than following Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, inwardly and outwardly, and does not follow him inwardly and outwardly, is a disbeliever.

Whoever invokes the account of Moses and al-Khidr to support this is mistaken on two counts.

The first is that Moses was not sent to al-Khidr, nor was al-Khidr obliged to follow him, for Moses was sent to the Children of Israel. As for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his message encompasses both kinds of accountable beings, jinn and humans; and even if

Making a hole in the ship and then repairing it, for the benefit of its owners and out of fear that the oppressor would seize it, was an act of kindness towards them, and that is permissible. Killing an assailant is permissible, even if he is a minor. Someone who cannot be prevented from leading his parents into disbelief except by being killed may be killed.

When Najda al-Harūrī asked Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, about killing boys, he told him: “If you know about them what al-Khidr knew about that boy, then kill them; otherwise, do not kill them.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.

As for showing kindness to an orphan without compensation and patiently enduring hunger, these are righteous deeds. Thus, none of this contravened Allah’s religious law.

: بَيْنَ الْكَوْنِيِّ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُ وَقَدَّرَهُ وَقَضَاهُ؛ وَإِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَأْمُرْ بِهِ وَلَا يُحِبُّهُ وَلَا يُثِيبُ أَصْحَابَهُ وَلَا يَجْعَلُهُمْ مِنْ أَوْلِيَائِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ وَبَيْنَ الدِّينِيِّ الَّذِي أَمَرَ بِهِ وَشَرَعَهُ وَأَثَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَكْرَمَهُمْ وَجَعَلَهُمْ مِنْ أَوْلِيَائِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ

Sa‘d, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, Ishāq, Dāwūd and others. Their opinions must be supported by evidence from the Quran and Sunnah. Following another’s opinion on his authority is permissible where doing so is allowed. That is, following any one of them is not obligatory upon the entire Muslim community as following the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is obligatory. Nor is following any one of them on his authority forbidden, as following someone who speaks without knowledge is forbidden.

If, however, someone adds to the religious law something that does not belong to it, such as fabricated hadiths, or interprets the texts contrary to Allah’s intent, or does anything similar, this constitutes alteration. One must therefore distinguish between revealed religious law, interpreted religious law and altered religious law, just as one distinguishes between the reality of the created order and the religious reality pertaining to divine commands, and between what is substantiated by the Quran and Sunnah and what relies solely on an individual’s spiritual experience and ecstasy.

Section

In His Book, Allah has distinguished, with regard to “will,” “command,” “decree,” “permission,” “prohibition,” “raising up,” “sending,” “speech” and “making,” between what pertains to the created order—which He creates, determines and decrees, even though He has not commanded it, does not love it, does not reward those who do it and does not make them His pious allies—and what pertains to religion, which He commands and prescribes, for which He rewards people, honours them and makes them His pious allies

and members of His successful party and His victorious army. This is among the greatest distinctions by which Allah’s allies are distinguished from His enemies. Whoever the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, employs in what He loves and is pleased with, and who dies in that state, is among His allies. Whoever devotes his deeds to what the Lord hates and dislikes, and dies in that state, is among His enemies.

Thus, the “will pertaining to the created order” is His will concerning all that He creates. All created things fall within His will pertaining to the created order. His will pertaining to religion, however, entails His love and pleasure and encompasses what He has commanded and established as religious law and religion. This is confined to faith and righteous deeds. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his heart tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky.”

Noah, peace be upon him, said to his people:

“My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if Allah wills to lead you astray.”

Allah Most High says:

“When Allah wills harm for a people, none can avert it, and they have no protector besides Him.”

Concerning the second kind of will, Allah Most High says:

“Whoever is ill or on a journey must fast an equal number of other days. Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you.”

He says in the verse concerning purification:

“Allah does not intend to impose hardship upon you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favour upon you, so that you may be grateful.”

After mentioning which marriages He has permitted and which He has forbidden, He says:

“Allah intends to make things clear to you, guide you to the ways of those before you, and accept your repentance. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

“Allah intends to accept your repentance, but those who follow their desires wish you to deviate far from the right path.”

“Allah intends to lighten your burden, for mankind was created weak.”

After mentioning what He commanded the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to do and what He forbade them, He says:

“Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O members of the household, and to purify you completely.”

The meaning is that He has commanded you, O members of the household, to do what removes impurity from you and purifies you completely. Whoever obeys His command is purified and has impurity removed from him, unlike whoever disobeys Him.

As for “command,” He says concerning the command pertaining to the created order:

“When We will something, all We say to it is, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

Allah Most High says:

“Our command is but a single command, like the blink of an eye.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Our command came upon it by night or by day, and We left it mown down, as though it had not flourished the day before.”

As for the command pertaining to religion, Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence, and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may take heed.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Indeed, Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent indeed is what Allah admonishes you to do. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.”

As for “permission,” He says concerning permission pertaining to the created order, when mentioning magic:

“They cannot harm anyone through it except by Allah’s permission.”

That is, by His will and power; otherwise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not permitted magic.

Concerning “permission pertaining to religion,” He says:

“Or do they have partners who have ordained for them in religion what Allah has not authorized?”

Allah Most High also says:

“Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner, and as one who calls to Allah by His permission.”

Allah Most High also says:

“We have sent no messenger except to be obeyed

by Allah’s permission.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah’s permission.”

As for “decree,” He says concerning the decree pertaining to the created order:

“He completed them as seven heavens in two days.”

He, glorified be He, also says:

“When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

Concerning the decree pertaining to religion, He says:

“Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him.”

That is, He has commanded this. It does not mean that He has predestined it, for others besides Him have indeed been worshipped, as He has stated in several places. For example, Allah Most High says:

“They worship besides Allah what can neither harm nor benefit them, and they say, ‘These are our intercessors with Allah.’”

And His intimate friend, peace be upon him, said to his people:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping—you and your forefathers? They are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.”

Allah Most High also says:

“You have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disassociate ourselves from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and enmity and hatred have arisen between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone’—except for Abraham’s words to his father, ‘I will certainly ask forgiveness for you, though I can do nothing to protect you from Allah.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“Say, ‘O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor do you worship what I worship. You have your religion, and I have mine.’”

This statement entails his disassociation from their religion; it does not entail his approval of it. Likewise, Allah Most High says in another verse:

“If they deny you, say, ‘I have my deeds, and you have yours. You are free of responsibility for what I do, and I am free of responsibility for what you do.’”

Any heretic who supposes that this signifies his approval of the disbelievers’ religion is among the most mendacious and disbelieving of people. The same applies to anyone who supposes that His words, “Your Lord has decreed,” mean “predestined,” that whatever Allah, glorified be He, decrees must occur, and thus claims that idol worshippers have worshipped none but Allah. Such a person is among the greatest disbelievers in the Scriptures.

As for “sending forth,” Allah Most High says concerning sending forth pertaining to the created order:

“When the first of the two promises came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours endowed with great might, who swept through your homes. It was a promise fulfilled.”

Concerning sending forth pertaining to religion, He says:

“It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves, reciting His verses to them, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.”

Allah Most High says:

“We certainly sent a messenger to every nation, saying, ‘Worship Allah and shun false gods.’”

As for “sending,” He says concerning sending pertaining to the created order:

“Do you not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, inciting them relentlessly?”

Allah Most High also says:

“It is He who sends the winds bearing glad tidings ahead of His mercy.”

Concerning sending pertaining to religion, He says:

“We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner.”

Allah Most High also says:

“We sent Noah to his people.”

Allah Most High also says:

“We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind.”

As for “making,” He says concerning that which pertains to the created order:

“We made them leaders calling

to the Fire.” Concerning that which pertains to religion, He says:

“For each of you We have appointed a law and a clear way.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Allah has not instituted any bahīrah, sā’ibah, wasīlah, or hām.”

As for “forbidding,” He says concerning that which pertains to the created order:

“We had already prevented him from nursing from any wet nurse.”

Allah Most High also says:

“It will be forbidden to them for forty years, during which they will wander through the land.”

Concerning that which pertains to religion, He says:

“Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Forbidden to you in marriage are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers’ daughters, and your sisters’ daughters,” to the end of the verse.

As for “words,” He says concerning words pertaining to the created order:

“She believed in the words of her Lord and His Scriptures.”

It is established in an authentic report that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

“I seek refuge in all of Allah’s perfect words from the evil of what He has created, from His wrath and punishment, from the evil of His servants, and from the promptings of the devils and their coming into my presence.”

He also said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever stops at a place and says, ‘I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words from the evil of what He has created,’ nothing will harm him until he leaves that place.”

He used to say:

“I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass, from the evil of what He has created in the earth, from the evil of what emerges from it, from the evil of the trials of night and day, and from the evil of everyone who comes by night, except one who comes with good, O
