“Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass” are those by which He brought all things into being. Neither the righteous nor the wicked can escape His creative act, His will, or His power. As for His “words pertaining to religion”—His revealed Books and the commands and prohibitions they contain—the righteous obey them, while the wicked disobey them. Allah’s pious allies are those who obey His words, His ordaining, His permission, and His will in matters of religion.

As for His words pertaining to the created order, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass, all creation falls under them, including Iblīs and his hosts, all disbelievers, and everyone else who enters the Fire. Although all creatures are alike in being encompassed by His creation, will, power, and decree, they differ with respect to His commands and prohibitions, His love, pleasure, and anger.

Allah’s pious allies are those who do what is commanded, refrain from what is forbidden, and patiently endure what is decreed. He loves them and they love Him; He is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. His enemies, the allies of the devils, although subject to His power, are those whom He hates, with whom He is angry, whom He curses, and to whom He is an enemy.

A detailed explanation of these points belongs elsewhere. I have written here only to draw attention to the principal aspects of “the distinction between the allies of the Most Merciful and the allies of Satan.” The essential distinction between the two lies in

judging them by their conformity to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Through him, Allah Most High distinguished His blessed allies from His wretched enemies; His allies, the people of Paradise, from His enemies, the people of the Fire; His allies, the people of guidance and rectitude, from His enemies, the people of error, misguidance, and corruption; and His enemies, the party of Satan, from His allies, in whose hearts He has inscribed faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him.

Allah Most High says:

“You will not find people who believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger”—to the end of the verse.

Allah Most High also says:

“When your Lord revealed to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, so strike above their necks and strike every fingertip of theirs.’”

He says concerning His enemies:

“Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you.”

He also says:

“Thus We have appointed for every prophet enemies—devils from among humans and jinn—who inspire one another with alluring words to deceive.”

And He says:

“Shall I tell you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar. They give ear, and most of them are liars. As for the poets, those who go astray follow them. Do you not see that they wander in every valley, and that they say what they do not do? Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and defend themselves after being wronged. Those who do wrong will come to know what fate awaits them.”

Allah Most High also says:

“So I swear by what you see and what you do not see: this is indeed the word of a noble messenger. It is not the word of a poet—how little you believe! Nor is it the word of a soothsayer—how little you take heed! It is a revelation from the Lord of all worlds. And if he had fabricated

any sayings in Our name, We would have seized him by the right hand, then severed his aorta, and none of you could have shielded him. Indeed, it is a reminder for the God-fearing. We certainly know that some of you deny it. It will surely be a source of regret for the disbelievers. Indeed, it is the absolute truth. So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.”

Allah Most High also says:

“So remind them, for by your Lord’s grace you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman”—through to His words: “if they are truthful.”

Thus Allah, glorified and exalted is He, declared our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, free of any association with those whom devils accompany: soothsayers, poets, and madmen. He explained that the one who brought him the Quran was a noble angel whom He had chosen.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among humankind.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of all worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart, so that you might be one of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel—it is he who brought it down upon your heart by Allah’s permission”—to the end of the verse.

Allah Most High also says:

“When you recite the Quran, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed”—through to His words: “and glad tidings for the Muslims.”

Thus He called him the Trustworthy Spirit and the Holy Spirit.

Allah Most High also says:

“So I swear by those that recede, that run their courses and retreat to cover.”

This means the stars that remain concealed in the sky before they rise. When they appear, people see them moving across the sky; when they set, they withdraw to their hiding place, which conceals them.

“And by the night as it retreats”—that is, when it departs and dawn approaches—“and by the dawn

as it breathes”—that is, as it arrives.

“Indeed, this is the word of a noble messenger”—namely Gabriel, peace be upon him—“possessed of strength, held in honor by the Lord of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy.” That is, he is obeyed in heaven and is trustworthy. Then He says:

“Your companion is not mad.”

That is, your companion whom Allah bestowed upon you as a blessing when He sent him to you as a messenger of your own kind, living among you, since you could not bear to see the angels. As Allah Most High says:

“They say, ‘Why has an angel not been sent down to him?’ Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been settled, and they would have been granted no respite. And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man”—to the end of the verse.

Allah Most High also says:

“He certainly saw him on the clear horizon”—that is, he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him.

“Nor is he danīn concerning the unseen”—that is, accused. In the other reading, “danīn”—that is, miserly, concealing knowledge and imparting it only for payment, as those who withhold knowledge unless they receive compensation do.

“Nor is this the word of an accursed devil.”

Thus He declared Gabriel, peace be upon him, free of being a devil, just as He declared Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, free of being a poet or a soothsayer.

Allah’s God-fearing allies are therefore those who follow the example of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They do what he commanded and refrain from what he forbade. They follow his example in those matters in which he instructed them to follow him. Allah supports them with His angels and a spirit from Him, and casts some of His light into their hearts. They receive the miraculous favors with which Allah honors His God-fearing allies. The miraculous favors granted to the best of Allah’s allies serve to establish a proof in religion or meet a need of the Muslims, just as the miracles of their Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served these purposes.

وَكَانَ فِى حِصْنٍ لَهُ بِأَرْضِ الْحِجَازِ، فَلَمَّا دَنَوْا مِنْهُ، وَقَدْ غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ، وَرَاحَ النَّاسُ بِسَرْحِهِمْ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ لأَصْحَابِهِ اجْلِسُوا مَكَانَكُمْ، فَإِنِّى مُنْطَلِقٌ، وَمُتَلَطِّفٌ لِلْبَوَّابِ، لَعَلِّى أَنْ أَدْخُلَ. فَأَقْبَلَ حَتَّى دَنَا مِنَ الْبَابِ ثُمَّ تَقَنَّعَ بِثَوْبِهِ كَأَنَّهُ يَقْضِى حَاجَةً، وَقَدْ دَخَلَ النَّاسُ، فَهَتَفَ بِهِ الْبَوَّابُ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ فَادْخُلْ، فَإِنِّى أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُغْلِقَ الْبَابَ. فَدَخَلْتُ فَكَمَنْتُ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ النَّاسُ أَغْلَقَ الْبَابَ، ثُمَّ عَلَّقَ الأَغَالِيقَ عَلَى وَتَدٍ قَالَ فَقُمْتُ إِلَى الأَقَالِيدِ، فَأَخَذْتُهَا فَفَتَحْتُ الْبَابَ، وَكَانَ أَبُو رَافِعٍ يُسْمَرُ عِنْدَهُ، وَكَانَ فِى عَلَالِىَّ لَهُ، فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ أَهْلُ سَمَرِهِ صَعِدْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَجَعَلْتُ كُلَّمَا فَتَحْتُ بَابًا أَغْلَقْتُ عَلَىَّ مِنْ دَاخِلٍ، قُلْتُ إِنِ الْقَوْمُ نَذِرُوا بِى لَمْ يَخْلُصُوا إِلَىَّ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ. فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ فِى بَيْتٍ مُظْلِمٍ وَسْطَ عِيَالِهِ، لَا أَدْرِى أَيْنَ هُوَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ. قَالَ مَنْ هَذَا فَأَهْوَيْتُ نَحْوَ الصَّوْتِ، فَأَضْرِبُهُ ضَرْبَةً بِالسَّيْفِ، وَأَنَا دَهِشٌ فَمَا أَغْنَيْتُ شَيْئًا، وَصَاحَ فَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ، فَأَمْكُثُ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ ثُمَّ دَخَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ مَا هَذَا الصَّوْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ. فَقَالَ لأُمِّكَ الْوَيْلُ، إِنَّ رَجُلاً فِى الْبَيْتِ ضَرَبَنِى قَبْلُ بِالسَّيْفِ، قَالَ فَأَضْرِبُهُ ضَرْبَةً أَثْخَنَتْهُ وَلَمْ أَقْتُلْهُ، ثُمَّ وَضَعْتُ ظُبَةَ السَّيْفِ فِى بَطْنِهِ حَتَّى أَخَذَ فِى ظَهْرِهِ، فَعَرَفْتُ أَنِّى قَتَلْتُهُ، فَجَعَلْتُ أَفْتَحُ الأَبْوَابَ بَابًا بَابًا حَتَّى انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى دَرَجَةٍ لَهُ، فَوَضَعْتُ رِجْلِى وَأَنَا أُرَى أَنِّى قَدِ انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى الأَرْضِ فَوَقَعْتُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُقْمِرَةٍ، فَانْكَسَرَتْ سَاقِى، فَعَصَبْتُهَا بِعِمَامَةٍ، ثُمَّ انْطَلَقْتُ حَتَّى جَلَسْتُ عَلَى الْبَابِ فَقُلْتُ لَا أَخْرُجُ اللَّيْلَةَ حَتَّى أَعْلَمَ أَقَتَلْتُهُ فَلَمَّا صَاحَ الدِّيكُ قَامَ النَّاعِى عَلَى السُّورِ فَقَالَ أَنْعَى أَبَا رَافِعٍ تَاجِرَ أَهْلِ الْحِجَازِ. فَانْطَلَقْتُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِى فَقُلْتُ النَّجَاءَ، فَقَدْ قَتَلَ اللَّهُ أَبَا رَافِعٍ. فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى النَّبِىِّ - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فَحَدَّثْتُهُ فَقَالَ «ابْسُطْ رِجْلَكَ». فَبَسَطْتُ رِجْلِى، فَمَسَحَهَا، فَكَأَنَّهَا لَمْ أَشْتَكِهَا قَطُّ).
translated_text:
The miraculous favors granted to Allah’s allies come only through the blessing of following His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They therefore fall, in reality, within the miracles of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. These include the splitting of the moon; the pebbles glorifying Allah in his palm; trees coming to him; the palm trunk yearning for him; his description of Jerusalem on the night of the Ascension; his accounts of past and future events; his bringing the mighty Book; and his multiplying food and drink on many occasions.

During the Battle of the Trench, for example, he fed the army to their fill from a pot of food without its contents diminishing, as related in the well-known hadith of Umm Salamah. During the expedition to Khaybar, he quenched the army’s thirst from a waterskin without its contents diminishing. In the year of Tabūk, he filled the army’s vessels from a small quantity of food without it diminishing, although they numbered some 30,000. Water flowed from between his fingers on several occasions, providing enough for everyone with him—as at al-Hudaybiyah, where they numbered some 1,400 or 1,500. He also restored Abū Qatādah’s eye after it had fallen onto his cheek, and it became the better of his two eyes.

[When he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah to kill Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Muhammad fell and broke his leg. The Prophet stroked it, and it healed.] (*)

He fed 130 men with roast meat, cutting off a piece for each of them and making two portions of it. They all ate from it, and some remained afterward. There was also the debt of thirty wasqs that ʿAbdullāh, Jābir’s father, owed to a Jewish man. Jābir said:

“He instructed the creditor to take all the dates in settlement of what was owed to him, but he refused. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then walked among the date palms and said to Jābir, ‘Harvest the dates for him.’ He paid him the thirty wasqs in full, and seventeen wasqs remained.”

There are many such examples. I have collected about a thousand miracles.
translated_footnote:
Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd said (pp. 96–98):

It is well known that this happened to Abdullāh ibn Atīk, may Allah be pleased with him, when he killed Ibn Abī al-Huqayq. This may therefore be a slip of the pen. Sahīh al-Bukhārī records that al-Barā ibn Āzib, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent some men of the Ansār against Abū Rāfi, the Jew, appointing Abdullāh ibn Atīk as their commander. Abū Rāfi used to harm the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and assist others against him. He lived in a fortress of his in the Hijāz. When they approached it, the sun had set and people were returning with their grazing livestock. Abdullāh said to his companions, ‘Stay where you are. I will go ahead and approach the gatekeeper tactfully, hoping to gain entry.’

“He approached the gate, then covered himself with his garment as though relieving himself. The people had already entered, and the gatekeeper called out to him, ‘O servant of Allah! If you want to enter, come in, for I am about to close the gate.’

“Abdullāh said: ‘I entered and hid. Once everyone had entered, he closed the gate and hung the keys on a peg. I went over to the keys, took them, and unlocked the gate. Abū Rāfi used to have people gather with him for conversation at night, and he was in his upper rooms. When his evening companions had left, I went upstairs to him. Whenever I opened a door, I closed it behind me from the inside, thinking, “If the people become aware of me, they will not reach me before I kill him.”

“‘I reached him and found him in a dark room among his family, but I did not know where in the room he was. I called, “Abū Rāfi!” He said, “Who is this?” I lunged towards the voice and struck him once with my sword, but I was so flustered that I achieved nothing. He cried out, so I left the room, waited a short while, and then went back in. I asked, “What is this noise, Abū Rāfi?” He replied, “Woe to your mother! A man in the room struck me with a sword just now.”

“‘I struck him again, severely wounding him but not killing him. Then I thrust the point of the sword into his belly until it penetrated his back, and I knew that I had killed him. I began opening the doors one by one until I reached a stairway of his. I put my foot down, thinking I had reached the ground, and fell. It was a moonlit night. My lower leg broke, so I bound it with a turban and went on until I sat down at the gate. I said to myself, “I will not leave tonight until I know whether I have killed him.”

“‘When the rooster crowed, a man announcing his death stood on the wall and said, “I announce the death of Abū Rāfi, the merchant of the people of the Hijāz.” I went to my companions and said, “Make haste to escape! Allah has killed Abū Rāfi.”

“‘I reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened. He said, “Stretch out your leg.” I stretched it out, and he stroked it. It was as though I had never suffered any pain in it.’”

translated_text:
The miraculous favors granted to the Companions, the Successors after them, and all other righteous people are exceedingly numerous.

For example, “Usayd ibn Hudayr” was reciting Sūrat al-Kahf when something like a canopy containing lamps descended from heaven. These were angels who had descended because of his recitation. Angels used to greet ʿImrān ibn Husayn. Salmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ were eating from a dish when the dish—or its contents—glorified Allah. ʿAbbād ibn Bishr and Usayd ibn Hudayr left the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night, and a light like the tip of a whip shone for them. When they parted, the light divided, accompanying each of them. This was narrated by al-Bukhārī and others.

There is also the account of {al-Siddīq, recorded in the two Sahīh collections: he took three guests home with him, and whenever he ate a morsel, an even greater quantity grew beneath it. They ate their fill, and the food became more plentiful than it had been before. Abū Bakr and his wife looked at it and found that there was more than before. He took it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Many people came to him, ate from it, and were satisfied}.

“Khubayb ibn ʿAdī” was held captive by the polytheists in Mecca—may Allah Most High honor it. Grapes would be brought to him to eat, although there was not a single grape in Mecca.

And “ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayrah: he was killed as a martyr, and they searched for his body but could not find it.

Something similar happened to “Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī,” who was thrown into the fire. He and the soldiers accompanying him walked across the Tigris while its floodwaters carried pieces of timber. He then turned to his companions and asked, “Are you missing any of your belongings, so that I may supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about them?” One of them replied, “I have lost a fodder bag.” He said, “Follow me.” The man followed him and found it caught on something, so he retrieved it.

When al-Aswad al-‘Ansī claimed prophethood, he summoned Abū Muslim and asked him, “Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “I cannot hear.” He asked, “Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “Yes.” Al-Aswad ordered a fire to be lit, and Abū Muslim was thrown into it. They found him standing in prayer within it, for it had become cool and safe for him.

He arrived in Medina after the death of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. ‘Umar seated him between himself and Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said, “Praise be to Allah, who did not let me die before I saw someone from the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, undergo what Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, underwent.”

A servant girl put poison in his food, but it did not harm him. A woman turned his wife against him, so he supplicated against her, and she became blind. She then came to him and repented, so he supplicated for her, and Allah restored her sight.

Once, he became hungry in al-Ahwāz, so he supplicated Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and asked Him for food. A basket of fresh dates wrapped in a silk cloth fell behind him. He ate the dates, and the cloth remained with his wife for some time.

A lion approached him while he was praying in a thicket at night. When he had concluded his prayer with the salutation of peace, he said to it, “Seek your provision somewhere else.” The lion turned away, roaring.

A man from al-Nakhaʿ had a donkey that died on the road. His companions said to him, “Come, let us divide your belongings among our mounts.” He replied, “Give me a little time.” Then he performed ablution thoroughly, prayed two rakʿahs, and supplicated Allah Most High. Allah restored his donkey to life, and he loaded his belongings onto it.

When Uways al-Qaranī died, they found among his clothes burial shrouds that had not been with him before. They also found a grave already dug for him, with a burial niche cut into rock. They buried him there, shrouded in those cloths.

One day, ʿAmr ibn ʿUqba ibn Farqad was praying in intense heat when a cloud shaded him. A wild beast would guard him while he tended his companions’ mounts, for he would stipulate, when joining his companions on military expeditions, that he would serve them.

When Mutarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr entered his home, his vessels would glorify Allah along with him. Once, he and a companion were walking in darkness when the tip of a whip shone, lighting their way.

Ibrāhīm al-Taymī would go a month or two without eating anything. Once, he went out to obtain food for his family but could find none. He passed some red sandy soil and took some of it, then returned to his family. When he opened his bundle, he found red wheat inside. Whenever he sowed any of it, each ear grew densely packed with grain from its base to its tip.

‘Utba al-Ghulām had asked his Lord for three things: a beautiful voice, abundant tears, and food without toil. Whenever he recited, he would weep and move others to tears, and his tears flowed throughout his life. He would return home and find his sustenance there, without knowing where it came from.

‘Abd al-Wāhid ibn Zayd was afflicted with paralysis. He asked his Lord to restore movement to his limbs at the time of ablution. Whenever it was time for ablution, his limbs would regain their movement, then become paralyzed again afterward.

This is a vast subject, and the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s close servants have been discussed at length elsewhere. As for the instances we know of concerning particular individuals, and those we know of in our own time, they are numerous.

translated_text:
It should also be understood that miraculous gifts may be granted according to a person’s need. If someone whose faith is weak, or who is in need, requires them, he may receive what strengthens his faith and meets his need. Someone whose closeness to Allah is more complete may have no need of them, and so receive nothing of this kind because of his higher rank and his lack of need—not because of any deficiency in his closeness to Allah. For this reason, such occurrences were more frequent among the Successors than among the Companions. This differs from the case of those through whom extraordinary events occur to guide people and meet their needs: these people are of greater rank.

This is unlike satanic states, such as the case of ‘Abd Allāh ibn Sayyād, who appeared during the Prophet’s lifetime, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Some of the Companions thought that he was the Dajjāl. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, withheld judgment about him until it later became clear to him that he was not the Dajjāl. He was, however, one of the soothsayers. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “I have concealed something for you.” He replied, “Al-dukh, al-dukh (smoke, smoke).” He had concealed for him Surah al-Dukhān (Smoke). The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said to him, “Begone! You will never exceed your station.”

He meant: you are merely one of the brethren of the soothsayers. A soothsayer would have a companion from among the devils who informed him of many unseen matters through what he overheard by stealth. They would mix truth with falsehood, as related in the authentic hadith narrated by al-Bukhārī and others, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The angels descend into the clouds and mention a matter decreed in heaven. The devils listen by stealth and convey it to the soothsayers, who add a hundred lies of their own to it.”

translated_text:
Muslim also narrated a hadith from Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said:

“While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was among a group of the Ansār, a shooting star was hurled, shining brightly. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked, ‘What would you say in the days of ignorance when you saw something like this?’ They replied, ‘We would say that a great man had died or a great man had been born.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘These are not hurled because of anyone’s death or birth. Rather, when our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him. Then the inhabitants of the heaven nearest to them glorify Him, followed by those nearest to them, until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of this heaven. Then the inhabitants of the seventh heaven ask the bearers of the Throne, “What did our Lord say?” They tell them, and the inhabitants of each heaven in turn ask for the news, until it reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. The devils snatch a hearing and are pelted, then pass what they heard on to their allies. Whatever they convey accurately is true, but they add to it.’”

In another narration, Ma‘mar said: “I asked al-Zuhrī, ‘Were they hurled in the days of ignorance?’ He replied, ‘Yes, but it intensified when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent.’”

Al-Aswad al-‘Ansī, who claimed prophethood, had devils who informed him of certain unseen matters. When the Muslims fought him, they feared that the devils would tell him what they were saying about him. Eventually, his wife helped them against him after his disbelief became clear to her, and they killed him.

translated_text:
Likewise, Musaylima the Liar had devils who informed him of unseen matters and helped him with certain things. There are many such people, including al-Hārith al-Dimashqī, who appeared in Syria during the reign of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Marwān and claimed prophethood. Devils would free his feet from shackles and prevent weapons from piercing him, and a marble slab would glorify Allah when he stroked it with his hand. He would show people men and horsemen in the air, saying, “These are angels,” when in fact they were jinn. When the Muslims seized him to kill him, a man thrust a spear at him, but it did not pierce him. ‘Abd al-Malik said to the man, “You did not mention Allah’s name.” He then mentioned Allah’s name, thrust the spear at him, and killed him.

Similarly, those who experience satanic states find that their devils leave them when something that drives them away, such as the Throne Verse, is recited in their presence. This is established in the authentic hadith collection in the account of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entrusted him with guarding the zakāt al-fitr alms, a devil stole from him night after night. Each time, he would seize him, but the devil would repent, so he would release him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would ask him, ‘What did your captive do last night?’ He would reply, ‘He claimed that he would not return.’ The Prophet would say, ‘He has lied to you, and he will return.’ On the third occasion, the devil said, ‘Let me go, and I will teach you something that will benefit you: when you go to bed, recite the Throne Verse, “Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence,” to its end. A guardian from Allah will remain over you, and no devil will approach you until morning.’ When he informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said, ‘He has told you the truth

Thus, when someone sincerely recites this verse in the presence of satanic states, it dispels them. This applies, for example, to someone who enters fire through a satanic state, or attends a gathering of whistling and clapping, where devils descend upon him and speak through his tongue in words whose meaning is unknown and which may be unintelligible. He may disclose what is in the heart of someone present, or speak in different languages, just as a jinn speaks through the tongue of a possessed person. The person experiencing this state is unaware of it, like someone whom Satan throws into convulsions through his touch, possessing him and speaking through his tongue. When he regains consciousness, he has no awareness of anything he said. Thus, a possessed person may be struck without the blows affecting the human being. On regaining consciousness, he reports that he felt nothing, because the blows fell upon the jinn possessing him.

Among these people are those to whom a devil brings foods, fruits, sweets, and other things unavailable in that place. Others are carried through the air by a jinn to Mecca, Jerusalem, or elsewhere. Some are carried there late on the Day of ‘Arafa and brought back that very night. Such a person does not perform Hajj as prescribed by Islamic law. Rather, he goes in his ordinary clothes, does not enter the consecrated state for pilgrimage when he comes level with the appointed boundary, does not recite the pilgrim’s invocation, does not stop at Muzdalifa, does not circumambulate the House, does not perform the ritual passage between al-Safā and al-Marwa, and does not stone the pillars. Instead, he stands at ‘Arafa in his ordinary clothes and returns that very night. This is not Hajj.

For this reason, one of these people saw the angels recording the pilgrims and asked, “Will you not record me?” They replied, “You are not among the pilgrims”—meaning those performing Hajj as prescribed by Islamic law.

translated_text:
There are several distinctions between the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies and the satanic states that resemble them.

One is that “the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s allies” arise from faith and piety, whereas “satanic states” arise from what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoral deeds, whether committed openly or secretly, sin, unjust aggression, associating with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and saying about Allah what you do not know.’”

Speaking about Allah without knowledge, associating partners with Him, wrongdoing, and immoral deeds have all been forbidden by Allah Most High and His Messenger. They therefore cannot be grounds for Allah Most High to honor someone with miraculous gifts. Thus, if such phenomena do not occur through prayer, remembrance of Allah, and recitation of the Quran, but instead occur through what Satan loves and through practices involving the association of partners with Allah, such as seeking aid from created beings—or if they are used to wrong others and commit immoral deeds—then they are satanic states, not miraculous gifts from the Most Merciful.

Among these people are those whose devil descends upon them when they attend a gathering of whistling and clapping, until it carries them through the air and takes them out of that house. If one of Allah Most High’s allies arrives, he drives the devil away, and the person falls. This has happened to more than one person.

Among these people are those who seek aid from a created being, living or dead, whether that living person is a Muslim, a Christian, or a polytheist. The devil then assumes the form of the person whose aid is sought

Among these people was a shaykh in Egypt who instructed his servant, saying, “When I die, do not let anyone wash me, for I shall come and wash myself.” When he died, his servant saw someone in his form and believed that it was the shaykh himself who had entered and washed himself. When the visitor had finished the washing—that is, washing the deceased—he vanished. This was a devil who had misled the deceased by telling him, “After death, you will come and wash yourself.” When the man died, the devil again came in his form to mislead the living, just as he had previously misled the deceased.

Some of them see a throne in the air with a light above it and hear someone addressing them, saying, “I am your Lord.” If the person has discernment, he recognizes that it is a devil, rebukes it, and seeks refuge in Allah from it, whereupon it disappears.

Some of them see figures while awake, one of whom claims to be a prophet, a man of truth, or a righteous shaykh. This has happened to more than one person. Others see in a dream that some eminent figure—whether al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, or someone else—has cut or shaved their hair, or dressed them in his cap or garment. They then awake wearing a cap, with their hair shaved or trimmed. In reality, it was the jinn who shaved or trimmed their hair.

These satanic experiences occur to those who depart from the Quran and Sunnah. They differ in degree, and the jinn who associate with them are of their own kind and follow their beliefs. Among the jinn are disbelievers, evildoers, and those who err. If the human is a disbeliever, an evildoer, or ignorant, they join him in disbelief, wickedness, and misguidance. They may assist him if he agrees to the acts of disbelief they choose, such as adjuring them by the names of those they revere among the jinn and others; writing Allah’s names or some of His words with filth; or reversing the order of Sūrat al-Fātihah, Sūrat al-Ikhlās, the Verse of the Throne, or other passages, and writing them with filth. They then make water sink into the ground for him and transport it, because of the acts of disbelief with which he pleases them.

They may also bring him a woman or boy whom he desires, either through the air or driven and forced to come to him. There are many other such things, which would take too long to describe, and belief in them is belief

in al-jibt and al-tāghūt. Al-jibt means sorcery, while al-tāghūt refers to devils and idols. If a man obeys Allah and His Messenger inwardly and outwardly, they can neither join him in such things nor make peace with him.

Since the prescribed worship of Muslims takes place in mosques, which are the houses of Allah, those who frequent the mosques are further removed from satanic experiences. Those who practise polytheism and religious innovations, however, venerate graves and shrines of the dead: they invoke the deceased, supplicate through him, or believe that supplication at his grave is answered. They are more susceptible to satanic experiences. It is established in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“May Allah curse the Jews and Christians; they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”

It is also established in Sahīh Muslim that, five nights before his death, he said:

“Among those most generous to me with their companionship and wealth is Abū Bakr. Were I to take an intimate friend from among the people of the earth, I would take Abū Bakr as an intimate friend. But your companion is Allah’s intimate friend. Let every small doorway into the mosque be sealed except the doorway of Abū Bakr. Those before you used to take graves as places of worship. Beware! Do not take graves as places of worship, for I forbid you to do so.”

The two Sahīh collections also relate that, during his illness, a church in Abyssinia was mentioned to him. They described its beauty and the images within it, and he said, “Whenever there died among those people

a righteous man, they would build a place of worship over his grave and make those images in it. Those are the worst of creation in Allah’s sight on the Day of Resurrection.”

In the Musnad and the Sahīh of Abū Hātim, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“Among the worst of creation are those who are still alive when the Hour overtakes them, and those who take graves as places of worship.”

In the Sahīh, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“Do not sit on graves or pray towards them.”

In al-Muwatta’, he is reported to have said:

“O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped. Great was Allah’s wrath against people who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”

In the Sunan, he is reported to have said:

“Do not make my grave a place of recurring gatherings. Send blessings upon me wherever you are, for your blessings reach me.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“Whenever a man greets me with peace, Allah restores my soul to me so that I may return his greeting.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah has appointed angels at my grave who convey to me the greetings of peace from my community.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday and the night preceding Friday, for your blessings are presented to me.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how are our blessings presented to you when you have

decayed—that is, decomposed?” He replied, “Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the flesh of the prophets.”

Allah Most High has said in His Book concerning the polytheists among the people of Noah, peace be upon him:

“And they said, ‘Never abandon your gods; never abandon Wadd, Suwā‘, Yaghūth, Ya‘ūq or Nasr.’”

Ibn ‘Abbās and others among the early generations said: These were righteous men among Noah’s people. When they died, the people remained in devotion at their graves, then fashioned statues of them and worshipped them. This was the beginning of idol worship.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, therefore forbade taking graves as places of worship, to close the door to associating partners with Allah. Likewise, he forbade prayer at sunrise and sunset, because the polytheists prostrate to the sun at those times, and Satan accompanies it as it rises and sets. Prayer at those times would thus resemble the prayer of the polytheists, so he closed this door.

Satan leads the children of Adam astray to the extent that he is able. Whoever worships the sun, moon and stars and invokes them—as those who practise invoking the stars do—has a devil descend upon him, speak to him and tell him about certain matters. They call this “the spirit of the stars,” but it is a devil. Although a devil may help a person achieve some of his aims, he harms him many times more than he benefits him. Whoever obeys him will ultimately come to evil, unless Allah turns to him in forgiveness. Likewise, devils may speak to idol worshippers

and likewise to those who seek help from someone dead or absent, or who call upon the dead, supplicate to Allah through them, or believe that supplication at their graves is better than in homes and mosques. They transmit a hadith that the experts unanimously agree is fabricated:

“When matters prove too difficult for you, turn to the occupants of graves.”

This is merely a fabrication by someone who opened the door to associating partners with Allah.

Adherents of innovation and polytheism who imitate them—among idol worshippers, Christians, and misguided Muslims—experience phenomena at shrines that they suppose are miracles granted to the righteous, although they actually come from devils. The devil does this to lead them astray. If you sincerely recite the Verse of the Throne there, this comes to nothing, for affirming Allah’s oneness drives the devil away. Thus, when a devil carried one of them through the air and he said, “There is no god but Allah,” he fell. Another example is that one of them may see a grave split open and a person emerge from it, whom he supposes to be the deceased, although it is a devil. This is a vast subject that cannot be treated fully here.

People fall into three groups regarding extraordinary phenomena:

“One group” denies that such things occur to anyone other than prophets, though it may acknowledge them in general

but rejects what it is told about many people because, in its view, they are not among Allah’s allies. Others suppose that anyone who displays any extraordinary phenomenon is an ally of Allah. Both views are mistaken. Thus, you find the latter saying that the polytheists and the People of the Book have supporters who help them fight the Muslims, and that these supporters are allies of Allah.

The former deny that there could be anyone among them who displays extraordinary phenomena. The correct position is the third: they do have supporters of their own kind, not allies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them.”

Devils attach themselves to these worshippers and ascetics who are not among Allah’s pious allies who follow the Quran and Sunnah. Each may therefore display extraordinary feats suited to his condition. However, their feats counteract one another, and when a firmly established ally of Allah Most High is present, he nullifies their feats. Each of them inevitably exhibits falsehood—whether through ignorance or deliberately—and sin corresponding to the condition of the devils attached to them. Through this, Allah distinguishes His pious allies from those allies of the devils who resemble them. Allah Most High says:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?”

“They descend upon every sinful liar.”

A “liar” is one who habitually lies, and “sinful” means wicked.

The polytheists adopted this as worship. By contrast, the worship of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his Companions consisted of what Allah commanded: prayer, recitation, remembrance, and the like, along with gatherings sanctioned by Islam. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his Companions never gathered to listen to singing, whether accompanied by handclapping, a tambourine, or ecstatic displays; nor did his cloak fall off. Rather, all such accounts are lies, by the consensus of those versed in his hadith.

When the Prophet’s Companions gathered, they would ask one of their number to recite while the rest listened. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, would say to Abū Mūsā al-Ash‘arī, “Remind us of our Lord.” He would then recite while they listened.

“The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by Abū Mūsā al-Ash‘arī while he was reciting and said to him, ‘I passed by you last night while you were reciting, and I began listening to your recitation.’ He replied, ‘Had I known you were listening, I would have made it truly beautiful for you.’” That is, he would have greatly beautified his recitation for him. As the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Beautify the Quran with your voices.”

He also said, peace and blessings be upon him:

“Allah is certainly more attentive in hearing—that is, listening—to a man with a beautiful voice reciting the Quran than the owner of a singing-girl is to her.”

“The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Ibn Mas‘ūd, ‘Recite the Quran to me.’ He replied, ‘Should I recite it to you when it was revealed to you?’ He said, ‘I like to hear it from someone else.’ So I recited Sūrat al-Nisā’ to him until I reached

this verse:

‘How will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these people?’

He said, ‘That is enough,’ and his eyes were streaming with tears.”

Such listening is the listening of the prophets and their followers, as Allah describes in the Quran:

“Those were the prophets whom Allah blessed, from the descendants of Adam, from those We carried with Noah, from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and weeping.”

He says of those who possess knowledge:

“When they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they recognize.”

Glorified is He, He praises those who listen in this way for the increase in faith, the trembling of their skin, and the tears that flow from their eyes. He, Most High, says:

“Allah has sent down the best message: a Book whose verses are consistent and oft-repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it; then their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah.”

He, Most High, also says:

“The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, whose faith increases when His verses are recited to them, and who put their trust in their Lord.”

“Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them.”

“They are the true believers. They will have ranks with their Lord, forgiveness, and a generous provision.”

As for the newly introduced practice of listening to handclapping, tambourines, and reed pipes, the Companions, those who followed them in righteousness, and all the other great imams of the religion did not make this a path to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, nor did they regard it as an act of drawing near to Him or of obedience.

Allah’s friends who possess knowledge recognize this and know that Satan has a considerable share in it. Thus, the best of those among them who attended such gatherings repented of doing so. The further someone is from knowledge and from perfect friendship with Allah, the greater Satan’s share in him. It is like wine, yet its effect on souls is greater than that of wine. Thus, when its practitioners become deeply intoxicated, devils descend upon them, speak through the tongues of some, and carry others through the air. Enmity may arise among them, just as it does among wine drinkers. One person’s devils may be stronger than another’s, and so they kill the latter.

The ignorant suppose that this is among the miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s God-fearing friends. In reality, it distances the person concerned from Allah and belongs to satanic states. Killing a Muslim is lawful only on grounds permitted by Allah. How, then, could killing someone whose life is inviolable be something with which Allah honors His friends? The highest honor lies in remaining steadfast in uprightness. Whatever Allah grants His servant of these things, if he uses it to help him do what Allah loves and is pleased with, what brings him nearer to Him and raises his rank, and what Allah and His Messenger command, he thereby gains greater distinction and nearness to Allah and His Messenger, and his rank rises. If, however, he uses it to help him do what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, such as associating partners with Allah, wrongdoing, and acts of indecency, he thereby deserves blame and punishment. Unless Allah Most High comes to his aid by granting him repentance or good deeds that erase sins, he will be like other sinners.

Thus, those who possess extraordinary abilities are often punished: sometimes by being deprived of them, just as a king is deposed from his kingdom or a scholar is stripped of his knowledge; sometimes by being deprived of voluntary acts of worship, descending from a special degree of friendship with Allah to its general degree; sometimes by falling to the rank of the defiantly sinful; and sometimes by apostatizing from Islam. This occurs among those whose extraordinary feats are satanic, for many of them apostatize from Islam. Many do not know that these feats are satanic, but suppose them to be miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s friends. Some of them suppose that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grants a servant something beyond the ordinary course of events, He will not hold him accountable for it—just as some suppose that when Allah grants a servant dominion, wealth, and power to act, He will not hold him accountable for these things.

Some use extraordinary abilities to pursue permissible matters that are neither commanded nor forbidden. Such a person belongs to the general body of Allah’s friends: the righteous who follow a middle course. As for the foremost, those brought near to Allah, they rank above these, just as the servant

Since extraordinary feats often lower a man’s rank, many righteous people repent of such things and seek Allah Most High’s forgiveness, just as they repent of sins such as unlawful sexual intercourse and theft. When such feats are offered to some of them, they ask Allah to remove them. All of them instruct the spiritual aspirant not to become preoccupied with them, make them his ambition, or boast of them—even though they believe them to be miraculous gifts. What, then, if they are actually from devils, who use them to lead people astray?

I know someone to whom plants speak of their beneficial properties, whereas it is actually the devil that has entered them who speaks to him. I also know people to whom stones and trees speak, saying, “Glad tidings to you, O friend of Allah!” Then the person recites the Verse of the Throne, and this ceases.

I know someone who sets out to hunt birds, and sparrows and other birds speak to him, saying, “Take me so that the poor may eat me.” A devil has entered them, just as it enters human beings, and speaks these words to him.

Some people are inside a locked house, then find themselves outside it without having opened it, or the reverse. The same happens at city gates: the jinn have swiftly carried them in or out. Or lights pass before someone, or a person he seeks appears before him. This comes from devils assuming the form of his companion. When he recites the Verse of the Throne repeatedly, all of this disappears.

I know someone to whom a speaker says, “I am of Allah’s command,” and promises him that he will be the Mahdī of whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave glad tidings; and extraordinary feats appear before him

such as his conceiving of control over birds and locusts in the air. Whenever he thinks of the birds or locusts moving right or left, they go where he wishes. Whenever he thinks of some livestock standing, sleeping, or moving away, what he wishes occurs without any outward movement on his part. They carry him to Mecca and bring him back, and bring him figures of beautiful appearance, telling him, “These are the cherubic angels; they wished to visit you.” He thinks to himself, “How have they taken the form of beardless youths?” Then he raises his head and finds them bearded. He is told, “The sign that you are the Mahdī is that a mole will appear on your body.” It appears, and he sees it. Other things happen too, all of them part of Satan’s cunning.

This is a vast subject. Were I to recount what I know of it, it would require a large volume. Allah Most High has said:

“As for man, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and granting him blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me.’”

“But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’”

Allah, Blessed and Most High, says:

“No!”

The word “No” conveys both rebuke and a call to attention: a rebuke against speaking in this way, and a call to heed the statements and commands that follow. Not everyone who receives worldly blessings regarded as marks of honour is thereby being honoured by Allah, Mighty and Majestic; nor is everyone whose share of them He restricts thereby being humiliated by Him. Rather, He—glory be to Him—tests His servant through prosperity and adversity. He may bestow worldly blessings upon someone whom He does not love and who holds no honour with Him, thereby leading him gradually towards ruin. And He may shield someone whom He loves and takes as His friend from such blessings, lest they diminish his rank with Him or cause him to fall into conduct that He dislikes.

Moreover, “miraculous gifts granted to Allah’s friends” must arise from faith and mindfulness of Allah. Whatever arises from disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience belongs to the extraordinary feats of Allah’s enemies, not to the miraculous gifts of His friends.

Thus, if a person’s extraordinary feats do not occur through prayer, Quran recitation, remembrance of Allah, night prayer, and supplication, but occur instead through associating partners with Allah—such as invoking the dead or the absent—or through wickedness, disobedience, and consuming forbidden things, such as snakes, wasps, beetles, blood, and other impurities, or through singing and dancing, especially with non-mahram women and beardless youths; if his extraordinary powers weaken when he hears the Quran and grow stronger when he hears Satan’s pipes, so that he dances long into the night, yet when prayer time comes he prays sitting down or pecks through his prayer like a rooster; and if he hates listening to the Quran, recoils from it, and forces himself to listen, having no love for it and finding in it neither spiritual relish nor delight in his state of ecstasy, while he loves listening to whistling and clapping and experiences ecstatic feelings through them—then these are satanic states. He is among those encompassed by the words of Allah Most High:

“Whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil who becomes his companion.”

The Quran is the remembrance of the Most Merciful. Allah Most High says:

“But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him up blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

“He will say, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me up blind when I used to see?’”

“He will say, ‘So it is: Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and so today you will be forgotten.’”

This means: you abandoned acting upon them. Ibn ‘Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, “Allah has guaranteed that whoever reads His Book and acts upon its teachings will neither go astray in this world nor suffer misery in the Hereafter.” He then recited this verse.

Section

It must also be known that Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to all humans and jinn. Every human and jinn is therefore obliged to believe in Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and follow him: to believe what he conveys and obey what he commands. Whoever has had the proof of his messengership established against him yet does not believe in him is a disbeliever, whether human or jinn.

Muslims unanimously agree that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent to both humankind and jinn. The jinn listened to the Quran and returned to their people as warners when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was leading his Companions in prayer in the valley of Nakhla upon his return from al-Tā’if. Allah informed him of this in the Quran, saying:

“And when We directed a group of jinn towards you to listen to the Quran, upon attending its recitation they said, ‘Listen attentively.’ Then, when the recitation ended, they returned to their people as warners.”

“They said, ‘O our people! We have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.’”

“‘O our people! Respond to Allah’s caller and believe in him. He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.’”

“‘And whoever does not respond to the caller of

Allah cannot escape Him on earth and has no protectors besides Him. Such people are clearly astray.’”

Allah Most High subsequently revealed:

“Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened and said, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. Exalted is the majesty of our Lord! He has taken neither a wife nor a child. The foolish one among us used to utter outrageous claims about Allah. We had thought that humans and jinn would never speak lies about Allah. Some men among humankind used to seek refuge with men among the jinn, thus increasing them in transgression.’”

That is, “the foolish one among us,” according to the more evident of the two scholarly views.

More than one of the early Muslims stated that when a man came to a valley, he would say, “I seek refuge with the mighty one of this valley from the evil of the foolish among his people.” When humans sought help from the jinn, the jinn grew in rebellion and disbelief, as Allah Most High said:

“Some men among humankind used to seek refuge with men among the jinn, thus increasing them in transgression.”

“They thought, just as you thought, that Allah would never raise anyone up.”

“We sought to reach heaven, but found it filled with mighty guards and shooting stars.”

The devils were being pelted with shooting stars even before the Quran was revealed. However, they would sometimes steal a hearing before a shooting star reached one of them. When Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, heaven was filled with mighty guards and shooting stars, and the shooting stars lay in wait for them before they could hear anything, as they said:

“We used to take up positions there to listen, but whoever listens now finds a shooting star lying in wait for him.”

And Allah Most High said in another verse:

“It was not the devils who brought it down. It is neither fitting for them, nor are they able to do so. Indeed, they are barred from hearing it.”

They said:

“We do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends right guidance for them.”

“Among us are the righteous, and among us are those otherwise; we have followed different paths.”

That is, they follow various ways, as the scholars have explained: among them are Muslims, polytheists, Christians, followers of the Sunnah, and followers of religious innovation.

“We have realized that we cannot escape Allah on earth, nor can we escape Him by fleeing.”

They stated that they could not escape Him, whether they remained on earth or fled from Him.

“When we heard the guidance, we believed in it. Whoever believes in his Lord need fear neither loss nor injustice.”

“Among us are those who submit to Allah, and among us are the unjust.”

That is, the wrongdoers. The verb aqsata means to act justly, whereas qasata means to act unjustly and oppress.

“Those who submit to Allah have sought out right guidance.”

“As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell.”

“If they were to remain steadfast on the way, We would give them abundant water to drink, to test them thereby. Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will subject him to an overwhelming punishment.”

“The mosques belong to Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah.”

“When the servant of Allah stood up to call upon Him, they almost crowded upon him in a mass.”

“Say: I call only upon my Lord, and I associate no one with Him.”

“Say: I have no power to bring you harm or right guidance.”

“Say: No one can protect me from Allah, nor will I find any refuge besides Him.”

That is, a shelter and a place of protection.

“All I can do is convey from Allah and deliver His messages. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.”

“Then, when they see what they have been promised, they will know whose supporters are weaker and whose numbers are fewer.”

Then, after the jinn heard the Quran, they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and believed in him. They were the jinn of Nisibis, as established in al-Sahīh in the hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd. It is also related that he recited Surah al-Rahmān to them, and whenever he said:

“Then which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?”

they replied: “We deny none of Your favors, our Lord; to You belongs all praise.”

“When they met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, they asked him for provisions for themselves and their animals. He said: ‘You may have every bone over which Allah’s name has been mentioned; you will find it abundantly covered with meat. Every dropping will be fodder for your animals.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Do not cleanse yourselves with either of these after relieving yourselves, for they are provisions for your brothers among the jinn.’”

This prohibition is established from him through several channels. Scholars have cited it as evidence prohibiting the use of these things for cleansing after relieving oneself. They said: “If using the provisions of the jinn and their animals for such cleansing is forbidden, then it is all the more forbidden to use food and fodder intended for humans and their animals.”

Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to all humans and jinn. This is of far greater standing before Allah Most High than the jinn’s being subjected to Solomon, peace be upon him. They were subjected to Solomon, who exercised royal authority over them, whereas Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to them to command them to do what Allah and His Messenger commanded, for he is Allah’s servant and Messenger. The station of a servant-messenger is above that of a prophet-king.

The point here is that relations between jinn and humans take various forms:

A human who commands the jinn to do what Allah and His Messenger have commanded—worshipping Allah alone and obeying His Prophet—and commands humans to do likewise is among the foremost allies of Allah Most High. In this capacity, he is one of the Messenger’s successors and deputies.

Someone who employs the jinn in matters lawful for him is like someone who employs humans in matters lawful for him. For example, he may command them to fulfill their obligations, forbid them from doing what is unlawful for them, and employ them in matters lawful for him. He thus stands in the position of kings who do the same. Supposing that he is one of the allies of Allah Most High, he belongs, at most, to the general ranks of Allah’s allies, standing as a prophet-king does in relation to a servant-messenger: as Solomon and Joseph stand in relation to Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all.

Whoever employs the jinn in what Allah and His Messenger forbid—whether in associating partners with Allah, killing someone whose life is inviolable, or committing aggression against such people short of killing them, such as making someone ill

or making him forget what he has learned, or other such wrongs—or in sexual immorality, such as having someone brought to him for illicit relations—has sought their assistance in sin and aggression. If he seeks their assistance in disbelief, he is a disbeliever; if he seeks their assistance in sins, he is sinful, whether his sin amounts to unrighteousness or falls short of it.

If, however, his knowledge of the Sharia is incomplete and he seeks their assistance in things he supposes to be miraculous gifts—for example, having them assist him in performing Hajj, fly him through the air during innovated devotional listening sessions, carry him to Arafat without his performing the lawful Hajj commanded by Allah and His Messenger, or transport him from one city to another, and the like—then he is deluded, and they have deceived him.

Many such people may not know that these things come from the jinn. They have merely heard that Allah’s allies receive miraculous gifts and perform extraordinary feats. Yet they lack sufficient understanding of the realities of faith and knowledge of the Quran to distinguish miraculous gifts from the Most Merciful from satanic deceptions. The jinn therefore deceive each person according to his beliefs. If he is a polytheist who worships celestial bodies and idols, they lead him to imagine that he benefits from that worship. His intention is to seek the intercession and mediation of the king, prophet, or righteous shaykh in whose likeness the idol was fashioned. He thus considers himself righteous, whereas his worship is, in reality, directed to Satan. Allah Most High says:

“And on the Day He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels, ‘Was it you that these people used to worship?’

They will say, ‘Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not they. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them believed in them.’”

The shaykh and imam, the learned and erudite scholar, the godly sage into whose heart the light of the Quran had been cast, Shaykh al-Islām Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-‘Abbās Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah be pleased with him and grant him contentment—said:

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds—abundant, good and blessed praise, as our Lord loves and is pleased with. I bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and that there is no deity besides Him. I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He chose, selected and guided. May Allah bestow blessings upon him and his family, and abundant peace, until the Day of Judgment.

A Noble Principle Concerning Miracles and Miraculous Favors

Although the term “miracle” encompasses every occurrence that departs from the ordinary course of things, both in its linguistic sense and in the usage of the early imams, such as Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others—who also call such occurrences “signs”—many later scholars distinguish terminologically between the two, reserving the term “miracle”

for a prophet, and “miraculous favor” for a friend of Allah. Both fall under the category of occurrences that depart from the ordinary course of things.

We say: The attributes of perfection fall under three headings: knowledge, power, and self-sufficiency. Alternatively, one may say: knowledge and power. Power is either the ability to act—that is, to bring about effects—or the ability to refrain from acting—that is, self-sufficiency. The first classification is better. These three attributes belong in their perfection to Allah alone: His knowledge encompasses all things, He has power over all things, and He has no need of any of creation.

The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to disclaim any claim to these three attributes, in Allah’s words:

“Say, ‘I do not tell you that I possess Allah’s treasures, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I follow only what is revealed to me.’”

Noah, peace be upon him, said likewise. Noah was the first of the messengers of firm resolve and the first messenger Allah Most High sent to the people of the earth; Muhammad is the last of the messengers and the last of those of firm resolve. Both disclaim these things.

This is because people sometimes demand that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, know the unseen, as in Allah’s words:

“They say, ‘When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?’”

And:

“They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to pass? Say, ‘Knowledge of it rests only with my Lord.’”

At other times, they demand that he bring about effects, as in His words:

“They say, ‘We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us,”

“or you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and cause rivers to flow abundantly through it,”

“or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.’”

" مُكَاشَفَةً "

translated_text:
up to His words:

“Say, ‘Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?’”

At other times, they fault him for having human needs, as in His words:

“They say, ‘What sort of messenger is this, who eats food and walks through the marketplaces? Why has no angel been sent down to him to be a warner alongside him? Or why has no treasure been bestowed upon him, or a garden provided for him to eat from?’”

Allah therefore commanded him to declare that he does not know the unseen, does not possess Allah’s treasures, and is not an angel with no need of food or wealth. He merely follows what is revealed to him. Following what is revealed to him is religion itself: obeying and worshipping Allah in knowledge and action, inwardly and outwardly.

He receives of those three only as much as Allah Most High grants him: he knows what Allah teaches him, can do what Allah enables him to do, and can dispense with whatever Allah frees him from needing, in matters that depart from the regular course of things or from what most people ordinarily experience.

Extraordinary occurrences belonging to the category of knowledge sometimes take the form of Allah enabling a servant to hear what others cannot hear. At other times, the servant sees what others cannot see, whether awake or asleep. At still other times, he knows what others do not know, through revelation and inspiration, or through the imparting of immediate knowledge or accurate discernment.

These experiences are termed unveiling, witnessing, disclosures, and communications: hearing involves communications, seeing involves witnessing, and knowledge involves disclosure. All of this is called “unveiling” and “disclosure,” meaning that the matter has been unveiled to him.

translated_text:
And whatever belongs to the category of “power” involves bringing about effects. This may come through resolve, sincerity, and an answered supplication. It may also be an act of Allah in which the servant has no influence whatsoever, such as the destruction of his enemy without any action on his part, as in His saying:

“Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine has openly declared war on Me. I shall surely avenge My friends as an enraged lion takes vengeance.”

Other examples include making people yield to him and love him, and similar things. The same applies to what belongs to the category of “knowledge and unveiling”: certain aspects of his condition may be disclosed to someone else. Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said concerning glad tidings:

“They are righteous dreams that a righteous man sees or that someone else sees concerning him.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“You are Allah’s witnesses on earth.”

Both “unveiling and the production of effects” may occur within the person himself, or they may not. Rather, Allah may disclose his condition to others and act on his behalf in ways he does not anticipate. As Yūsuf ibn Asbāt said, “No servant is ever sincere with Allah without Allah acting on his behalf.” Ahmad ibn Hanbal also said, “If sincerity were placed upon a wound, it would heal.”

Yet when unveiling or the production of effects occurs in someone else for a person’s sake, that person is also its cause, even if it is in the other person that the ordinary course of things is transcended. The miracles of the prophets, their signs, and the proofs of their prophethood fall within this.

translated_text:
Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was granted every kind of “miracle and extraordinary occurrence.” As for knowledge, reports of the unseen, hearing, and sight, examples include his accounts of the earlier prophets and their peoples, his conversations with those prophets and his experiences with them, and his accounts of people other than prophets, whether friends of Allah or others. These agree with what the People of the Book possess and have inherited through mass transmission or otherwise, without his having learned it from them.

Likewise, his reports concerning divine lordship, the angels, Paradise, and Hell agree with those of the prophets before him, without his having learned from them. Their agreement with what was transmitted from the prophets can sometimes be established through the widely available scriptures in their possession and other accounts transmitted on a mass scale, and sometimes through knowledge held by select scholars among them. In matters such as these, the testimony of the People of the Book may be sought. This is among the wise purposes of allowing them to remain upon payment of the jizya. This is not the place to discuss that in detail.

His reports of matters beyond ordinary perception, both past and present, thus belong to the category of “extraordinary knowledge.” The same applies to his reports of future events, such as the dominion of his community, the fall of the Persian and Roman empires, fighting against the Turks, and thousands upon thousands of other reports he gave.

Some of these are recorded in works on “the proofs of prophethood,” “the Messenger’s biography,” and “his virtues,” as well as works of “Quranic commentary,” “hadith,” and “military campaigns.” Examples include Dalā’il al-Nubuwwa (The Proofs of Prophethood) by Abū Nuʿaym and by al-Bayhaqī, Ibn Ishāq’s biography of the Prophet, hadith works containing chains of transmission such as the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, compiled collections such as Sahīh al-Bukhārī, and other works, including material that

The same applies to what others foretold about him, as found in the books of the earlier prophets. In our time, these comprise twenty-two prophetic writings in the possession of the Jews and Christians, such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the books of Isaiah, Habakkuk, Daniel, and Jeremiah. Likewise, there are the predictions of people other than prophets, including rabbis and monks; reports from the jinn and disembodied voices; and predictions by soothsayers such as Satīh, Shiqq, and others. There are also dreams and their interpretations, such as Chosroes’ dream and the chief Magian priest’s interpretation of it. Similarly, the earlier prophets’ accounts of what had passed and gone by are among the signs of their prophethood.

As for “power and the production of effects,” these concern either the upper world or what lies beneath it. What lies beneath it is either simple or composite. The simple comprises either the atmosphere or the earth; the composite comprises animals, plants, or minerals. Animals, in turn, are either rational or non-rational.

Examples concerning the upper world include the splitting of the moon and the return of the sun for Joshua son of Nun. Another is its return when ʿAlī missed the prayer while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sleeping with his head in his lap—if the hadith is authentic. Some, such as al-Tahāwī and al-Qādī ʿIyād, judged it authentic. Others, such as Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī, classified it as a report stopping at a Companion, and this is the more correct view. His ascension to the heavens is another example.

An extraordinary occurrence, whether an unveiling or an exercise of power, is among the righteous deeds prescribed by religion and divine law—either obligatory or recommended—if it achieves a benefit sought by religion. If it achieves something permissible, it is among Allah’s worldly blessings, which call for gratitude. But if it involves something forbidden or discouraged, it becomes grounds for punishment or abhorrence, as in the account of the man who was given the signs but cast them off: Balʿām ibn Bāʿūrāʾ.

Nevertheless, the person concerned may be excused because of his independent judgment, his reliance on another’s judgment, deficient intellect or knowledge, an overpowering spiritual state, incapacity, or necessity. His case would then resemble that of Barh the worshipper.

The “prohibition” may concern either the means by which the extraordinary occurrence is brought about or its intended purpose. An example of the former is addressing Allah with a forbidden supplication, thereby transgressing against Him. Allah Most High says:

“Call upon your Lord humbly and privately. Indeed, He does not love those who transgress.”

The same applies to forbidden deeds that produce an unveiling or an exercise of power.

The second case includes supplicating against someone for something he does not deserve, or praying that an oppressor be aided and helping him through one’s spiritual resolve—as do the enemy’s protectors and those possessors of spiritual states who assist oppressors. translated_text:
Section

The words of Allah Most High are of “two kinds”: words governing creation and words concerning religion.

His words governing creation are those in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sought refuge when he said:

“I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass.”

He, glorified is He, said:

“His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

And He Most High said:

“And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice.”

The entire universe falls under these words, as do all extraordinary occurrences involving disclosure and the exercise of power.

“The second kind” consists of His words concerning religion: the Quran and the divine law with which Allah sent His Messenger. These comprise His commands, prohibitions, and statements. The servant’s share in them consists in knowing them, acting upon them, and enjoining what Allah has commanded, just as the servant’s share in the first kind, in general and in particular, consists in knowing created things and affecting them—that is, in accordance with those words.

The first kind thus pertains to divine decree and creation, while the second pertains to divine law and religion. Disclosure in the first sphere consists in knowing events in creation; disclosure in the second consists in knowing the commands of divine law. Power in the first sphere consists in bringing about effects in created things; power in the second consists in bringing about effects in religious matters. And just as

 إذَا عُرِفَ هَذَا فَالْأَقْسَامُ ثَلَاثَةٌ:
 إمَّا أَنْ يَتَعَلَّقَ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْقُدْرَةِ أَوْ بِالدِّينِ
translated_text:
the first kind of power is divided into effects upon oneself—such as walking on water, flying through the air, and sitting on fire—and effects upon others, such as causing illness, restoring health, bringing about destruction, enriching, and impoverishing, so too the second kind is divided into effects upon oneself, through obeying Allah and His Messenger and adhering inwardly and outwardly to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and effects upon others, through enjoining obedience to Allah and His Messenger. One is then obeyed in a manner sanctioned by divine law, so that people accept one’s commands to obey Allah and His Messenger through the words concerning religion, just as, in the first case, they accepted what one wished to bring about in them through the words governing creation.

With this established, know that the absence of extraordinary knowledge and power does not harm a Muslim’s religion. If nothing of the unseen is disclosed to him and nothing in creation is subjected to his control, this does not diminish his rank with Allah. Indeed, their absence may be more beneficial to his religion, provided that possessing them is neither obligatory nor recommended in his particular case. By contrast, the absence of religion and of acting upon it leaves a person deficient and blameworthy, either making him deserving of punishment or depriving him of reward. This is because, through knowing religion, teaching it, and enjoining it, the servant attains the pleasure, blessings, and reward of Allah alone. Knowledge of creation and the ability to affect it, however, bring none of this unless they fall within religion. Rather, he may be obliged to give thanks for them, and he may incur sin through them.

Once this is understood, there are three categories:

It pertains either to knowledge and power, or to religion
