 قُلْت:
 فَهَذَا رَجُلٌ كَثِيرُ الشُّرْبِ لِلْخَمْرِ وَمَعَ هَذَا فَلَمَّا كَانَ صَحِيحَ الِاعْتِقَادِ يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ شَهِدَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِذَلِكَ وَنَهَى عَنْ لَعْنِهِ. وَأَمَّا الْمُبْتَدِعُ فَمِثْلُ مَا أَخْرَجَا فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَعَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الخدري وَغَيْرِهِمَا - دَخَلَ حَدِيثُ بَعْضِهِمْ فِي بَعْضٍ - 
{أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يُقَسِّمُ فَجَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ نَاتِئَ الْجَبِينِ كَثَّ اللِّحْيَةِ مَحْلُوقَ الرَّأْسِ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ أَثَرُ السُّجُودِ وَقَالَ مَا قَالَ. فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ ضئضئ هَذَا قَوْمٌ يَحْقِرُ أَحَدَكُمْ صَلَاتَهُ مَعَ صَلَاتِهِمْ وَصِيَامَهُ مَعَ صِيَامِهِمْ وَقِرَاءَتَهُ مَعَ قِرَاءَتِهِمْ يَقْرَءُونَ الْقُرْآنَ لَا يُجَاوِزُ حَنَاجِرَهُمْ يَمْرُقُونَ مِنْ الْإِسْلَامِ كَمَا يَمْرُقُ السَّهْمُ مِنْ الرَّمِيَّةِ؛ لَئِنْ أَدْرَكْتهمْ لَأَقْتُلَنهُمْ قَتْلَ عَادٍ}
 وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ؛ 
{لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ مَاذَا لَهُمْ عَلَى لِسَانِ مُحَمَّدٍ لَنَكَلُوا عَنْ الْعَمَلِ}
 وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ 
{شَرُّ قَتْلَى تَحْتَ أَدِيمِ السَّمَاءِ خَيْرُ قَتْلَى مَنْ قَتَلُوهُ}
 . 
" قُلْت "
: فَهَؤُلَاءِ مَعَ كَثْرَةِ صَلَاتِهِمْ وَصِيَامِهِمْ وَقِرَاءَتِهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ الْعِبَادَةِ وَالزَّهَادَةِ أَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِقَتْلِهِمْ وَقَتَلَهُمْ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
translated_text:
‘May Allah curse him! How often he is brought before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger.’”

I said: Here was a man who frequently drank wine. Yet because his beliefs were sound and he loved Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, testified to this and forbade cursing him.

As for the religious innovator, consider the report recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their two Sahīhs, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, Abū Sa‘īd al-Khudrī, and others—with portions of their narrations combined:

“The Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, was distributing some goods when a man approached him with a prominent brow, a thick beard, a shaved head, and a mark of prostration between his eyes. He said what he said, whereupon the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, declared: ‘From this man’s stock will emerge people whose prayer will make any of you consider his own prayer insignificant, whose fasting will make him consider his own fasting insignificant, and whose recitation will make him consider his own recitation insignificant. They recite the Quran, but it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. If I encounter them, I will certainly kill them as ‘Ād were killed.’”

Another version states:

“If those who fight them knew what Muhammad has promised them, they would cease doing deeds.”

Another version states:

“They are the worst of those slain beneath the sky, while the best of those slain are those whom they kill.”

I said: Despite their abundant prayer, fasting, and recitation, and their devotion to worship and asceticism, the Prophet, may Allah Most High bless him and grant him peace, commanded that they be killed. ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib and those with him from among the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, killed them

original_text:
وَذَلِكَ لِخُرُوجِهِمْ عَنْ سُنَّةِ النَّبِيِّ وَشَرِيعَتِهِ وَأَظُنُّ أَنِّي ذَكَرْت قَوْلَ الشَّافِعِيِّ:
 لِأَنْ يُبْتَلَى الْعَبْدُ بِكُلِّ ذَنْبٍ مَا خَلَا الشِّرْكَ بِاَللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَنْ يُبْتَلَى بِشَيْءِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأَهْوَاءِ.
 فَلَمَّا ظَهَرَ قُبْحُ الْبِدَعِ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَأَنَّهَا أَظْلَمُ مِنْ الزِّنَا وَالسَّرِقَةِ وَشُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ وَأَنَّهُمْ مُبْتَدِعُونَ بِدَعًا مُنْكَرَةً فَيَكُونُ حَالُهُمْ أَسْوَأَ مِنْ حَالِ الزَّانِي وَالسَّارِقِ وَشَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ أَخَذَ شَيْخَهُمْ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ:
 يَا مَوْلَانَا لَا تَتَعَرَّضُ لِهَذَا الْجَنَابِ الْعَزِيزِ - يَعْنِي أَتْبَاعَ أَحْمَد بْنِ الرِّفَاعِيِّ -
 فَقُلْت مُنْكِرًا بِكَلَامِ غَلِيظٍ:
 وَيْحَك؛ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ هُوَ الْجَنَابُ الْعَزِيزُ وَجَنَابُ مَنْ خَالَفَهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعِزِّ يَا ذُو الزرجنة 
(١)
 تُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تُبْطِلُوا دِينَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَقَالَ: يَا مَوْلَانَا يَحْرُقُك الْفُقَرَاءُ بِقُلُوبِهِمْ فَقُلْت: مِثْلَ مَا أَحْرَقَنِي الرَّافِضَةُ لَمَّا قَصَدْت الصُّعُودَ إلَيْهِمْ وَصَارَ جَمِيعُ النَّاسِ يُخَوِّفُونِي مِنْهُمْ وَمِنْ شَرِّهِمْ وَيَقُولُ أَصْحَابُهُمْ إنَّ لَهُمْ سِرًّا مَعَ اللَّهِ فَنَصَرَ اللَّهَ وَأَعَانَ عَلَيْهِمْ. وَكَانَ الْأُمَرَاءُ الْحَاضِرُونَ قَدْ عَرَفُوا بَرَكَةَ مَا يَسَّرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي أَمْرِ غَزْوِ الرَّافِضَةِ بِالْجَبَلِ.
 وَقُلْت لَهُمْ:
 يَا شِبْهَ الرَّافِضَةِ يَا بَيْتَ الْكَذِبِ - فَإِنَّ فِيهِمْ مِنْ الْغُلُوِّ وَالشِّرْكِ وَالْمُرُوقِ عَنْ الشَّرِيعَةِ مَا شَارَكُوا بِهِ الرَّافِضَةَ فِي بَعْضِ صِفَاتِهِمْ وَفِيهِمْ مِنْ الْكَذِبِ مَا قَدْ يُقَارِبُونَ بِهِ الرَّافِضَةَ فِي ذَلِكَ أَوْ يُسَاوُونَهُمْ
original_footnote:
(١) كذا بالأصل. والزرجون: الخمر. أنظر اللسان، مادة " زرجن "
قال الشيخ ناصر بن حمد الفهد (ص ٩٩):
والذي يظهر لي أن العبارة هي (يا ذو الزرجنة)، بمعنى (يا صاحب الخديعة)، فإن الزرجنة - كما في القاموس - التخارج والخب والخديعة.
translated_text:
because they had departed from the Prophet’s Sunnah and his prescribed way. I believe I also mentioned al-Shāfi‘ī’s statement:

“For a servant to be afflicted with every sin other than associating partners with Allah is better than being afflicted with any of these deviant doctrines.”

When the ugliness of religious innovations in Islam became clear—that they are a greater wrong than fornication, theft, and drinking wine, and that these people practised reprehensible innovations, making their condition worse than that of the fornicator, thief, and wine-drinker—their shaykh, ‘Abd Allāh, began saying:

“Our master, do not assail this august company”—meaning the followers of Ahmad ibn al-Rifā‘ī.

I rebuked him harshly:

“Woe to you! What is this ‘august company’? Those who oppose them are more deserving of honour, you trickster (1)! You want to nullify the religion of Allah and His Messenger!”

He said, “Our master, the Sufis will burn you with their hearts.”

I replied, “Just as the Rāfidah burned me when I intended to ascend to their mountain! Everyone began warning me about them and their evil, while their followers said that they had a secret between themselves and Allah. Yet Allah granted me victory and helped me against them.”

The commanders present already knew the blessings of what Allah had facilitated in the campaign against the Rāfidah in the mountain.

I said to them:

“You who resemble the Rāfidah! You house of lies!”

For their extremism, their association of partners with Allah, and their departure from the prescribed religious law give them some of the same characteristics as the Rāfidah; and their lying is such that they may approach the Rāfidah in this respect or equal them
translated_footnote:
(1) Thus in the original. Al-zarjūn means wine. See Lisān al-ʿArab, under the root z-r-j-n.
Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd states (p. 99):
“It seems to me that the wording is yā dhū al-zarjana (‘O master of deceit’), since al-zarjana—as defined in al-Qāmūs—means evasion, guile, and deception.”

أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ مِنْ أَكْذَبِ الطَّوَائِفِ حَتَّى قِيلَ فِيهِمْ:
 لَا تَقُولُوا أَكْذَبَ مِنْ الْيَهُودِ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا أَكْذَبَ مِنْ الْأَحْمَدِيَّةِ عَلَى شَيْخِهِمْ وَقُلْت لَهُمْ: أَنَا كَافِرٌ بِكُمْ وَبِأَحْوَالِكُمْ 
{فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ لَا تُنْظِرُونِ}
 . وَلَمَّا رَدَدْت عَلَيْهِمْ الْأَحَادِيثَ الْمَكْذُوبَةَ أَخَذُوا يَطْلُبُونَ مِنِّي كُتُبًا صَحِيحَةً لِيَهْتَدُوا بِهَا فَبَذَلْت لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ وَأُعِيدُ الْكَلَامُ أَنَّهُ مَنْ خَرَجَ عَنْ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ ضَرَبْت عُنُقَهُ وَأَعَادَ الْأَمِيرُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَاسْتَقَرَّ الْكَلَامُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ. وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَ وَعْدَهُ وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ.
translated_text:
or even surpass them, for they are among the most deceitful groups. It has even been said of them:

“Do not say, ‘More deceitful than the Jews in their lies about Allah,’ but rather, ‘More deceitful than the Ahmadiyyah in their lies about their shaykh.’”

I said to them: “I disavow you and your spiritual states. ‘So plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite.’”

When I refuted the fabricated hadiths they cited, they began asking me for reliable books by which they could be guided, and I made these available to them. It was reiterated that I would behead anyone who departed from the Book and the Sunnah. The commander repeated these words, and the matter was settled on that basis.

All praise is due to Allah, who fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, and routed the confederates by Himself.

عَنْ 
" الْمُرْشِدَةِ "
 كَيْفَ كَانَ أَصْلُهَا وَتَأْلِيفُهَا؟ وَهَلْ تَجُوزُ قِرَاءَتُهَا أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -
 قَائِلًا:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ،
 أَصْلُ هَذِهِ:
 أَنَّهُ وَضَعَهَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ التومرت الَّذِي تَلَقَّبَ بِالْمَهْدِيِّ وَكَانَ قَدْ ظَهَرَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فِي أَوَائِلِ الْمِائَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ مِنْ نَحْوِ مِائَتَيْ سَنَةٍ وَكَانَ قَدْ دَخَلَ إلَى بِلَادِ الْعِرَاقِ وَتَعَلَّمَ طَرَفًا مِنْ الْعِلْمِ وَكَانَ فِيهِ طَرَفٌ مِنْ الزُّهْدِ وَالْعِبَادَةِ. وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ إلَى الْمَغْرِبِ صَعِدَ إلَى جِبَالِ الْمَغْرِبِ؛ إلَى قَوْمٍ مِنْ الْبَرْبَرِ
translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām and defender of the Sunnah, peerless in his age and an ocean of knowledge, one of the remaining masters of independent legal reasoning and an authority for later generations, the crown of those who know Allah and the exemplar of discerning scholars, the scholar to whom seekers journey and the choicest of those firmly grounded in knowledge, the leader of ascetics and the ideal of those who strive, the luminous and authoritative imam, the godly scholar qualified for independent legal reasoning, Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-Abbās Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halīm ibn Abd al-Salām ibn Taymiyyah al-Harrānī—may Allah preserve his exalted standing in this world and the next, and grant him ascent to the summit of perfection, joyful at heart and wholly content—was asked:

“Concerning al-Murshidah (The Guide): how did it originate and come to be composed? Is it permissible to read it or not?”

He replied—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Its origins are as follows: it was composed by Abū Abd Allāh Muhammad ibn Abd Allāh ibn al-Tūmart, who assumed the title of al-Mahdī. He had emerged in the Maghreb in the early fifth century AH, some two hundred years ago. He had travelled to Iraq and acquired some knowledge, and he possessed a measure of asceticism and devotion to worship. When he returned to the Maghreb, he went up into its mountains, to a group of Berbers

وَغَيْرُهُمْ:
 جُهَّالٍ لَا يَعْرِفُونَ مِنْ دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ إلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ فَعَلَّمَهُمْ الصَّلَاةَ وَالزَّكَاةَ وَالصِّيَامَ وَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ شَرَائِعِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَاسْتَجَازَ أَنْ يُظْهِرَ لَهُمْ أَنْوَاعًا مِنْ المخاريق لِيَدْعُوَهُمْ بِهَا إلَى الدِّينِ فَصَارَ يَجِيءُ إلَى الْمَقَابِرِ يَدْفِنُ بِهَا أَقْوَامًا وَيُوَاطِئُهُمْ عَلَى أَنْ يُكَلِّمُوهُ إذَا دَعَاهُمْ وَيَشْهَدُوا لَهُ بِمَا طَلَبَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِثْلَ أَنْ يَشْهَدُوا لَهُ بِأَنَّهُ الْمَهْدِيُّ الَّذِي بَشَّرَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الَّذِي يُوَاطِئُ اسْمُهُ اسْمَهُ وَاسْمُ أَبِيهِ اسْمَ أَبِيهِ. وَأَنَّهُ الَّذِي يَمْلَأُ الْأَرْضَ قِسْطًا وَعَدْلًا كَمَا مُلِئَتْ جَوْرًا وَظُلْمًا. وَأَنَّ مَنْ اتَّبَعَهُ أَفْلَحَ وَمَنْ خَالَفَهُ خَسِرَ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْكَلَامِ. فَإِذَا اعْتَقَدَ أُولَئِكَ الْبَرْبَرُ أَنَّ الْمَوْتَى يُكَلِّمُونَهُ وَيَشْهَدُونَ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ عَظُمَ اعْتِقَادُهُمْ فِيهِ وَطَاعَتُهُمْ لِأَمْرِهِ. ثُمَّ إنَّ أُولَئِكَ الْمَقْبُورِينَ يَهْدِمُ عَلَيْهِمْ الْقُبُورَ لِيَمُوتُوا وَلَا يُظْهِرُوا أَمْرَهُ وَاعْتَقِدَ أَنَّ دِمَاءَ أُولَئِكَ مُبَاحَةٌ بِدُونِ هَذَا وَأَنَّهُ يَجُوزُ لَهُ إظْهَارُ هَذَا الْبَاطِلِ لِيَقُومَ أُولَئِكَ الْجُهَّالُ بِنَصْرِهِ وَاتِّبَاعِهِ. وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ عَنْهُ أَهْلُ الْمَغْرِبِ وَأَهْلُ الْمَشْرِقِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرُوا أَخْبَارَهُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْحِكَايَاتِ أَنْوَاعًا. وَهِيَ مَشْهُورَةٌ عِنْدَ مَنْ يَعْرِفُ حَالَهُ عَنْهُ. وَمِنْ الْحِكَايَاتِ الَّتِي يَأْثُرُونَهَا عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ وَاطَأَ رَجُلًا عَلَى إظْهَارِ الْجُنُونِ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَالِمًا يَحْفَظُ الْقُرْآنَ وَالْحَدِيثَ وَالْفِقْهَ فَظَهَرَ بِصُورَةِ الْجُنُونِ وَالنَّاسُ لَا يَعْرِفُونَهُ إلَّا مَجْنُونًا. ثُمَّ أَصْبَحَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ وَهُوَ عَاقِلٌ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَالْحَدِيثَ وَالْفِقْهَ وَزَعَمَ أَنَّهُ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْمَنَامِ وَعُوفِيَ مِمَّا كَانَ
translated_text:
and others—ignorant people who knew of the religion of Islam only what Allah willed. He taught them prayer, zakāh, fasting, and other prescribed duties of Islam. He considered it permissible to perform various deceptive tricks before them in order to call them to the religion. He would go to graveyards and bury people there, having secretly arranged with them to speak to him when he called them and to testify to whatever he requested. For example, they would testify that he was the Mahdī foretold by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whose name would match the Messenger’s name and whose father’s name would match that of the Messenger’s father; that he would fill the earth with equity and justice just as it had been filled with oppression and injustice; and that whoever followed him would prosper, while whoever opposed him would lose, and other such statements.

Once those Berbers believed that the dead spoke to him and testified on his behalf in this way, their faith in him and obedience to his commands grew stronger. He would then collapse the graves upon those buried inside, so that they would die and not expose his deception. He believed that it was permissible to shed their blood even apart from this, and that he was entitled to display this falsehood so that those ignorant people would support and follow him.

Those in the Maghreb and the East who recorded accounts of his life related various stories of this kind about him. They are well known among those familiar with his circumstances.

Among the stories they relate about him is that he secretly arranged with a man to feign madness. This man was a scholar who had memorized the Quran, hadith, and jurisprudence. He presented himself as mad, and people knew him only as a madman. Then one morning he appeared perfectly sane, reciting the Quran, hadith, and jurisprudence. He claimed that he had learned all this in a dream and had been cured of what had afflicted him

, and it is also reported that he told them that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had taught him this. They thus came to think highly of that man.

It is also related that they had a day they called the Day of Distinction, on which he supposedly distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Anyone they knew to be one of their allies they counted among the people of Paradise and spared his life; anyone they knew to be one of their enemies they counted among the people of the Fire and deemed it lawful to kill.

He deemed it lawful to shed the blood of many thousands of Mālikīs in the Maghreb who adhered to the Book and the Sunnah, following the school of Mālik and the people of Medina. They studied the Quran, hadith—including the two Sahīh collections, al-Muwatta’, and other works—and jurisprudence according to the school of the people of Medina. Yet he claimed that they likened Allah to His creation and attributed a body to Him, although they did not hold such views. Nor is any follower of Mālik known to have openly professed that Allah resembles His creation or has a body.

On the strength of this interpretation and similar ones, he also deemed it lawful to seize their property and commit other forbidden acts. This resembled the violations against Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamā‘ah that the Jahmiyyah, who denied the divine attributes—including the philosophers, the Mu‘tazilah, and all other deniers of the attributes—deemed lawful when they subjected people to an inquisition during “the caliphate of al-Ma’mūn.” They openly proclaimed that the Quran was created and that Allah would not be seen in the Hereafter. They denied that Allah has knowledge, power, speech, will, or any other attributes subsisting in His essence.

Anyone who agreed with them in this denial of the attributes had his life and property protected by them. They appointed him to public offices, granted him a stipend from the public treasury, accepted his testimony, and ransomed him from

 يَقُولُونَ:
 هَذَا مُشَبِّهٌ؛
 هَذَا مُجَسِّمٌ لِقَوْلِهِ:
 إنَّ اللَّهَ يُرَى فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ غَيْرُ مَخْلُوقٍ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ. فَدَامَتْ هَذِهِ الْمِحْنَةُ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِضْعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً فِي أَوَاخِرِ خِلَافَةِ الْمَأْمُونِ وَخِلَافَةِ أَخِيهِ الْمُعْتَصِمِ وَالْوَاثِقِ بْنِ الْمُعْتَصِمِ ثُمَّ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى كَشَفَ الْغُمَّةَ عَنْ الْأُمَّةِ فِي وِلَايَةِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ عَلَى اللَّهِ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَامَّةَ خُلَفَاءِ بَنِي الْعَبَّاسِ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دُونَ ذُرِّيَّةِ الَّذِينَ أَقَامُوا الْمِحْنَةَ لِأَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ. فَأَمَرَ الْمُتَوَكِّلُ بِرَفْعِ الْمِحْنَةِ وَإِظْهَارِ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَأَنْ يُرْوَى مَا ثَبَتَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَالصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ مِنْ الْإِثْبَاتِ النَّافِي لِلتَّعْطِيلِ.

 لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ وَلَا يَقُولُونَ: وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ وَأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَمْتَحِنُونَ النَّاسَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: 
{لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ}
 فَإِذَا قَالُوا وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ أَنْكَرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَذْهَبُ سَلَفِ الْأُمَّةِ وَأَئِمَّتِهَا أَنْ يُوصَفَ اللَّهُ بِمَا وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ وَبِمَا وَصَفَهُ بِهِ رَسُولُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تَحْرِيفٍ وَلَا تَعْطِيلٍ وَمِنْ غَيْرِ
translated_text:
captivity. Anyone who did not agree with them that the Quran was created, or with the other innovations that followed from this, they killed, imprisoned, beat, or denied a stipend from the public treasury. They would not appoint him to any public office, accept his testimony, or ransom him from the disbelievers.

They would say, “This man likens Allah to His creation; this man attributes a body to Him,” because he said that Allah would be seen in the Hereafter, that the Quran was the speech of Allah, uncreated, that Allah rose over the Throne, and similar things. This inquisition against the Muslims continued for ten-odd years, during the latter part of al-Ma’mūn’s caliphate and the caliphates of his brother al-Mu‘tasim and al-Wāthiq ibn al-Mu‘tasim. Then Allah Most High lifted this affliction from the community during the reign of al-Mutawakkil ‘alā Allāh, whose descendants Allah made to constitute most of the Abbasid caliphs, rather than the descendants of those who had subjected Ahl al-Sunnah to the inquisition. Al-Mutawakkil ordered that the inquisition be ended, that the Book and the Sunnah be openly proclaimed, and that the authentic reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the Companions, and the Successors affirming the divine attributes and rejecting their denial be transmitted.

Those Jahmiyyah who denied the divine attributes had gone so far in altering the religion that they would write on the coverings of the Kaaba, “There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise,” rather than saying, “And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.” They would also test people with the words of Allah Most High:

“There is nothing like unto Him.”

If they continued, “And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing,” they would rebuke them.

The position of the early generations of this community and its imams is that Allah is to be described as He has described Himself and as His Messenger has described Him, without distortion or denial, and without

specifying how His attributes are or likening them to those of creation. They do not deny of Allah what He has affirmed of Himself, nor do they liken His attributes to those of His creation. Rather, they know that nothing is like Allah—in His essence, His attributes, or His actions. Just as His essence does not resemble other essences, His attributes do not resemble other attributes. Allah Most High sent the messengers, who described Him through detailed affirmation and general negation.

The enemies of the messengers—the Jahmiyyah, the philosophers, and others like them—described Him through detailed negation and general affirmation.

For Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has stated in His Book that He knows all things; that He has power over all things; that He is the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all; that He is the Almighty, the All-Wise; that He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful; and that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He has stated that He loves the God-fearing, those who do good, and the patient; that He does not love corruption and does not approve of disbelief for His servants; that He is pleased with the believers and they are pleased with Him; that He is angry with the disbelievers and curses them; that good words ascend to Him and righteous deeds raise them; that He spoke directly to Moses; and that the Trustworthy Spirit brought the Quran down from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

As He says:

“Say, ‘The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth.’”

The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, as He says in another verse:

“Say, ‘Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel—it is he who brought it down upon your heart by Allah’s permission, confirming what came before it.’”

And He Most High says:

“The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, so that you may be one of the warners.”

And He Most High says:

“On that Day, some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord.”

And He Most High says:

“For those who do good is the finest reward, and more.”

 وَقَدْ اسْتَفَاضَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الصِّحَاحِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:

 وَ 
{إنَّ النَّاسَ قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؛ هَلْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ؟

 قَالُوا:

 قَالُوا:
 لَا.

 فَشَبَّهَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الرُّؤْيَةَ بِالرُّؤْيَةِ وَلَمْ يُشَبِّهْ الْمَرْئِيَّ بِالْمَرْئِيِّ؛ فَإِنَّ الْعِبَادَ لَا يُحِيطُونَ بِاَللَّهِ عِلْمًا؛ وَلَا تُدْرِكُهُ أَبْصَارُهُمْ.
 كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى:
 
{لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ}
 .
 وَقَدْ قَالَ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ:
 مِنْ السَّلَفِ وَالْعُلَمَاءِ إنَّ 
" الْإِدْرَاكَ "
 هُوَ الْإِحَاطَةُ فَالْعِبَادُ يَرَوْنَ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى عِيَانًا وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ فَهَذَا وَأَمْثَالُهُ مِمَّا أَخْبَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَرَسُولُهُ.
 وَقَالَ تَعَالَى فِي النَّفْيِ:
 
{لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ}
 
{فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا}
translated_text:
And it is authentically reported in Sahīh Muslim, on the authority of Suhayb, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will announce, ‘O people of Paradise, Allah has made you a promise that He wishes to fulfil for you.’ They will say, ‘What is it? Has He not brightened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us to Paradise, and protected us from the Fire?’” He continued, “Then the veil will be lifted, and they will look upon Him. He will have given them nothing dearer to them than looking upon Him; this is the ‘more.’”

It has also been widely transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic hadith collections that he said:

“You will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night when it is full, having no difficulty seeing Him.”

And that the people said, “O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?” He said, “Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun in a clear sky, with no clouds obscuring it?” They said, “No.” He said, “Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon in a clear sky, with no clouds obscuring it?” They said, “No.” He said, “You will indeed see your Lord just as you see the sun and the moon.”

Thus he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, likened the act of seeing to the act of seeing; he did not liken the One seen to the things seen. For the servants cannot encompass Allah in knowledge, nor can their vision comprehend Him. As He Most High says:

“Vision does not comprehend Him, but He comprehends all vision.”

A number of the early generations and scholars have stated that “comprehension” means encompassing. Thus the servants will see Allah Most High with their own eyes, but they will not encompass Him. These and similar matters are among those that Allah and His Messenger have told us.

And He Most High says by way of negation:

“There is nothing like Him.”

“So do not set up rivals to Allah.”

translated_text:
“Do you know of any equal to Him?”

“And there is none comparable to Him.”

In these verses, He makes clear that Allah has no equal, no rival, no likeness, and no peer.

Whoever says, “Allah’s knowledge is like my knowledge, His power is like my power, His speech is like my speech, His will, love, pleasure, and anger are like my will, love, pleasure, and anger, His rising over the Throne is like my rising, His descent is like my descent, or His coming is like my coming,” or anything similar, has likened Allah to His creation and made Him their equal. Exalted is Allah above what they say! Such a person is misguided, wicked, and an advocate of falsehood—indeed, a disbeliever.

Whoever says, “Allah has no knowledge, power, speech, will, hearing, sight, love, pleasure, anger, rising over the Throne, coming, or descent,” has denied Allah’s most beautiful names and most exalted attributes and deviated concerning His names and signs. Such a person is misguided, wicked, and an advocate of falsehood—indeed, a disbeliever.

Rather, the position of the leading scholars and the early generations is to affirm the attributes while rejecting any likeness to created beings: affirmation without likening Him to creation, and declaring Him free of imperfection without denying His attributes. As Nu'aym ibn Hammād al-Khuzā'ī, al-Bukhārī’s teacher, said:

“Whoever likens Allah to His creation has disbelieved, and whoever denies what Allah has described Himself with has disbelieved. Nothing with which Allah has described Himself, or His Messenger has described Him, constitutes likening Him to creation.”

What further clarifies this is that Allah Most High has told us that in Paradise there are water, milk, wine, honey, meat, fruit, silk, gold, silver, and other things. the created things in Paradise share names with the created things in this world, while their realities are not alike, how could the Creator be like a created being merely because He shares a name with it?

Allah Most High has described Himself as All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and has described the human being as hearing and seeing; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as living, and some of His servants as living; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as compassionate and merciful, and His Prophet as compassionate and merciful; yet the one is not like the other. He has described Himself as knowing and forbearing, and some of His servants as knowing and forbearing; yet the one is not like the other. He has called Himself the King, and has called some of His servants kings; yet the one is not like the other.

Such examples abound in the Quran and Sunnah. This, then, was the position of the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars, including the imams of the schools of law, such as Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, and others: affirmation without likening Him to creation, and declaring Him free of imperfection without denying His attributes. They neither adopted the position of those who deny His attributes nor that of those who liken the Creator to created beings. This is the way of the messengers and those who believe in them.

As for the philosophers and others like them who oppose the messengers—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them—they describe the Lord Most High through “negative attributes”: He is not this, not that, not such-and-such. They do not describe Him with any affirmative attributes, but only through negations that could equally describe what does not exist. translated_text:
distinction between what they affirm and what does not exist. Yet they say, “He exists; He is not nonexistent.” Thus they contradict themselves, affirming Him in one respect and denying Him in another.

They also say, “He is absolute existence, distinguished by no attribute.” Yet people know that what is absolute cannot exist in reality, for nothing that exists is absolute, without any particular identity or distinction from anything else. Such a thing exists only in a person’s mental conceptions: one conceives of something absolute, even though it has no reality outside the mind. Thus these philosophizing Jahmīs who deny the divine attributes do not acknowledge the Creator—glorified and exalted is He—as existing apart from His creation. Rather, they either make Him an absolute conceived in people’s minds, make Him indwell created things, or say that He is the very existence of created things.

It is known that Allah existed before He created His creatures. When He created them, He did not enter into them, nor did He bring them into Himself. Nothing of His essence is within His creatures, and nothing of His creatures is within His essence. This is what the Quran and Sunnah indicate, and what the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars unanimously affirmed.

The Jahmī deniers of the divine attributes among the philosophers, the Mu‘tazilah, and others—who subjected the Muslims to the ordeal mentioned earlier—held this misguided position. When Allah Most High granted the people of the Sunnah and the community ascendancy and victory, this denial remained in the hearts of many of their followers. They consequently began to appear at times alongside the esotericist Qarmatian Rāfidah, at times alongside the Jahmī proponents of union between God and creation, and at times to agree with them

This was also the belief of the author of al-Murshidah (The Guide), as he explicitly stated in a lengthy book in which he explained his position on this matter. There he stated that Allah Most High is absolute existence, as Ibn Sīnā, Ibn Sab‘īn, and others like them maintain.

For this reason, his al-Murshidah does not mention the belief set forth by the leading scholars of knowledge and religion among the people of the Sunnah and the community: scholars of hadith, jurisprudence, Sufism, speculative theology, and others among the followers of the four imams and beyond. This belief is stated by the leading Hanafī, Mālikī, Shāfi‘ī, and Hanbalī scholars; the speculative theologians among the Kullābīs, Ash‘arīs, Karrāmīs, and others; the masters of Sufism and asceticism; and the scholars of hadith. All of them agree that Allah Most High is living, knows by His knowledge, and is powerful by His power.

As Allah Most High says:

“And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.”

And He says:

“But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you: He sent it down with His knowledge.”

And He says:

“No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge.”

And He says:

“Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?”

And He says:

“And the heaven We built with strength”—that is, with power.

translated_text:
‘When any of you intends to undertake a matter, let him pray two units of prayer other than the obligatory prayer. Then let him say:

O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your immense bounty. You have power, and I have none; You know, and I do not; and You are the Knower of all unseen things. O Allah, if You know that this matter—and he should name it—is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. But if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it. Decree what is good for me wherever it may be, then make me content with it.’”

The four imams and all the others mentioned agree that Allah Most High will be seen in the Hereafter and that the Quran is the speech of Allah. Yet the author of al-Murshidah mentions none of the affirmations upheld by the various groups among the people of the Sunnah and the community. Nor does he mention belief in the prophethood of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—or in the Last Day and what the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—reported concerning Paradise and Hell, resurrection and reckoning, the trial of the grave, the Cistern, and the Prophet’s intercession—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—for those guilty of major sins. All these fundamentals are agreed upon among the people of the Sunnah and the community, and their scholars customarily include them in concise statements of creed. Instead, he restricted its contents to what accords with his foundational position: that Allah is absolute existence. This is the position of the philosophers and the Jahmīs

translated_text:
and the Shia and others like them, whose views the various groups of the people of the Sunnah and the community—including the adherents of the four schools and others—have unanimously rejected as false, judging them to be misguided.

In it, he presented the statements of those who deny the divine attributes, without mentioning a single affirmative attribute of Allah Most High. At its beginning, he claimed that every legally accountable person is obliged to know these things. Yet the imams agree that Muslims are obliged only to fulfil what Allah and His Messenger have made obligatory. No one may impose upon Muslims anything that Allah and His Messenger have not made obligatory. Some of his statements concern matters mentioned by Allah and His Messenger, which must therefore be believed. Others have not been mentioned by Allah, His Messenger, or any of the early generations and imams. People are therefore not obliged to profess what Allah has not obliged them to profess.

A person may make a statement that is true, yet not everyone is obliged to profess it, nor may he oblige people to do so. How much more objectionable is this when the statement contains falsehood? The negations he sets out contain both truth and falsehood: the truth must be followed, and the falsehood must be avoided. We have discussed this at length in a substantial book.

We have also explained why he called his followers al-Muwahhidūn (“those who affirm Allah’s oneness”). This is among the things Muslims have objected to, for the entire community of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—affirms Allah’s oneness, and none of those who affirm His oneness will remain in the Fire forever.

And tawhīd (affirming Allah’s oneness) is what Allah Most High has explained in His Book and through His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—as in His words:

“Say, ‘He is Allah, the One; Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.’”

This surah is equivalent to one-third of the Quran. And His words:

“Say, ‘O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship. Nor will I worship what you have worshipped, nor will you worship what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“So know that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and women.”

And He says:

“We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me, so worship Me.’”

The Jahmī deniers of the divine attributes, among the Muʿtazilah and others, called the negation of the attributes tawhīd. Thus, anyone who says that the Quran is Allah’s speech and is not created, or that Allah will be seen in the Hereafter, or says, “I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and ask You to grant me ability through Your power,” is not, in their view, someone who affirms Allah’s oneness. Rather, they call him someone who likens Allah to creation and ascribes a body to Him. The author of al-Murshidah called his followers al-Muwahhidūn, following those who invented a tawhīd for which Allah had sent down no authority and deviated from the tawhīd with which Allah revealed the Quran.

He also said concerning Allah Most High’s power that He has power over whatever He wills. This agrees with the view of the philosophers, ʿAlī al-Aswārī, and other speculative theologians who say that He has no power to do anything other than what He has done. The position of the Muslims, however, is that Allah has power over

all things, whether He wills them or not. As the Most High says:

“Say, ‘He has power to send punishment upon you from above you or from beneath your feet, or to divide you into factions.’”

It is authentically reported in al-Sahīh that when the words of the Most High were revealed, “Say, ‘He has power to send punishment upon you from above you,’” the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said, “I seek refuge in Your Face.” At “or from beneath your feet,” he said, “I seek refuge in Your Face.” At “or to divide you into factions and make you taste one another’s violence,” he said, “These two are less severe.”

They said: Allah thus has power to do both, although He does not will to do them. Indeed, Allah has assured this community, through its Prophet, that He will neither set against them an enemy from outside their ranks who would annihilate them, nor destroy them through a famine encompassing them all.

The Most High has also said:

“Does man think that We will not gather his bones? Yes indeed; We are able even to make his fingers level.”

Allah has power to do that, although He does not will it. The Most High has also said:

“Had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance.”

And the Most High says:

“Had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community.”

Allah Most High has power to do that: had He willed it, He would have brought it about through His power, but He does not will it.

In another book, we have explained what he said in it, word by word, and clarified what is correct, what is mistaken, and what is ambiguous in its wording.

Thus, a scholar who understands the true nature of its contents and knows what the Book and the Sunnah teach will not be harmed by it, for he gives everything its due. No Muslim needs to study or read it. Nor may anyone turn away from what the Book and the Sunnah teach, and what the early generations of this community and its imams agreed upon, in favour of what some people have introduced, which may contain something contrary to that or lead people to oppose it. No one may devise a creed or a form of worship for people on his own authority. Rather, he must follow, not innovate, and take guidance from established example, not originate his own. For Allah, glorified be He, sent Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as a witness.

He said to him:

“Say, ‘This is my way: I call to Allah with clear insight—I and those who follow me.’”

And the Most High said:

“Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.”

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—taught the Muslims everything they needed concerning their religion. Muslims therefore take their entire religion—beliefs, acts of worship, and everything else—from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and what the early generations of this community and its imams agreed upon. None of this contradicts sound reason, for whatever contradicts sound reason is false, and there is no falsehood in the Book, the Sunnah, or scholarly consensus. They do, however, contain expressions that some people may not understand, or from which they may derive a false meaning. The fault lies with those people, not with the Book and the Sunnah; for

Allah Most High has said:

“We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, and as guidance, mercy, and good news for the Muslims.”

And Allah knows best. All praise belongs to Allah alone. May His blessings and peace be upon our master Muhammad, his family, and his Companions. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. My success comes only through Allah. In Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn.

He was asked about a man who had a discussion with another person concerning those who read al-Murshida (The Guide). The first said, “Some scholars have said that we are not permitted to read al-Murshida.” The other said, “Whoever does not read it is a disbeliever.”

The answer:

All praise belongs to Allah.

As for the second speaker, who said, “Whoever does not read it is a disbeliever,” he is a liar, misguided, mistaken, and ignorant. He must be called upon to repent of such a statement. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he must receive a severe punishment that deters him and others like him from saying such things.

Indeed, if the implications of his statement, “Whoever does not read it is a disbeliever,” are understood, and he persists in it after becoming aware of them, then he himself is the disbeliever who must be called upon to repent. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death. And Allah knows best.

 فَهُمْ قَوْمٌ اقْتَرَنَتْ بِهِمْ الشَّيَاطِينُ كَمَا يَقْتَرِنُونَ بِإِخْوَانِهِمْ؛ فَإِذَا حَضَرُوا سَمَاعَ الْمُكَاءِ وَالتَّصْدِيَةِ أَخَذَهُمْ الْحَالُ فَيَزِيدُونَ وَيَرْغُونَ. كَمَا يَفْعَلُهُ الْمَصْرُوعُ. وَيَتَكَلَّمُونَ بِكَلَامِ لَا يَفْهَمُونَهُ هُمْ وَلَا الْحَاضِرُونَ؛ وَهِيَ شَيَاطِينُهُمْ تَتَكَلَّمُ عَلَى أَلْسِنَتِهِمْ عِنْدَ غَيْبَةِ عُقُولِهِمْ كَمَا يَتَكَلَّمُ الْجِنِّيُّ عَلَى لِسَانِ الْمَصْرُوعِ وَلَهُمْ مُشَابِهُونَ فِي الْهِنْد مِنْ عُبَّادِ الْأَصْنَامِ وَمُشَابِهُونَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ يُسَمَّى أَحَدُهُمْ الْمُصَلِّي؛ وَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ مِنْ جِنْسِ الزُّطِّ الَّذِينَ لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ؛ فَإِذَا كَانَ لِبَعْضِ النَّاسِ مَصْرُوعٌ أَوْ نَحْوُهُ أَعْطَاهُمْ شَيْئًا فَيَجِيئُونَ وَيَضْرِبُونَ لَهُمْ بِالدُّفِّ وَالْمَلَاهِي وَيَحْرُقُونَ وَيُوقِدُونَ نَارًا عَظِيمَةً مُؤَجَّجَةً وَيَضَعُونَ فِيهَا الْحَدِيدَ الْعَظِيمَ حَتَّى يَبْقَى أَعْظَمَ مِنْ الْجَمْرِ وَيَنْصِبُونَ رِمَاحًا فِيهَا أَسِنَّةٌ ثُمَّ يَصْعَدُ أَحَدُهُمْ يَقْعُدُ فَوْقَ أَسِنَّةِ الرِّمَاحِ قُدَّامَ النَّاسِ وَيَأْخُذُ ذَلِكَ الْحَدِيدَ الْمَحْمِيَّ وَيُمِرُّهُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ وَأَنْوَاعِ ذَلِكَ. وَيَرَى النَّاسُ حِجَارَةً يُرْمَى بِهَا وَلَا يَرَوْنَ مَنْ رَمَى بِهَا وَذَلِكَ مِنْ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ الَّذِينَ يَصْعَدُونَ بِهِمْ فَوْقَ الرُّمْحِ وَهُمْ الَّذِينَ يُبَاشِرُونَ النَّارَ وَأُولَئِكَ قَدْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ بِذَلِكَ كَالْمَصْرُوعِ الَّذِي يَضْرِبُ ضَرْبًا وَجِيعًا وَهُوَ لَا يُحِسُّ بِذَلِكَ؛ لِأَنَّ الضَّرْبَ يَقَعُ عَلَى الْجِنِّيِّ فَكَذَا حَالُ أَهْلِ الْأَحْوَالِ الشَّيْطَانِيَّةِ وَلِهَذَا كُلَّمَا كَانَ الرَّجُلُ أَشْبَهَ بِالْجِنِّ وَالشَّيَاطِينِ كَانَ حَالُهُ أَقْوَى وَلَا يَأْتِيهِمْ الْحَالُ إلَّا عِنْدَ مُؤَذِّنِ الشَّيْطَانِ وَقُرْآنِهِ فَمُؤَذِّنُهُ الْمِزْمَارُ وَقُرْآنُهُ الْغِنَاءُ.
translated_text:
among them, they are people to whom devils have attached themselves, just as they attach themselves to their brethren. When they attend gatherings of whistling and clapping, the state seizes them; they grow more frenzied and bellow, as a possessed person does. They utter words that neither they nor those present understand. It is their devils speaking through their tongues while their reason is absent, just as a jinn speaks through the tongue of a possessed person.

They have counterparts among the idol worshippers of India, and others in the Maghrib, each of whom is called al-Musallī. These people in the Maghrib are of the same kind as the Zutt, who have no share of good. If someone has a possessed person or someone similarly afflicted in his household, he gives them something. They then come and play frame drums and musical instruments for them. They burn things and kindle a great, blazing fire, placing large pieces of iron in it until they become hotter than glowing embers. They set up spears with sharp points; then one of them climbs up and sits on the spearheads before the people. He takes that heated iron and passes it over his hands, and performs other such feats.

People see stones being thrown without seeing who throws them. This is the work of their devils, who lift them onto the spear and are themselves the ones in direct contact with the fire. Those people may be unaware of this, like a possessed person who is beaten severely yet feels nothing, because the blows fall upon the jinn. Such is the condition of those who experience satanic states. Thus, the more closely a man resembles the jinn and devils, the stronger his state becomes. This state comes upon them only in the presence of Satan’s caller to prayer and his Quran: his caller to prayer is the pipe, and his Quran is singing.

 مِنْهُمْ: فَهُمْ يَصْنَعُونَ أَدْوِيَةً كَحَجَرِ الطَّلَقِ وَدُهْنِ الضَّفَادِعِ وَقُشُورِ النَّارِنْجِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ. يَمْشُونَ بِهَا عَلَى النَّارِ وَيُمْسِكُونَ نَوْعًا مِنْ الْحَيَّاتِ يَأْخُذُونَهَا بِضْعَةً وَيَقْدُمُونَ عَلَى أَكْلِهَا بِفُجُورِ وَمَا يَصْنَعُونَهُ مِنْ السُّكَّرِ وَاللَّاذَنِ وَمَاءِ الْوَرْدِ وَمَاءِ الزَّعْفَرَانِ وَالدَّمِ فَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ حِيَلٌ وَشَعْوَذَةٌ يَعْرِفُهَا الْخَبِيرُ بِهَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ. وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ تَأْتِيه الشَّيَاطِينُ وَذَلِكَ هُمْ أَهْلُ الْمُحَالِ الشَّيْطَانِيِّ.

Nor does this state come upon them during prayer, remembrance of Allah, supplication, or Quran recitation. These states bring no benefit in religious or worldly affairs. If their states were of the same kind as those experienced by Allah’s righteous servants and His pious allies, they would arise during the religious acts of worship Allah has commanded. They would also bring religious and worldly benefits, such as multiplying food and drink in times of scarcity, bringing down rain when needed, and securing victory over enemies in times of danger.

Yet these people, with their deceptive satanic states, destroy blessings, intensify dangers, and consume people’s wealth wrongfully. They neither enjoin what is right nor forbid what is wrong, nor do they strive in Allah’s cause. Rather, they side with whoever gives to them, feeds them, and honours them—even if he is a Tatar. Indeed, they favour the Tatars over the Muslims and become their accursed helpers and supporters. Some of them seek to induce their state through forms of sorcery and associating partners with Allah, which Allah Most High and His Messenger have forbidden.

As for those among them who practise “trickery,” they prepare compounds using such substances as talq stone, frog fat, bitter-orange peel, and the like. They use these to walk on fire. They also handle a particular kind of snake, taking it as a morsel and wickedly venturing to eat it. Whatever they concoct from sugar, labdanum, rosewater, saffron water, and blood is all trickery and sleight of hand, recognizable to anyone versed in these matters. Some of them are visited by devils: these are the practitioners of satanic trickery.

Section

As for what they have mentioned concerning their excessive veneration of spiritual guides:

It must be understood that the righteous guides who are to be followed in religion are those who follow the path of the prophets and messengers, such as the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers, those who followed them in righteousness, and those whose good name is honoured within the Muslim community. Their way is to call people to Allah, to obey Him and His Messenger, and to follow His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The aim is that all religious devotion should be for Allah alone and that Allah’s word should be supreme.

For Allah Most High says:

“I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

“I seek no provision from them, nor do I wish them to feed Me.”

“Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of Strength, the Ever-Firm.”

The messengers commanded people to worship none but Allah and to devote their religion sincerely to Him, fearing none but Him, hoping in none but Him, and calling upon none but Him.

Allah Most High says:

“The mosques belong to Allah, so do not call upon anyone alongside Allah.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, fears Allah and is mindful of Him—it is they who will triumph.”

Thus He made obedience due to Allah and the Messenger, but reverent fear and mindfulness due to Allah alone.

Allah Most High says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. Indeed, to Allah we turn in hope.’”

Thus, giving is attributed to both Allah and the Messenger:

“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.”

What is lawful is what the Messenger of Allah has declared lawful; what is forbidden is what he has forbidden; and religion is what he has prescribed. No one, whether of earlier or later generations, may depart from obedience to him or from his law. Whoever does not acknowledge him inwardly and outwardly is a disbeliever who will abide in the Fire forever.

The best of the righteous spiritual guides and Allah’s pious friends are those who follow him most closely, are nearest to him, know his religion best, and are most obedient to his commands—such as Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī, and all those who followed them in righteousness.

As for sufficiency, it belongs to Allah alone. Hence they said:

“Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.”

They did not say, “and His Messenger.” As Allah Most High says:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ But this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you.”

That is, Allah alone is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you. He alone suffices them, for to Him, glorified is He, belong sovereignty and all praise, and He is sufficient for His servant. As Allah Most High says:

“Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?”

Allah Most High also says:

“When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I answer the supplication of the supplicant when he calls upon Me”—to the end of the verse.

It is reported that one of the Companions said, “O Messenger of Allah, is our Lord near, so that we may speak to Him quietly, or far away, so that we must call out to Him?” Allah Most High then revealed this verse.

He, glorified is He, is All-Hearing, Near, Responsive, and Merciful. He is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child. He knows of His servants’ circumstances what no one else knows; He can meet those needs of theirs that no one else can meet; and He shows them a mercy that no one else can show them.

The spiritual guides who are followed as examples point people towards Him and guide them to Him. They are like imams in prayer: they pray, and people pray behind them. They are also like a guide who leads pilgrims to the Sacred House: he directs them to it, while he and they all make pilgrimage to it. They have no share in divinity. Rather, anyone who assigns them any such share is like the Christian polytheists concerning whom Allah said:

“They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah, and also the Messiah, son of Mary, though they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him!”

Noah, peace be upon him, said:

“Say: I do not tell you that I possess Allah’s treasuries, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel.”

Allah likewise commanded Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to say this. Thus, no one may call upon a dead or absent spiritual guide. Indeed, no one may call upon any dead or absent person, whether a prophet or anyone else. One must not say to any of them, “O my master so-and-so, I am in your keeping,” or “under your protection.” Nor may one say, “I seek your help and your protection.” Nor, upon stumbling, may one say, “O so-and-so!” Nor may one say, “Muhammad and ‘Alī,” or “Lady Nafīsah,” or “my master Shaykh Ahmad,”

or “Shaykh ‘Adī,” or “Shaykh ‘Abd al-Qādir,” or any other such words or expressions involving calling upon a dead or absent person, asking them for things, seeking their aid in distress, or seeking their support. Rather, these are among the deeds of the polytheists and the acts of worship practised by the misguided.

It is well known that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the foremost of creation. It is established in Sahīh al-Bukhārī:

“When the people suffered drought, ‘Umar sought rain through al-‘Abbās, saying, ‘O Allah, whenever we suffered drought, we would seek to draw near to You through our Prophet, and You would grant us rain. Now we seek to draw near to You through our Prophet’s uncle, so grant us rain.’ And they would be granted rain.”

During the Prophet’s lifetime, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they would seek to draw near to Allah through his supplication and intercession for them. Likewise, on the Day of Resurrection, people will seek to draw near to Allah through him and ask him to intercede with their Lord. Allah will then permit him to intercede, and he will intercede for them. Do you not see that Allah says:

“Who is there who can intercede with Him except by His permission?”

Allah Most High also says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. They do not possess even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any supporter among them.’”

“Intercession before Him is of no avail except for one to whom He has given permission.”

He, glorified is He, thus makes clear that none of His creatures possesses any part of His dominion, that He has no partner in it, and that He has no supporter—that is, anyone who helps Allah Most High as kings help one another. He also makes clear that intercession before Him is of no avail except for one to whom He has given permission.

“On the Day of Resurrection, people will come to Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, asking them to intercede. Yet none of these, who are the foremost of creation, will intercede for them, until they come to Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Then he will come before his Lord, praise Him with words of praise, and prostrate before Him. Once He permits him to intercede, he will intercede for them.”

Such is the position of these, who are the best of creation; what, then, of others? After the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died, they did not call upon him, seek his aid in distress, or ask him for anything, whether at his grave or far from it. Indeed, they did not even pray at his grave or anyone else’s grave. Rather, they invoked blessings and peace upon him, obeyed his commands, followed his law, and fulfilled the duties that Allah Most High loves concerning His own rights, the rights of His Messenger, and the rights of His believing servants. For he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised Jesus son of Mary. I am only a servant, so say: ‘Allah’s servant and Messenger.’”

He also said:

“O Allah, do not let my grave become an idol that is worshipped.”

And he said:

“Do not make my grave a place of recurring observance. Invoke blessings upon me wherever you are, for your invocations of blessings reach me.”

And he said:

“May Allah curse the Jews and Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”

He was warning against what they had done.

A man said to him, “Whatever Allah wills and you will.” He replied, “Have you made me a rival to Allah? Say: ‘Whatever Allah alone wills.’”

He also said:

“Do not say, ‘Whatever Allah wills and Muhammad wills.’ Rather, say, ‘Whatever Allah wills, then Muhammad wills.’”

It is related in al-Musnad that Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal prostrated before him. He said, “What is this, Mu‘ādh?”

He replied, “O Messenger of Allah, I saw people in the Levant prostrating before their bishops, and they attribute this practice to their prophets.”

He said, “Mu‘ādh, if I were to command anyone to prostrate before another, I would command a woman to prostrate before her husband, because of the great right he has over her.”

translated_text:
Mu‘ādh, tell me: if you passed by my grave, would you prostrate before it?” He replied, “No.” He said, “Prostration is proper only for Allah”—or words to that effect.

If it is impermissible to prostrate before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whether alive or dead, or before his grave, how could it be permissible to prostrate before anyone else?

Indeed, it is authentically reported that he said:

“Do not sit on graves, and do not pray facing them.”

He thus prohibited praying towards graves, just as he prohibited taking them as places of worship. Accordingly, when they enlarged the mosque and incorporated his chamber into it, they gave its rear a ridged form, angled away from alignment with the qiblah, so that no one would pray towards the Prophet’s chamber. What, then, of prostrating towards anyone else, whoever he may be?

As for someone saying, “This prostration is for Allah Most High,” if he is lying, lying is disgrace enough. If he is telling the truth, he must be called upon to repent; if he repents, well and good, but otherwise he is to be put to death. For prostration may only be performed in a prescribed manner: prostration during prayer, prostration for forgetfulness, prostration upon recitation, and—according to one of the two scholarly views—prostration of gratitude.

As for prostrating immediately after prayer without a reason, the scholars have disapproved of it. Likewise, the practice of some shaykhs of performing two prostrations after witr was neither practised by any of the early generations nor recommended by any of the imams. Rather, these people had heard a hadith narrated by Abū Mūsā, the one found in al-Wazā’if: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to

“He used to pray two units of prayer after witr while seated, but did not do so regularly.”

Thus, the two units of prayer were called “two prostrations,” as in other hadiths. This, then, is the origin of that practice. These two units of prayer are discussed elsewhere.

As for the two prostrations, there is no basis for them, nor for prostration on its own without a reason. The scholars have called it an innovation. What, then, of prostrating towards a created being without observing the conditions of prayer? This resembles someone who prostrates eastwards in a church with the Christians and says, “It is for Allah,” or prostrates with the Jews towards the Rock and says, “It is for Allah.” Indeed, the Christians’ and Jews’ prostration to Allah, even though directed elsewhere than the Muslims’ qiblah, is better than prostration to anyone other than Allah.

Rather, this is like those who prostrate to the sun at sunrise and sunset, or to certain stars and idols, and say, “It is for Allah.”

Section

As for “vows to the dead”—whether prophets, shaykhs, or others—or to their graves or those residing at their graves, such vows constitute polytheism and disobedience to Allah Most High, whether what is vowed is financial support, gold, or anything else. This resembles making vows to churches, monks, and temples of idols.

It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Whoever vows to obey Allah must obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey Allah must not disobey Him.”

The scholars agree that a vow to commit disobedience must not be fulfilled. Rather, according to one of the two scholarly opinions, the person who made it must offer the expiation for an oath. This applies when the vow is made to Allah. If, however, the vow is made to someone other than Allah, it is like swearing by someone other than Allah, and this is polytheism. The person must therefore seek Allah’s forgiveness for it; such a vow must not be fulfilled, and no expiation is due. Whoever gives money in charity to the poor and devout will have his reward with the Lord of the worlds.

Moreover, making a vow in the first place is itself prohibited. It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade making vows and said:

“It brings no good; it merely extracts something from the miser.”

If a person does make a vow, he must fulfill whatever it entails of obedience to Allah, such as prayer, charity, fasting, and pilgrimage, but not what does not constitute obedience to Allah Most High.

Section

As for men establishing bonds of brotherhood with non-mahram women, being alone with them, and looking at their concealed adornment, this is forbidden by the consensus of the Muslims. Whoever makes this part of religion is a brother of the devils. Allah Most High says:

“When they commit a shameful deed, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command shameful deeds. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Let no man be alone with a woman, for Satan is the third of them.”

He also said:

“Beware of entering upon women.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, what about the husband’s male relative?” He replied, “The husband’s male relative is death.”

Whoever does not desist from this must receive a severe punishment that deters him and others like him who persist in corruption and defiance.

translated_text:
Section

As for swearing by anyone other than Allah—whether angels, prophets, shaykhs, kings, or others—it is prohibited and does not constitute a binding oath, by agreement of the imams. Their only disagreement concerned swearing specifically by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The majority hold that an oath sworn by him or by anyone else is not binding. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Whoever wishes to swear an oath, let him swear by Allah or remain silent.”

He also said:

“Whoever swears by anyone other than Allah has associated partners with Him.”

Thus, whoever swears by his shaykh, his shaykh’s tomb, his life, or his right over Allah; by kings, the sultan’s favor, the sword, or the Kaaba; by his father, his father’s tomb, or anything similar—such swearing is prohibited, and his oath is not binding, by agreement of the Muslims.

Section

As for someone saying to a person who reproves him, “You are a follower of the religious law,” this is a correct statement. If, however, he means by this that he does not follow the religious law, or is not obliged to follow it, and that “I am not bound to follow it,” then the term “religious law” has come to have three meanings in common usage: the revealed law, the interpreted law, and the altered law.

translated_text:
As for the revealed law, it is what is established from the Messenger in the Quran and Sunnah. All generations, earlier and later, must follow this law, and the best of Allah’s allies are those who follow it most completely. Whoever does not commit himself to this law, impugns it, or considers it permissible for anyone to depart from it is called upon to repent; if he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is put to death.

As for the interpreted law, it consists of rulings that scholars have reached through independent reasoning. It is permissible to follow one of the imams in such matters, but people are not obliged to adhere to the position of any particular imam.

As for the altered law, it consists of fabricated hadiths, distorted interpretations, misleading innovations introduced into the religious law that are not part of it, and judging by other than what Allah has revealed. It is not permissible for anyone to follow these or anything similar.

Judges rule only on the basis of outward evidence, while Allah Most High deals with what is hidden within. A judge’s ruling does not change the true nature of things. It is authentically reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“You bring your disputes before me, and some of you may be more eloquent in presenting their case than others. I judge only on the basis of what I hear. If I award anyone something belonging to his brother, he must not take it, for I am only allotting him a piece of the Fire.”

These are the words of the leader of judges and the master of Adam’s descendants.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, also said:

“When a judge exercises independent judgment and reaches the correct decision, he has two rewards; when he exercises independent judgment but errs, he has one reward.”

He also said:

“Judges are of three kinds: two are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who knows the truth and judges accordingly is in Paradise. A man who judges between people in ignorance is in the Fire. A man who knows the truth but judges contrary to it is in the Fire.”

Whoever departs from the revealed law with which Allah sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, imagining that he is following “reality,” resembles the polytheists who reject the messengers. The term “reality” may refer to “the reality of creation,” “reality based on religious innovation,” or “reality grounded in revealed law.”

“The reality of creation” consists in believing in divine decree and predestination, and that Allah is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all things. This must be believed, but it may not be invoked as a justification. Rather, Allah has the conclusive argument against us. Whoever invokes predestination as an argument has an invalid argument, and whoever invokes predestination to excuse his sins has an unacceptable excuse.

As for “reality based on religious innovation,” it consists in pursuing the path to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, on the basis of the spiritual taste, ecstasy, love, and desire that arise in a person’s heart, without following the Book and Sunnah. This is like the way of the Christians: sometimes they worship other than Allah, and sometimes they worship without Allah’s command—like the Christians who associated partners with Allah and took their scholars

As for the religion of the Muslims, it is as Allah Most High says:

“So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”

He Most High also says:

“To test you as to which of you is best in deeds.”

Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād said: “The most sincere and the most correct.” They asked: “What is meant by the most sincere and the most correct?”

He said: “If a deed is sincere but not correct, it will not be accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it will not be accepted. It must be both sincere and correct. Sincerity means that it is done for Allah, and correctness means that it accords with the Sunnah.”

For this reason, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb used to say in his supplication:

“O Allah, make all my deeds righteous, make them purely for Your sake, and let no one else have any share in them.”

As for “reality grounded in revealed law,” it consists in putting into practice what Allah and His Messenger have prescribed, such as sincerity towards Allah, reliance upon Allah, fear of Allah, gratitude to Allah, patience with Allah’s judgment, love for Allah and His Messenger, hatred for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, and other things that Allah and His Messenger love. These are the realities of the people of faith and the path of those endowed with spiritual knowledge.

Enjoining what is right—the truth with which Allah sent His Messenger—and forbidding what is wrong—all forms of religious innovation and wickedness that oppose that truth—are indeed among the greatest obligations and finest acts of obedience. Indeed, this is the path of the religious leaders and spiritual masters whose example we follow in this regard.

Allah Most High says:

“Let there be among you a group who call to goodness, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. It is they who will be successful.”

This is the verse cited as evidence that spiritual masters are to be followed in matters of religion. Whoever does not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is neither a spiritual master nor someone whose example should be followed.

later spiritual masters approved of it and regarded it as commendable. Some have cited as evidence the report that “the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, clothed Umm Khālid bint Khālid ibn Sa‘īd ibn al-‘Ās in a garment and said to her, ‘Sinnā!’” Sinnā means “beautiful” in the language of Abyssinia. She had been born in Abyssinia, which is why he addressed her in that language. They also cited the hadith concerning “the cloak that a woman wove for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. One of the Companions asked him for it, and he gave it to him. The Companion said, ‘I wanted it to be my shroud.’”

Neither of these two hadiths provides evidence for the manner in which they practise this. Giving someone clothing to wear is like giving him anything else that benefits him. Taking a garment from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to seek its blessing is like taking some of his hair to seek its blessing. This is not the same as wearing a garment or cap as an expression of following someone and taking him as an example. Rather, in some respects, the practice resembles the robes of honour that kings bestow upon those whom they appoint to office, serving as insignia and marks of authority and distinction. Hence they describe this as an honour. At most, this and similar practices may be classed as permissible acts. If accompanied by a righteous intention, they become commendable on that account. But to regard this as a sunnah and a path to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not justified.

As for a group’s affiliation with a particular spiritual master, there is no doubt that people need someone from whom to learn faith and the Quran, just as the Companions learned them from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Successors learned them from the Companions. It is through this that one follows the forerunners

who came first, faithfully following their example. Just as a person has someone to teach him the Quran and similar subjects, so too he has someone to teach him the inward and outward aspects of religion. This need not be confined to any particular person, nor does it require affiliation with a particular spiritual master. Anyone who imparts religious benefit to another is his teacher in that respect. Likewise, any deceased person whose sayings, deeds, or legacy reach someone and benefit him in his religion is his teacher in that respect. Thus, the earlier generations of this community are the teachers of those who succeed them, generation after generation. No one may affiliate himself with a spiritual master and make following him the basis of loyalty and enmity.

Rather, he must show loyalty to all people of faith and all who are known for piety, whether spiritual masters or others. He must not single anyone out for greater loyalty unless that person’s greater faith and piety become apparent to him. He should therefore give precedence to those whom Allah Most High and His Messenger have given precedence, and favour those whom Allah and His Messenger have favoured. Allah Most High says:

“O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.”

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“No Arab has any superiority over a non-Arab, nor any non-Arab over an Arab; no black person has any superiority over a white person, nor any white person over a black person, except through piety.”

translated_text:
Section

As for someone saying, “You belong to such-and-such a spiritual master, and he is your master in this world and the Hereafter,” this is a reprehensible innovation, both because he has devoted himself to someone other than Allah and because the statement “your master in this world and the Hereafter” has no basis in reality.

If he means that they will be together in Paradise, that is for Allah to decide, not him. If he means that the master’s intercession on his behalf will be accepted, no one intercedes for another except by Allah Most High’s permission. If He permits his intercession on that person’s behalf, it will be accepted; otherwise, it will not. Merely saying, “You are my spiritual master in the Hereafter,” does not make him an intercessor for the speaker—and this is assuming that the master is among those entitled to intercede. It has already been explained that the foremost of the messengers and of all creation will not intercede until Allah permits him to do so, after others have declined. How many claim to be spiritual masters, yet have deficiencies in knowledge and faith known only to Allah Most High!

As for the saying:

“If any of you expected good from a stone, Allah would benefit him through it,”

this is a saying of polytheists and fabricators of lies. Idol-worshippers expected good from their idols, yet both they and their idols became fuel for Hell, as Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, you and what

you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will enter it.”

But the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself. If he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs. If he draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm’s length. If he draws near to Me by an arm’s length, I draw near to him by an armspan. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.’”

Whoever can find guidance without affiliating himself with a particular spiritual master has no need to do so. Such affiliation is not recommended for him; rather, it is discouraged. But if he cannot worship Allah as He has commanded except through such affiliation—for example, if he lives somewhere where guidance, knowledge, faith, and religious practice are weak, and those who would teach and discipline him will do so only if he affiliates himself with their master—or if affiliation with a master would increase his religious commitment and knowledge, then he should do whatever is best for his religion. Such a situation generally arises only through his own negligence; otherwise, if he sought guidance in the proper way, he would find it.

As for affiliation that divides Muslims, abandoning communal unity and concord for division, following the path of innovation, and departing from the Sunnah and adherence to it, this is prohibited. Whoever does so incurs sin and thereby departs from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.

As for the statement, “Allah is pleased when the spiritual masters are pleased and angry when they are angry,” this does not apply to all spiritual masters, nor is it exclusive to them. Rather, whoever is in accord with Allah—pleased with what pleases Allah and angered by what angers Allah—Allah is pleased when he is pleased and angry when he is angry, whether he is a spiritual master or someone else. Any spiritual master who is not like this does not possess this quality.

An example is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Abū Bakr al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, following an exchange between him and Suhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and others concerning Abū Sufyān ibn Harb. Abū Sufyān had passed by them, and they said:

“The swords have not taken their full toll on Allah’s enemy.”

Abū Bakr said, “Do you say this about the chief of Quraysh?” He then went to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and told him what had happened. The Prophet said:

“Perhaps you have angered them, Abū Bakr. If you have angered them, you have indeed angered your Lord”—or words to that effect.

The narrator said: Abū Bakr then went out to them and asked, “My brothers, have I angered you?”

They replied, “No; may Allah forgive you, Abū Bakr.”

Their anger was for Allah’s sake.

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is reported to have said:

“He says

—Allah Most High—‘Whoever shows enmity to a close servant of Mine has challenged Me to war. Nothing by which My servant draws near to Me compares to what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he grasps, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate over anything I do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must face it.’”

Allah loves this believer who draws near to Him through voluntary acts after fulfilling the obligatory duties, because he has done what Allah loves; the recompense corresponds to the deed.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.”

In truth, the servant at whose pleasure Allah is pleased, and at whose anger He is angry, is himself pleased with what pleases Allah and angered by what angers Him. Let these two serve as examples of someone who loves what Allah loves, hates what Allah hates, is pleased with what Allah is pleased with because it pleases Allah, and is angered by what angers Him. Yet no human being can maintain this continually. Even the most perfect of creation must sometimes feel ordinary human anger and pleasure. Hence the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in an authentic hadith:

“O Allah, I am only human and become angry as humans do. So any Muslim whom I have insulted or cursed, though he did not deserve it—make that a blessing and a purification for him, and a means of drawing him near to You on the Day of Resurrection.”
